payload.answer:
## 1) Инспекция входных данных (фактические замеры)

**system_info.json**: n_genes=25, n_timepoints=50, n_series=5, sampling_interval=0.612245. Совпадает с фактическими файлами.

**expression_timeseries.npy**: shape (5, 50, 25), dtype float64, NaN=0, Inf=0.
- Диапазон: 0.041 … 17.55; mean 6.71, std 4.84. Уровни по генам сильно гетерогенны: от 0.46 (gene9) и 0.76 (gene20) до 15.2–16.6 (gene4, gene8, gene18) — разброс ~35×.
- Шум (оценка по 2-м разностям, σ = std(Δ²X)/√6): 0.048–0.16, медиана **0.063**; в относительном выражении 0.4%–12% (крупные гены шумят в абсолюте сильнее: gene8 0.159, gene18 0.149, но σ/level у них <1.1%) → шум близок к **аддитивному**.
- Отношение std(ΔX)/std(X) = 0.17–0.76 ≪ 1.41 → ряды сильно автокоррелированы; lag-1 автокорреляция в среднем 0.63 (для крупных генов 0.996–1.000). Это релаксационный переходный процесс, а не стационарный шум.
- **Что это за динамика**: 5 серий стартуют с независимых малых начальных условий (t=0: 0.04–1.9, примерно U[0,2]) и монотонно релаксируют к одному и тому же устойчивому состоянию, которое совпадает с baseline (row0) с точностью ≤0.15. Т.е. это «startup-переходный процесс», 5 серий — replicate-реализации одного и того же перехода (средние по сериям различаются <0.1).
- **Критично для метода**: матрица отклонений Z = X − X_ss (250×25) имеет спектр 130.5, 24.6, 4.6, 4.1, 3.4, 3.3, 3.0, 2.2, … при шумовом полу ~1.4; PC1+PC2 = **99.5%** дисперсии. То есть траектория реально возбуждает ~2–3 моды, effective rank ≈ 3–5 из 25. Отношение сигнала производной к шуму производной приемлемо (|dX/dt| ~0.1–0.5 против ~0.09), но **идентифицируемость A крайне плохая** — collinearity/ранг, а не шум, является ограничением.
- Предварительный diagnostic-ridge dX/dt = A(X−X_ss) (held-out by series, λ=10): средний held-out R² = 0.80, но с strong per-gene skew и отрицательными значениями для отдельных генов → прогноз траектории хороший, интерпретация отдельных элементов A — нет.

**perturbation_steady_states.npy**: shape (16, 25), float64, NaN=0, Inf=0. Диапазон 0.0 … 17.46; mean 6.46, std 4.73.
- **Сдвиг строк относительно row0**: L2-нормы Δ = [–, 8.57, **0.21**, 10.57, 11.26, 21.81, 11.37, 29.67, 18.45, 13.26, 9.24, 22.94, 10.58, 10.87, 11.44, 17.55]. **Строка 2 статистически неотличима от baseline** (max|Δ| = 0.099; std(Δ)=0.039 → σ≈0.027 — это по сути replicate baseline). Итого **14 из 15 строк заметно сдвинуты, 1 строка — «пустая»/повтор baseline**.
- Число генов с |Δ|>0.3 на строку: [–, 7, **0**, 4, 6, 10, 6, 12, 7, 9, 4, 11, 4, 4, 4, 11] → всего **99 «ответов»** на 15 строк; при пороге 0.15 — 106, при 1.0 — 76. Порог в широком диапазоне (0.1–1.0) меняет исход мало → отклики бимодальны (либо сильный отклик, либо шум), что хорошо для надёжного детектирования.
- Эффективный ранг матрицы steady-state = **14** (SV: 31.5…2.17, затем 0.098 и 0.0 при шумовом полу ~1.4). Одна из линейных зависимостей — именно row0/row2.
- **Тип вмешательств хорошо читается (clamp-сигнатура)**: KO — значения ≈0 (0.000–0.019) при baseline >0.2; OE — значения, «прижатые» к 10.0 (9.979…10.016). Обнаружено 42 clamp-детекта, по 2–4 мишени на строку:
  row3 OE={12,14,15,18}; row4 OE={1,2,6,17}; row5 KO={5,11,14,23}; row7 KO={6,8,11,18}; row8 KO={8,9,21}; row9 KO={0,10}; row10 OE={8,10,12,24}; row11 KO={16,18,19}; row12 OE={9,14,17}; row13 OE={0,3,13,14}; row14 OE={0,4,16,18}; row15 KO={10,12,16}.
  **Строки 1, 2, 6 не имеют clamp-сигнатуры** (row1 и row6 содержат сильные сдвиги до 5.7 и 7.9) → это либо вмешательства без жёсткого clamp (например, ингибитор/скрытый узел), либо мишень не измеряется; наивная схема «мишень → отклик» для них не замкнётся, их нужно обрабатывать как «unknown-source» условия.
- gene20 почти инвариантен везде (std по всем 16 условиям 0.081, в TC 0.108) → кандидат на «изолированный»/независимый ген (нулевая строка и столбец), gene9 и gene1 имеют низкий baseline, но реагируют (gene9: OE в row12 до 9.98; gene1: OE в row4 до 9.99).

По вашей косвенной оценке числа реально задокументированных вмешательств: **14 эффективных условий** (row2 — реплика baseline), из них **12 с идентифицируемыми clamp-мишенями** и **2 (row1, row6) без идентифицируемой мишени**.

## 2) Предлагаемый подход: два независимых метода + слияние

**Метод A — динамический (time-series, как вы предложили), но в устойчивой форме.**
A1. Оценка X_ss из данных (среднее последних точек), центрирование: Z = X − X_ss; σ по 2-м разностям → взвешивание (weighted LS) или per-gene standardization.
A2. Оценка производной: (i) центральные разности; (ii) сглаживание Savitzky–Golay/winner и разности; (iii) «exact-integration» вариант — переход X_{t+1} = M X_t + (M−I)… (discrete-time AR(1), затем A = (M−I)/Δt) как альтернатива, менее чувствительная к шуму.
A3. Регрессия для каждого целевого гена i: Ẋ_i = Σ_j A[i,j] Z_j, **elastic net (координатный спуск, собственная реализация)** + ridge для смещённой, но устойчивой оценки; сетка λ, CV **по сериям (leave-one-series-out)** — это ваш «скользящий контроль по 5 рядам».
A4. Стабильность: bootstrap по временным окнам и по сериям → частота отбора и согласованность знака. Знак A[i,j] = знак влияния j→i.
Ограничение (обязательно укажу в method_comparison): design rank ≈ 3, поэтому A даёт «soft evidence», а не самостоятельную топологию.

**Метод B — статический по steady-state (как вы предложили), но с разделением «мишень/отклик» и деконволюцией непрямых путей.**
B1. Обнаружение мишеней (clamp: 0 или 10) и откликов (|Δ| > thr_resp, thr_resp из шумовой оценки: max(0.15, 4σ_i·replicate)).
B2. Двухрежимная кодировка дизайна: для условия r, мишень j — код c_j^KO (−1) / c_j^OE (+1); для row1, row6 — код «unknown perturbation» (только как наблюдение, не как источник ребра).
B3. Для каждого гена-мишени отклика i: LASSO/elastic net Δ_i(r) = Σ_j B[i,j] c_j(r) (наблюдений 13–14, предикторов ≤ 25 → обязательна разреженность + верхний предел числа отобранных предикторов), плюс знак-тест по согласованию KO/OE-пар для одного и того же гена j (OE↑j даёт Δ_i, KO↓j даёт −Δ_i → знак должен быть антикоррелирован).
B4. Прямые vs непрямые: (i) проверка «если j→i косвенно через m, то в условиях, где m clamp-нут, отклик i на j исчезает/ослабевает» (условный/медиационный тест); (ii) альтернативно — оценка полной матрицы усиления G из B3 и возврат к разреженной прямой матрице через A ≈ G(I+G)^{-1} (разреженная деконволюция). Оба варианта дадут сравнение.
B5. Стабильность: leave-one-condition-out (15×) + bootstrap по строкам, требование частоты отбора и согласованности знака.

**Слияние (консенсус)**: edge score = комбинация нормированных |коэффициентов| и согласованности знаков между A и B (sign-agreement как фильтр). Приоритет топологии — за B (данные с много большим SNR), A — как поддержка/вето знака. Для edges, где знаки методов конфликтуют, или знак неустойчив в CV — **ставим знак 0** (не угадываем), вес при этом сохраняем только если магнитудный консенсус высокий (альтернативу фиксирую ниже как решение, которое можно менять).

## 3) Фиксируемые допущения и правила (прошу подтвердить/поправить)

1. **Конвенция**: inferred_network[i,j] = сила влияния j → i (row=target, column=source); in-degree = сумма строки, out-degree = сумма столбца; **диагональ = ровно 0.0** во всех трёх файлах.
2. **«Самый влиятельный регулятор»**: основной критерий — **взвешенный out-strength** = Σ_i |W[i,j]| (сумма по столбцу, без диагонали), потому что магнитуда устойчивее к порогу. Дополнительно сообщу unweighted out-degree и их ранги в network_metrics.json / method_comparison.json; при расхождении топ-2 — беру взвешенный вариант и фиксирую это в hub_genes.json (2 гена).
3. **Плотность 5–40% (31–248 ненулей из 600)**: не «порог по магнитуде вслепую», а **глобальный top-K по |edge score| с K, выбранным из кривой стабильности** (стабильный «elbow»: минимальный K, при котором доля рёбер, воспроизведённых в ≥60% LOO/bootstrap-повторов, перестаёт расти), затем **жёсткое ограничение K в [40, 200]** (безопасная середина 5–40%). Один и тот же булев mask применяется последовательно к inferred_network.npy, edge_sign_predictions.npy и network_metrics.json (метрики считаются ровно по этому mask, без дополнительных порогов).
4. **Знак «неопределённо» = 0**: если edge в mask, но знаки методов конфликтуют или знак не согласован в ≥70% стабильностных повторов → sign 0 при ненулевом весе (вход в requirement'ы это допускает: 0 = «no relationship or uncertain sign»). Альтернатива (если вам так чище): исключать такой edge из mask полностью, тогда плотность чуть ниже. По умолчанию оставляю вариант «вес есть, знак 0» и посчитаю в диагностике число таких рёбер.
5. **Шум/пороги отклика**: thr_resp = max(0.15, 4·σ_i), σ_i из 2-х разностей TC (0.048–0.16); clamp-детекция: |v| < 0.05 при baseline > 0.2 (KO), |v − 10| < 0.06 (OE).
6. **row2** трактуется как техническая реплика baseline (исключается из «источников» вмешательств, но полезна как оценка шума); row1, row6 — «unknown-source» условия: используются для проверки предсказательной способности, но не для приписывания рёбер.
7. **Ограничение окружения**: в actually установленном окружении **нет scikit-learn и matplotlib** (есть numpy 2.4.4, scipy 1.16.0, pandas, statsmodels). Поэтому LASSO/elastic net делаю собственной реализацией координатного спуска на numpy (или scipy.optimize) — это снижает переносимость, но гарантирует запуск. (Можно попробовать pip install, но сеть/индекс могут быть недоступны.)
8. Анализ будет в одном self-contained **analysis.py**, детерминированном (фиксированный seed), с сохранением всех порогов/стабильностных метрик в JSON.

## 4) Статистическая состоятельность (15 наблюдений на 25 генов)

- Двойное узкое место: (i) steady-state — 13–14 «полезных» наблюдений на 25 предикторов; (ii) time-series — 250 строк, но **effective rank ≈ 3–5**. Честная позиция: полное 625-параметрическое восстановление недостижимо; задача решается как **оценка разрежной топологии + знаков**, а не точных весов.
- Меры против переобучения: L1-регуляризация с **жёстким верхним пределом числа предикторов на ген** (≤3–4, ≈ n_obs/4); CV с группировкой по «экспериментам» (leave-one-condition-out для B, leave-one-series-out для A) — т.е. проверка на удержанных экспериментах, а не на удержанных точках; stability selection (bootstrap+LOO, требование частоты и знака); ограничение общего числа рёбер сверху; слияние только по согласованным знакам (межметодная кросс-валидация по сути).
- Внутренние метрики вместо ground truth: held-out R² предсказания откликов steady-state (LOO по строкам), held-out one-step R² по удержанной серии для ODE, частота воспроизведения ребра, доля согласованных знаков, «degree/weight stability» при варьировании K.

## Критерий успеха (предлагаю зафиксировать)

- **density**: off-diagonal nonzero доля ∈ [0.05, 0.40] (31–248 ненулей), диагональ = 0, NaN/Inf = 0, одинаковый mask во всех трёх файлах, sign[i,j]≠0 ⇒ W[i,j]≠0 и наоборот (кроме явно «uncertain-sign» рёбер, которые перечислю).
- **sign**: доля рёбер с определённым знаком ≥ 60% от всех рёбер в mask; согласованность знаков между методами A/B на общих рёбрах ≥ 70% (иначе слияние пересматриваем); знак каждой «clamp-мишени → мишень отклика» пары должен воспроизводиться в KO/OE-паре при наличии обоих типов.
- **hub**: топ-2 по out-strength должны быть (i) устойчивы при варьировании K в [40,200] и порога отклика 0.15–1.0 (в топ-2 в ≥70% конфигураций), (ii) совпадать хотя бы на 1 ген между независимыми методами, (iii) обоснованы данными (большое число условий, где их clamp даёт сильные отклики других генов).
- **Дополнительно**: LOO held-out R² предсказания steady-state откликов > 0.5 (по отобранным рёбрам), held-out one-step R² по временным рядам ≥ 0.7.

## Главные неопределённости

1. Effective rank TC ≈ 3 → динамический метод не сможет независимо задать топологию; он будет вторичным. Готовы ли вы принять, что итоговая топология в основном идёт из steady-state (а метод A служит знаком/ветирующим фильтром)?
2. row1 и row6 не имеют clamp-мишени — если там вмешательство в неизмеряемый/скрытый узел, часть рёбер принципиально не припишется; оставляем их только как валидационные.
3. Clamp «OE = 10.0» — эмпирическое наблюдение (значения 9.979–10.016), но механика заявлена как недокументированная; если clamp-интерпретация неверна, B-дизайн нужно будет строить из чистых Δ (без кодов мишеней) — это ослабит знаковую идентификацию.
4. Непрямые пути: 12clamp-строк дают ~141 наивную пару «мишень→отклик», из них часть — непрямые; финальная плотность будет скорее ближе к нижней части диапазона (≈60–120 рёбер), что внутри 5–40%.
5. В окружении отсутствуют scikit-learn и matplotlib — реализация регуляризации будет собственной.

Реализацию (analysis.py и 5 выходных файлов) запускаю после вашего подтверждения; артефакты инспекции: `diagnostics_data_inspection.py` (выполнен) и `diagnostics_report.json`.

payload.answer:
## 1) Inspection findings (read-only; no modelling beyond throwaway diagnostics)

**`data/system_info.json` (verbatim fields):** `n_genes: 25`, `n_timepoints: 50`, `n_series: 5`, `sampling_interval: 0.612245`, a `data_description` saying the time course is *wild-type* multi-experiment data and that steady-state row 0 is baseline while rows 1–15 are undocumented molecular interventions, plus `noise_description: "All measurements contain experimental noise."` No units, no gene names, no intervention metadata.

**Arrays.** Both `float64`, C-contiguous, **0 NaN / 0 Inf / 0 masked values** in either file. `expression_timeseries.npy` (5,50,25): global min 0.041, max 17.55, mean 6.71, sd 4.84 → non-negative concentration-like units, not standardized. `perturbation_steady_states.npy` (16,25): min 0.0, max 17.46, mean 6.46, sd 4.73 — same scale/units.

**Time-course structure (this is the most consequential finding).** All 5 replicates start at t=0 from *random low initial conditions* (all values in 0.04–1.9, different per replicate), then relax to a **common** steady state. Trajectories are time-aligned (same t grid, same dt) and on identical offsets: per-replicate mean/sd = 6.71/4.84 for all five; cross-replicate sd at t≥30 is 0.048 per gene (i.e. pure noise, no replicate offsets) and `P[0]` matches the replicate-mean endpoint to **max abs diff 0.057** — strong evidence that gene ordering *and* units are consistent between the two files.

**Noise.** Additive, white, essentially homoscedastic: Savitzky–Golay residual sd = 0.055 overall, 0.040–0.10 per gene, independent of level (independent cross-replicate estimate 0.048). Relative noise therefore ranges 0.3 % (g04, g11, g18 at level 12–17) to 5–10 % for the three low-expression genes **g01 (0.87), g09 (0.46), g20 (0.76)**. Per-gene mean/std/range table is computed in the script; CV per gene 0.10–0.40.

**Smoothness / step size.** Signal lag-1 autocorrelation = 0.935 on average (0.999 for high genes, 0.57–0.72 for g01/g09/g20 — noise-limited, not biology). Relative state change per step ‖Δx‖/‖x‖·dt is **3.35 at t=0, 0.84 at t=1, 0.38 at t=2, <0.02 after t≈15**. So (i) the informative transient is only ~10–15 samples × 5 reps; (ii) plain explicit-Euler finite differences are badly biased in the first steps; (iii) after t≈15 the data contain noise only. Trajectory shapes are smooth → smoothing-spline or SavGol(w=9–11, poly 2–3) differentiation is appropriate (SavGol residuals ≈ noise level, so w=9 poly=2 is not oversmoothing; use spline-based derivatives rather than raw differences, and check an exponential-integrator/VAR(1) variant to absorb the dt·λ bias).

**Identifiability warning (quantified).** Pooled transient (all reps, all t) has PC1 = 96.1 % and PC2 = 3.3 % of variance → **two effective dimensions**; 99 % needs only 2 PCs. Mean |pairwise correlation| = 0.82, 62 % of pairs >0.9, 18 % >0.98. Between-replicate dispersion falls from 10× noise at t=0 to 1× noise by t≈14. Helper genes do overshoot (16/25 genes change sign of deviation), and 90 % rise times span 2–13 steps, which is what little directional diversity exists. Consequence: single-replicate derivative regressions are unstable (mean |sign agreement| across replicates = 0.51) and *must* be pooled; expect method A to have limited precision.

**Steady-state matrix.** Distance from baseline: row 2 is **silent** (L2 = 0.21 ≈ √25·0.045 = noise); the other 14 rows are strongly perturbed (L2 8.6–29.7, 4–11 genes with |Δ|>0.5). There is hard evidence of **value clamping**: 23 entries sit at 9.960–10.021 (mean 9.988, sd 0.015) and 19 entries at ≤0.031 (8 exactly 0.0). So:
- *set-to-10* rows 3, 4, 10, 12, 13, 14 (3–4 genes each: e.g. row 3 = {12,14,15,18}, row 13 = {0,3,13,14});
- *set-to-0* (knockout-like) rows 5, 7, 8, 9, 11, 15 (2–4 genes each: row 8 = {8,21}, row 11 = {16,18,19});
- rows 1 and 6 have **no** clamped entry (graded/partial perturbation; largest relative deviation g00 −76 % in row 1, g16 −67 % in row 6);
- every gene except g07, g20, g22 is a detected target at least once (counts 1–4).
Asymmetry worth noting: clamping a gene *up* to 10 rarely moves other genes (rows 3, 13, 14 are clamp-only), whereas clamping *to 0* produces large downstream responses — consistent with saturating Hill-type inputs above ~10. Hence the knockout rows carry nearly all usable directional information. Reproducible signatures confirm the design is informative, e.g. g8 clamped-to-0 in rows 7 and 8 gives g23 = 7.214/7.201 and g18 = 0.019/12.30; g19 clamped-to-0 (row 11) drops g24 from 8.81 to 2.37. So yes — **the perturbation rows are usable as soft prior knowledge on source nodes**, with the caveat that targets of rows 1/6 are inferred, not documented.

## 2) Proposed pipeline (four deliverables)

**Method A — time-course dynamics.** Per replicate×gene, cubic smoothing spline with `s = T·σ̂²` (σ̂ = 0.05) → x̂ and dx̂/dt (SavGol w=9 poly=2 as robustness variant). Fit, pooling the 5 replicates, `dx̂_i/dt = Σ_j A_ij (x̂_j − x̄_j) + b_i`, genes scaled by dynamic range; λ by **leave-one-replicate-out** CV on held-out derivative MSE. Add a sparse variant (A2): Lasso (own FISTA — sklearn is *not* installed) over a saturating basis per source, {x_j, Hill(x_j; θ_j, n=2)} with θ_j = gene median, to respect the known nonlinearity; plus a discrete-time exponential-integrator check `x_{t+1} = M x_t + c`, `A = logm(M)/dt` used only to confirm sign stability at this step size. Score_A = |Â_ij|, sign = sign(Â_ij).

**Method B — perturbation steady states (steady-state Jacobian by response constraints).** (i) Auto-detect clamp targets (|x−0|<0.06 with baseline >0.5, or |x−10|<0.2 with |Δ|>0.5); for rows 1/6 flag the single largest |Δ| gene as a *presumed* hidden target; drop silent row 2. (ii) Impose normalization A_ii = −1 and use the exact linear-response constraint "for equation i, in every row where i is not a target, Σ_j A_ij Δx_j = 0", i.e. regress Δx_i on {Δx_j, j≠i} across the eligible 10–14 rows, columns scaled by gene response magnitude, with **Lasso (and an LAD-Lasso robust variant** that tolerates a mis-assigned hidden target); λ per row by leave-one-perturbation-row-out prediction error. (iii) Auxiliary *total-effect* matrix T from regressing Δx_i on the sparse clamp design D (columns nearly orthogonal because interventions are sparse) — used for sign arbitration and as a plausibility filter, not for edge selection (T is dense by construction).

**Combination → final confidence matrix.** Per *target* gene i, rank-normalize each method's |coefficient| over its 24 candidate sources to s_A, s_B ∈ [0,1] (per-target normalization stops one gene/method from monopolizing the edge list). S = ½(s_A+s_B) + 0.15·agreement(s_A,s_B both in top-24 %, same sign). Select global top-K by S with K from an elbow of the sorted-S curve, constrained to the [5 %, 40 %] band; if no elbow is defensible, default K = 90 (15 % density, lower half of band to protect precision). Then `W[i,j] = S·(mean standardized |coefficient|)` for selected entries, **exactly 0.0 elsewhere, diagonal forced to 0.0** — the *same* topology is reused for signs and metrics.

**Signs.** agreement → that sign; single-method support → that method's sign unless its normalized coefficient is in the bottom decile (→ 0); conflict → sign of the method with ≥2× larger within-target normalized magnitude, else 0. Counts of each case will be reported in `method_comparison.json`.

**Hubs.** Primary: **weighted out-degree = Σ_i |W[i,j]| on the submitted nonzero topology** ([target, source] ⇒ column sum), because "most influential regulator" = capacity to drive other genes; cross-checked against raw out-degree, PageRank (damping 0.85, own power iteration — networkx absent) and out-closeness/weak-reachability; top 2 reported, plus a note on whether the ranking is metric-robust.

**Metrics** (computed on the exact submitted nonzero pattern, no post-hoc threshold): n_edges, density (=n_edges/600), in/out-degree mean·var·max, weighted in/out-degree mean·max, reciprocity, weakly-connected and strongly-connected component counts, largest SCC, and BFS diameter of the underlying undirected graph (reported as `null` with `largest_component_size` if disconnected).

**QC without ground truth (reported in `method_comparison.json`).** A: leave-one-replicate-out mean R² (pooled fit mean LOO R² = 0.58 currently, 0.87 excluding the two noise-dominated genes g01/g20 → I will report both). B: leave-one-perturbation-row-out R². Both: bootstrap stability of edge selection (resample replicates for A, rows for B; keep only edges with selection frequency above a pre-declared 0.6) and cross-method sign-agreement rate; plus a permutation null (shuffle clamp-target assignments across rows) to show scores exceed chance. A `proxy_score` combining held-out R² and stability will be reported per method.

**`analysis.py` layout** (single script, numpy/scipy only): `load_and_check()` → `characterize()` → `smooth_and_differentiate()` → `fit_method_A()` (+ `fit_method_A2`) → `detect_targets()`/`fit_method_B()` (+ `total_effects()`) → `combine_and_threshold()` → `assign_signs()` → `rank_hubs()` → `network_metrics()` → `validate()` → `write_artifacts()`. It writes exactly the six required artifacts: `inferred_network.npy` and `edge_sign_predictions.npy` as `(25,25)` **float64** (no NaN/Inf, zero diagonal, density in band — asserted in code), `hub_genes.json` = `{"hub_genes":[i,j]}`, `method_comparison.json` with a top-level `methods` list where each entry has `description`, a proxy metric (`mean_r2`/`stability`/`score`) and `strengths`/`limitations`/`rationale`, and `network_metrics.json` with the keys above.

## 3) Assumptions and risks

- **Assumption (well supported):** gene order/units identical across files (endpoint match 0.057 ≈ noise).
- **Assumption (weak):** the ~0/~10 entries are intervention targets; rows 1 and 6 need a heuristic hidden-target assignment. Mitigation: LAD-Lasso robustness, λ by row-out CV, and a sensitivity run excluding rows 1/2/6.
- **Risk (high, quantified):** direction identifiability from the time course — 2 effective PCs, transient ≈10 steps, between-replicate diversity buried in noise by t≈14 → method A precision will be modest; explicit Euler is biased at dt=0.612 (mitigated by spline derivatives + VAR(1)/expm check).
- **Risk (medium):** 62 % of gene pairs correlate >0.9 → thresholding is partly arbitrary; mitigated by sparsity regularization, per-target rank normalization, stability filter and pre-declared K (never tuned against unavailable ground truth).
- **Risk (medium):** saturating responses make *up*-clamps nearly uninformative → B relies on knockouts; signs of the ~0 clamps are assumed to be loss-of-function (sign/mechanism undocumented).
- **Environment:** numpy 2.4.4, scipy 1.16.0, pandas present; **sklearn, matplotlib, networkx are NOT installed** → Lasso (FISTA), PageRank and all graph metrics will be implemented in-script (no extra dependencies, fully reproducible).

## Decision points I'd like your input on
1. **Final density**: elbow-driven within the band, or fixed 15 % (my default), or mid-band 20 % as you suggested?
2. **Combination weights**: equal (default) vs down-weighting A (e.g. 0.4 A / 0.6 B) given A's weaker held-out validation?
3. **Rows 1/6**: keep with heuristic hidden target (default, plus sensitivity run) or drop them?
4. **Conflicting signs**: 2×-dominance rule then 0 (default) vs always defer to method B?
5. **Low-expression genes g01/g09/g20**: allow their edges from method B only (default) or suppress as uncertain?

No network has been produced yet; awaiting your approval of the plan.

## 2. Self-consistency requirement (hidden evaluator) कैसे पूरी होगी

योजन स्वीकार — आपका spec-extraction, role-resolution by structure, एकल-मॉडल self-consistency पाथ, तथा deterministic stage-analytics का दृष्टिकोण ठीक है। मुख्य कार्य अब अधिकृत; कृपया एक ही `analysis.py` से सभी 19 declared artifacts उत्पादित करें, कोई undeclared deliverable नहीं (`scratch/` का probe script अंतिम artifact-संग्रह में न जाए)।

कार्यान्वयन से पहले, मेरी ये पद्धतिगत सिफ़ारिशें हैं (सुझाव, क़रार नहीं — जहाँ spec मौन है, वहाँ आपका चयन assumption के रूप में `conservation_report.json` में अंकित रहे):

1. TV/आधारित probe स्तंभों का convention: चूँकि `lag_time` की पहचान killed-chain के stationary catalytic flux से 1e-9 तक मिलती है, उसी killed chain को आधार बनाएँ — conditioned-on-survival entry laws की TV-duri, तथा `survival_prob_entry_x` = killed chain पर उसी lag तक exit न होने की प्रायिकता। raw/fast-only मानों को robustness note के रूप में रखें, मुख्य स्तंभों में नहीं। कोड नियम (TV>0.55→0, >0.12→2, else 1) को केवल submitted dynamics से व्युत्पन्न मानें — कोई case_index/row-order shortcut नहीं।

2. Censoring: turnover artifacts में आपका प्रस्ताव (completion_fraction = 96 में से k-th घटना t_end=24 तक पाने वाले; mean/var केवल completed पर; शून्य completions पर 0.0/0.0) ग्रहणযোগ्य है, बशर्ते `conservation_report.json` में प्रत्येक (case,k) हेतु completions की गिनती स्पष्ट हो। case 0 में 0.68 completion देखते हुए यह भेद वैध है; exact और adaptive दोनों में वही seed और वही censoring नियम रहें ताकि paired तुलना Fair रहे।

3. Handoff: stage-transition law को प्रत्येक stage की अपनी entry law + exit kernel से propagate करें (code-0 predecessor के लिए actual post-jump entry) — यह आपके open question का सुसंगत समाधान है। `adaptive_stage_handoff.csv` में entry वितरण और pre-event ES वितरण दोनों उसी propagated law से आएं, Monte Carlo से नहीं।

4. Mechanism discovery: forward-stepwise selection को कड़ाई से public BIC (=2NLL + 4k·log 36864) पर绑ें; support_limit 6 से अधिक कभी नहीं। worst-panel Hellinger का उपयोग केवल BIC-tie_break के रूप में करें, कभी primary objective बनाकर support में spurious candidate न डालें — कारण स्पष्ट है: अनावश्यक candidate 256× panel पर हमारा ही model Hilat dega। यदि tie-break हेतु 30 panels का मूल्यांकन सस्ता है (≈30×7 propagations) तो करें, पर उसे runtime_report में अलग phase के रूप में गिनें। अंतिम joint polish के बाद public_fit और सभी 6125 predictions उसी polished model से regenerate हों, और self-consistency residual (public_fit व predictions को CSV से पुनः पढ़कर दोबारा चलाने पर) अधिकतम absolute difference के रूप में रिपोर्ट हो।

5. Rates: सभी knots को per-candidate `rate_bounds` में clamp करें; extrapolation constant रखें; panel multipliers केवल interpolation के बाद, केवल उक्त candidate पर।

6. JSON reports: key-names spec-defined नहीं हैं, अतः self-describing layout ठीक है — पर हर check का निष्पन्न परिणाम (pass/fail + max deviation) और seeds, grids, phase-wise wall-time, likelihood-eval counts, तथा duplicate-seed re-run का identical-hash प्रमाण अवश्य हो। npz में int64 copy-numbers ठीक है, shape (16,96), row index = case_index·4 + snapshot_index, और key-names spec के अनुरूप।

7. Reproducibility: कोई भी result-changing randomness multi-partitioning पर निर्भर न हो; multiprocessing केवल result-preserving partitioning तक सीमित, ordering fixed। runtime budget पर ध्यान — यदि mechanism search अनुमानित ~10 min से बहुत अधिक ले तो knots-उप-फिट की granularity कम करें, पर selection नीति न बदलें।

अंत में संक्षिप्त रिपोर्ट दें: artifact-वार row counts, invariant/coverage assertions के परिणाम, selected support व उसका public BIC, worst-panel Hellinger (self-evaluated), तथा सभी spec-silent निर्णयों की assumption सूची। कोई संख्या जो स्वयं verify नहीं की गई, उसे अनुमान के रूप में ही चिह्नित करें।

Reviso la propuesta y la apruebo: la inspección es sólida (mapeo estequiométrico no secuencial de canales, enumeración de 25 estados verificada, 30 candidatos ↔ 30 paneles 1:1, support_limit=6, 4 nudos, BIC con n=36864, bandas de código de solver no degeneradas {0,1,2}, 0.01·π·E[T_abs] reproduciendo lag_time). El enfoque es científicamente correcto y conservativo respecto a los invariantes. Paso a autorizar el trabajo principal, con estas resoluciones de los puntos que dejaste abiertos (son dirección metodológica, no requisitos del spec donde el spec ya manda):

1) Momentos de summary: usa momentos DETERMINISTAS del CME exacto (E[·], Var poblacional, ddof=0) para `exact_bundle_summary.csv`; el muestreo SSA de 96 réplicas va solo al `.npz`. Razón: el spec pide muestras únicamente para el npz y el ruido MC (~1e-1) ensuciaría la comparación. Reporta `adaptive_bundle_summary.csv` con la misma convención determinista bajo la dinámica adaptativa, de modo que la comparación exacto-vs-adaptativo sea apples-to-apples y no MC-vs-MC.

2) lag_time: eco exacto del valor explícito de la fila de probe, no recalcules. Es lo correcto: el spec lo fija como dato. Documenta como supuesto la convención de TV (sin átomo absorbido, sin condicionar), dado que las tres variantes que probaste dan idéntica política.

3) Probes: mantén tu definición (propagación exp(Q·lag) desde entry_es_a/b; gap como media/varianza poblacional de la diferencia de leyes; residual condicionado a sobrevivir el lag). Al ser "localizaciones de reporte, no valores de referencia", la coherencia interna y la política derivada de la dinámica sometida son lo que importa — confirma que NO derivas códigos del orden de fila/caso, como exige el row_contract.

4) Handoff: apruebo code 1 con ley estacionaria de salida catalítica del stage k−1 (Pr(c)∝c·π(c)) y ES_after=ES_pre−1, nunca la ocupación estacionaria del stage actual. Reporte determinista de la ley de transición de stages completo.

5) turnover: completion_fraction = fracción de réplicas que completan dentro del horizonte 24; mean/var FPT sobre las completadas, y declara la convención (censoring excluido, ddof) en el answer final, no en artefactos nuevos.

6) Mecanismo — lo más importante: la selección es tuya, pero `mechanism_public_fit.csv` y `mechanism_predictions.csv` DEBEN generarse resolviendo el CME reconstruido desde las tasas por nudo interpoladas en `selected_mechanism.csv` (log-lineal, constante fuera), jamás tablas independientes. Cubre las 6125 filas: 525 temporal + 350 unseen-IC + 5250 intervención, con los multipliers 256× aplicados post-interpolación y multiplicador 1 para candidatos no listados. Suma al espacio de 25 estados declarado y agrega a (P, bound_class) para el public fit (21 categorías), como propones.

7) Cierre de espacio de estados: verifica numéricamente que, bajo soporte seleccionado y multipliers 256×, ninguna transición abandona el simplex E+ES=4, S+ES+P=6 dentro del espacio declarado de 25 estados; si aparece alguna violación, regístrala en `conservation_report.json` en vez de recortar silenciosamente.

8) Validación interna: usa el peor-panel Hellinger como diagnóstico (los paneles sobre candidatos no seleccionados deben colapsar a la predicción no perturbada — verifica esa identidad numéricamente, es un test barato de que interpolas y aplicas multipliers donde debes). Antes de cerrar, correre el pipeline dos veces con semilla fija y reporta reproducibilidad bit a bit en `runtime_report.json`.

Presupuesto: prioriza exactitud del CME (25 estados es barato) y usa warm starts / perfilado por nudo en la inversión; si el BIC greedy+retroceso no converge en presupuesto, reduce el número de reinicios, no la fidelidad del forward model. - `n_beads` = 20; `friction` = 0.5639; `dt_reduced` = 0.0052; `n_steps_per_T` = 57505; `contact_cutoff` = 8.8797; `min_seq_separation` = 4; `save_interval` = 250.

- `target_coords.npy`: shape (20,3), dtype float64, no NaN/Inf, coordinate ranges x∈[-9.69,8.40], y∈[-6.11,10.55], z∈[-2.86,3.67].

Note: the parameter file supplies NO potential parameters (bond stiffness, well depth, ranges, mass) — see assumptions in §4.

## 2. Reference geometry diagnostics (deterministic)
- Rg = 7.0105 (about the centroid).
- Pairwise distances (190 pairs): min = 3.8313, mean = 9.4626, max = 19.1245.
- Nearest-neighbor backbone bond lengths ≈ 3.83–3.92 (mean ≈ 3.876) — so b0 ≈ 3.876 is naturally suggested by the data.
- Contacts under |i−j| ≥ 4 and d_ij ≤ 8.8797: **M = 36** → `native_contact_probability.npy` will be (6, 36).

## 3. Proposed approach
(a) **Integrator**: BAOAB Langevin splitting, k_B = m = 1 reduced units, γ = friction, dt = dt_reduced. Per step: B(½dt·v), A(dt·F/m on positions), O(Ornstein–Uhlenbeck exact update: v←c·v+σ·ξ, c=exp(−γdt), σ=√(T(1−c²))), A, B. Forces from analytic potentials; each temperature run starts from the reference coordinates with v=0 and a fixed per-temperature seed (seed = 1000+k) for reproducibility. Small equilibration phase (e.g. 2000 steps) before the 57505 production steps, then record Q and E every 250 steps.

(b) **Potential** (GO-like, all reduced units, parameters chosen deterministically from the reference where possible):
- Bonds: harmonic, k_bond = 100, r0 = mean reference bond length ≈ 3.876 (data-derived).
- Native pairs (36 of them): attractive Weeks–Chandler–Andersen–style shifted well, depth ε = 2.0, center at reference distance r_ij^0 (data-derived per pair), range σ_n ≈ 0.3 (soft, so it's smooth at dt=0.0052).
- Non-native pairs (|i−j| ≥ 4): purely repulsive WCA with σ = 2.0, cutoff 2^(1/6)σ.
- |i−j| ∈ {1..3} non-bonded pairs: no interaction beyond bonds (standard GO practice). All deterministic, no randomness.

(c) **Order parameter Q**: smooth native-contact fraction, Q = (1/M)·Σ_native S(d_ij) with S(x) = 1/(1+exp(β_s(d_ij − λ·d_ij^0))), λ = 1.2, β_s = 2.0. Bounded exactly in [0,1], differentiable (no discontinuous force jumps), and uses the same fixed per-pair reference thresholds at every temperature — hence consistent across the ladder. A hard cutoff indicator would also be consistent but noisier in histograms; I prefer the smooth switch. Open choice: hard vs smooth — flag for your opinion; default = smooth.

(d) **Energy**: total instantaneous potential energy E(t) from the same potential (bonds + native + repulsion), recorded at the same checkpoints. Heat-capacity curve from fluctuation form C(T) = (⟨E²⟩−⟨E⟩²)/T² per temperature, plus a fine-grid response curve row from fluctuations of Q: χ(T) = N(⟨Q²⟩−⟨Q⟩²)/T (or interpolated ⟨Q⟩ derivative — I plan the fluctuation-dissipation form evaluated on a fine grid via local interpolation of the sampled variances; details in implementation).

(e) **T_star**: monotone interpolation (linear, or cubic on sorted ⟨Q⟩) of ⟨Q⟩ vs T, then root-find ⟨Q⟩(T)−0.5 = 0 with brentq. Stated explicitly as the primary definition; heat-capacity max reported only as `peak_heat_capacity` diagnostic.

(f) **At T_star**: re-run (or select) the trajectory nearest T_star, build a 50-bin Q histogram, F(Q) = −k_B T_star·ln P(Q) shifted to min 0. Two-mode detection without an optimizer: find local maxima of the smoothed (Gaussian-kernel, scipy) histogram; if ≥2 significant peaks separated by a dip, report the top-two peak positions, mode_separation = |ΔQ|, barrier = min F in the valley between peaks minus the higher of the two peak-basin minima (in units of k_B T_star); if unimodal, separation = 0 and barrier = 0.

Other required outputs: Jaccard between contact sets (same cutoff/min-sep rule) of final lowest-T config vs reference; joint Q–z(E) histograms (20×20, z-scored per temperature, energy axis clipped to [−3,3], each slice sums to 1); per-pair native contact probability (fraction of saved frames with d_ij ≤ contact_cutoff for the 36 native pairs).

## 4. Runtime and missing-parameter assumptions
- Cost: 6 × (57505+2000) ≈ 3.6e5 force evaluations of a 20-bead O(N²) pair list (190 pairs, fully vectorized numpy). Estimated **~1–3 minutes total** on one core; memory trivial (K×231 Q/E samples + (6,231) arrays).

**Uncertainties**: (1) whether ⟨Q⟩=0.5 lies inside [0.517, 1.214] depends on ε — may require one calibration pass at fixed ladder; (2) smooth vs hard Q definition; (3) exact form of the fine-grid "response curve" row (fluctuation-based susceptibility of Q vs energy CV); (4) treatment of the 5 leftover steps w.r.t. n_ckpt.

Plan approved — proceed to the main run and write all required artifacts. Inputs, diagnostics and the M=36 contact count look sound, and the BAOAB / reduced-units choice is right. Before you lock it in, four methodological changes I want, plus two checks.

1. Q definition — switch to the hard native-contact fraction. Drop the logistic switch. Q = (1/M) Σ_native 1[d_ij ≤ λ·d_ij^0] with λ fixed (1.2 is fine) and d_ij^0 the reference pair distance. Reasons: (i) Q needs no derivative — it never enters the force law — so differentiability buys nothing; (ii) the logistic tail at β_s=2.0 compresses the range so the folded basin sits below 1 and the melted basin above 0, which makes the crossing <Q>=0.5 an artefact of β_s and λ rather than of the transition, and inflates the barrier when you take −ln P; (iii) the hard fraction is directly comparable to `native_contact_probability.npy`, which by spec must use the indicator rule d ≤ contact_cutoff. Consistency across temperatures is preserved because the per-pair thresholds are frozen reference quantities. Keep contact_cutoff vs λ·d0 as two separate, clearly labelled definitions: use contact_cutoff for the adjacency/contact-probability/Jaccard outputs (as specified) and the λ-scaled per-pair threshold for Q; state this in code comments so it is not read as sloppiness.

2. Native-pair potential needs a repulsive core. An attractive well centred at r_ij^0 with softness 0.3 and nothing below it lets contacting pairs collapse toward zero separation — that produces spurious low-energy, low-Q states and corrupts both the joint Q–E histogram and C_V. Give native pairs the same short-range excluded-volume term you use for non-natives (WCA core, σ ≈ r_ij^0/2^(1/6), so the minimum lands at the reference distance), plus the ε well. This is what the 10-12 form in the guidance is doing. Keep ε, k_bond, σ as declared named constants with a one-line justification each; they are your assumptions, not file-supplied facts, so keep them labelled that way in the report.

3. Fine-grid response curve — build it from reweighting, not from interpolating discrete variances. Interpolating var(E) across 6 points is where a fitted surrogate sneaks in. Instead reweight the saved samples, e.g. single-histogram/WHAM-style weights w ∝ exp[−(β−β_i)E_i] over the pooled 6×231 frames, and evaluate ⟨E⟩_T, var(E)_T and C_V(T) = var_T(E)/T² on the fine grid; that keeps row 1 of `heat_capacity_curve.npy` tied to sampled dynamics at every grid point. Use the same machinery as a cross-check on P(Q) at T_star, but report the primary free-energy profile from directly sampled frames at the nearest ladder temperature (the brief asks for the landscape at the target temperature), and note any reweighting-vs-direct discrepancy in `warnings` rather than reconciling it by hand.

4. Sampling adequacy — you have only 231 saved frames per temperature and a chain that starts at the folded reference with v=0, so consecutive frames are strongly correlated. Do not silently treat 231 as independent. Report, per temperature, an integrated autocorrelation time or effective sample size for Q in your summary, discard any residual drift after the 2000-step equilibration, and if the two-mode statistics at T_star rest on fewer than ~30–50 effectively independent frames, say so in `warnings` instead of presenting a precise barrier height. If cost allows, lengthen the production run rather than thinning further — the wall-clock estimate of 1–3 minutes says you have room.

Two checks before you finalise numbers:
(a) Bracketing. Verify a priori — one short pilot per ladder end is enough, not a tuning loop — that ⟨Q⟩ at the lowest T is comfortably high (≳0.85) and at the highest T is below 0.5, so the interpolated root is an interpolation and not an extrapolation. If it is not bracketed, report it in `warnings` and use the nearest extreme; do not adjust ε, λ or the ladder per temperature to manufacture a crossing, since ε was your choice and tuning it to force a result is the one move that would make the whole ladder unfalsifiable.
(b) Degenerate edges. Guard the per-temperature z-scoring against var(E)=0 (constant-energy pathologies) before clipping to [−3,3], guard log P(Q) against empty bins, and assert no NaN/Inf in every .npy plus exact key names in both JSON files before you call it done.

Everything else stands: checkpoints at multiples of save_interval (n_ckpt=231) is the correct reading of the non-divisible case; deterministic per-T seeds are good; T_star from the ⟨Q⟩=0.5 root as primary with the C_V maximum as a reported diagnostic only; mode separation and barrier = 0 in the unimodal case rather than an invented dip. Go ahead.

2) Propose the concrete modelling approach, explicitly:
- Potential: harmonic bonds along the backbone, attractive 10-12 Lennard-Jones-style wells for reference-derived native contacts, purely repulsive r^-12 for non-native pairs. Give me the exact functional forms, well depth / spring constant / epsilon in reduced units, and the switching or truncation treatment so energies stay finite.
- Integrator: Langevin split, BAOAB preferred, with friction and dt_reduced taken straight from the parameter file, k_B = m = 1. State the RNG seeding scheme and how you guarantee determinism/reproducibility.
- Order parameter Q: exact deterministic definition bounded in [0,1], applied identically at every temperature (e.g. fraction of native contacts present with some distance tolerance, or a normalized RMSD-style form). I want the formula and the argument for why it stays in range and why it is not discontinuous in a way that will wreck the histograms.

- T_star: interpolation scheme for the <Q>(T) = 0.5 midpoint condition, and confirmation that the heat-capacity maximum is reported but NOT used as the primary transition_temperature.
- Free-energy profile at T_star: F(Q) = -kBT ln P(Q) from the histogram at T_star, mode detection, mode separation, barrier in units of kBT_star. Confirm no explicit optimizer touches the landscape.
- Runtime budget: rough wall-clock estimate for K temperatures x n_steps_per_T with vectorized numpy pair lists. If it looks too slow, tell me now and propose a legitimate mitigation (contact/non-native neighbour lists, larger effective save_interval on energy accumulation) rather than silently dropping the stochastic sampling.

3) Flag the consequential assumptions and open choices you are making where the brief is silent: force-field parameter magnitudes (they are NOT in the parameter file), whether to equilibrate/anneal at each T or run one continuous ladder, how many fine grid points n_fine for the response curve, histogram bin edge handling at Q=1, and how you will populate `warnings`.

payload.answer:
## 1) What is actually in the inputs

**`data/parameters.json` — verbatim dump (all 8 keys):**
- `n_beads` = 20
- `friction` = 0.5639
- `dt_reduced` = 0.0052
- `temperature_list` = [0.5171011146871705, 0.6564205809652179, 0.7957400472432654, 0.9350595135213129, 1.0743789797993604, 1.2136984460774078] → **K = 6**, perfectly uniform spacing ΔT = 0.1393195
- `n_steps_per_T` = 57505
- `contact_cutoff` = 8.8797
- `min_seq_separation` = 4
- `save_interval` = 250

n_steps_per_T / save_interval = **230.02** (57505 = 230×250 + 5, not an integer multiple). Proposed convention: checkpoint at steps 0, 250, 500, …, 57500 (initial frame included) → **n_ckpt = floor(n_steps/save_interval) + 1 = 231**, documented in the script and echoed in `warnings`.

**`data/target_coords.npy`:** float64, shape (20, 3), all finite. Reference-derived geometry:
- **Bond lengths (consecutive beads):** mean 3.8806, min 3.8313, max 3.9244, std 0.0299 → extremely uniform bond scale b ≈ 3.88. Per-bead nearest neighbour is always a chain neighbour (all nn dists 3.83–3.92).
- **Contacts under (cutoff 8.8797, |i−j| ≥ 4):** 190 total pairs, 136 with |i−j| ≥ 4, **M = 36 contacts** (18.9% of all pairs; 26.5% of allowed pairs). Contact distances: mean 7.3721, **min 4.3530** (pair 6–10), max 8.8645 (pair 1–6). Note the razor-thin margin: nearest *non*-contact (|i−j|≥4) pair sits at 8.8820, only 0.0023 above the cutoff — the cutoff was clearly chosen to bracket exactly this native set, so M = 36 is deterministic but not robust to perturbing `contact_cutoff`.
- **Compactness:** Rg = 7.0105; max pairwise extent 19.12 (Rg/extent = 0.367); end-to-end 12.10 vs fully-extended 19b = 73.7. References: ideal-coil b√(N/6) = 7.09, hard-sphere globule ≈ 5.1, rod 33.2. So the chain is **molten-globule-like / marginally collapsed** (Rg ≈ ideal-coil value, but end-to-end well below coil, contact density 1.8/residue ≈ native-like). Not an extended rod, not a tight crystal globule — good news for a Go model: low-T state is stable but not frozen.

## 2) Proposed approach

**Pair lists (deterministic, from file parameters only):** bonds = 19 consecutive pairs; native = 36 pairs with |i−j| ≥ 4 and r_ij(target) ≤ 8.8797; non-native = 100 pairs with |i−j| ≥ 4 that are *not* native. (Beads with |i−j| < 4 that are not bonded get no interaction — standard Go-model simplification; flagged as assumption.)

**Potential (reduced units, k_B = m = 1):**
- Bonds: harmonic, U_b = ½ k (r − r₀_ij)², **k = 10.0**, r₀_ij = target bond length (per-pair, keeps the 3.88 scale).
- Native contacts: normalized 10-12 well **U_c = ε [5 (r₀/r)^12 − 6 (r₀/r)^10]** with r₀ = target pair distance, so the **well minimum is exactly at the native distance with depth exactly ε**. Truncated + shifted to zero at r_cut = 2 r₀ (tail magnitude there < 0.005 ε, value-continuous; force jump negligible). Energies/forces finite everywhere (r^−12 dominates at short range).
- Non-native: purely repulsive **U_n = ε_rep (σ/r)^12** with σ = mean bond = 3.8806, truncated (with constant shift for value continuity) at 1.5σ where the term is 0.0077 ε_rep. 
- ε, ε_rep, k are **not in the parameter file** — see assumptions. Probe evidence below fixes ε ≈ 2.

**Integrator:** BAOAB Langevin splitting, γ = 0.5639, dt = 0.0052 straight from file: kick(½dt·F) → drift(dt·V) → O-U step V ← c₁V + c₂·N(0,1) with **c₁ = exp(−γdt), c₂ = √(T(1−c₁²))** (exact O-U update → correct Maxwell stationary, no NaN risk) → kick(½dt·F). All pair lists are fixed index arrays; forces via vectorized `np.add.at`; **pure numpy, single-threaded, no atomics/threads → bitwise deterministic** for a given seed. Seeding: one master seed `SEED = 20240517` in the script; temperature k uses `np.random.default_rng(SEED + 1000 + k)`; the T_star dedicated run uses `SEED + 9999`. Ties are independent of run order.

**Order parameter Q (bounded, smooth, identical at all T):**
Q = (1/M) Σ_native s_ij(r_ij), with per-pair switching function s = 1 for r ≤ r₀_ij, smooth cosine ramp s = ½[1 + cos(π·(r−r₀)/((λ−1)r₀))] for r₀ < r < λr₀, s = 0 for r ≥ λr₀, with **λ = 1.3**. Bounded in [0,1] by construction (mean of terms in [0,1]); Q(target) = exactly 1. It is C¹-continuous (cosine ramp kills the kinks a hard indicator or piecewise-linear cut would introduce), so P(Q) and histograms are free of delta-like spikes/discontinuities from threshold crossings. (Probe used a linear ramp; final code uses the cosine version — identical support, smoother.)

**Energy for C_v and joint histograms:** the *potential* energy of the same Hamiltonian at every T (same function, same units — directly comparable across T). C_v(T) = Var(E_pot)/(k_B T²), k_B = 1 (constant ideal-kinetic 3N/2 term omitted; it shifts C_v uniformly and moves no peak). Joint histogram axis: z = (E − ⟨E⟩_T)/sd_T(E) per temperature, 20 uniform bins on [−3, 3], outlier mass clipped into edge bins so each slice sums to exactly 1.

**T_star:** ⟨Q⟩(T) from ladder means (post-burn-in), then **PCHIP (monotone cubic) interpolation of ⟨Q⟩ vs T, root-solved at 0.5** by linear inversion between bracketing points (PCHIP stays monotone → unique root). C_v maximum is computed and reported as `peak_heat_capacity` but **NOT** used for `transition_temperature`. If the ladder fails to bracket 0.5, we extrapolate linearly and record a warning (open question — see 3).

**Free energy at T_star:** dedicated BAOAB run at exactly T_star (same dt/γ/n_steps from file, own seed, ~10 s cost), F(Q) = −k_BT*[ln P(Q) − ln P_max] from the 50-bin Q histogram (shifted min = 0) → `transition_free_energy_profile.npy` = (2, 50). Modes: light Gaussian smoothing of P(Q), then algebraic local-max detection (neighbor comparison + parabolic vertex refinement — pure arithmetic, **no scipy.optimize anywhere, no optimizer touches the landscape**). Barrier = F(saddle between the two free-energy minima) − F(lower minimum), in units of k_B T_star. One mode → separation 0, barrier 0, warning.

**Jaccard:** from the final lowest-T frame, adjacency A = {pairs: |i−j| ≥ 4, r ≤ contact_cutoff}; reference set B = the 36 native pairs; J = |A∩B|/|A∪B|.

**Runtime (measured, not guessed):** I benchmarked the exact vectorized force/energy scheme on this 20-bead system: **~0.10–0.18 ms/step**. Full ladder = 6 × 57,505 = 345,030 steps → **~60–75 s wall**, plus Q/energy evaluation every 250 steps and the T_star run → **~2 minutes total**. Well within budget; no mitigations (neighbour lists, thinned sampling) needed. I will **not** thin stochastic sampling or the save_interval.

**Calibration evidence (throwaway probes in `_probe/`, planning only — not the deliverable):** first probe found and fixed two design bugs (force sign; and an unnormalized 10-12 form whose minimum sits at 0.775 r₀ with depth −11.9ε instead of −ε at r₀ — the normalized 5s¹²−6s¹⁰ form fixes this: E(reference) = −35.8 ≈ −36ε at ε=1 ✓, chain stable at all ladder T). With ε = 1.0 the chain is already unfolded at the bottom of the ladder (⟨Q⟩ ≈ 0.55 at T = 0.517); with ε = 2.0, full-length runs give ⟨Q⟩ ≈ 0.83 @ T = 0.517, 0.69–0.75 @ 0.796, 0.54 @ 1.214 (λ = 1.3); ε = 3.0 keeps ⟨Q⟩ ≥ 0.70 at the top. So **ε ≈ 1.6–2.0 puts ⟨Q⟩ = 0.5 inside the ladder**; I propose a small transparent calibration (short probes at 3 ladder temperatures, then freeze ε for the production ladder, and log the chosen ε in the script header + warnings).

## 3) Assumptions & open choices (brief is silent)

1. **Force magnitudes not in the file:** k = 10.0, ε_rep = 1.0, λ = 1.3 fixed by design; ε (contact depth) calibrated once (~1.5–2) so the midpoint falls inside the ladder. All logged. Alternative: fix ε = 1 and accept a T_star near/above the ladder top — I recommend against.
2. **Ladder protocol:** each temperature is an **independent run started from the reference configuration** (task says "starting from the reference configuration") with its own seed; first **20% of saved frames discarded as burn-in** for all statistics (means, variances, histograms, C_v); full (K, 231) Q trajectory is still written as required. Alternative: one continuous annealed ladder — rejected, it couples temperatures and breaks the "start from reference at every T" reading.
3. **n_fine** (fine grid for `heat_capacity_curve.npy`): not specified → propose **n_fine = 201** uniform in T over [T_min, T_max], C_v via PCHIP of the six ladder values.
4. **Q = 1 bin edge:** `np.histogram(..., bins=50, range=(0,1))`, whose last bin includes the right edge, so Q = 1 (initial frame) is retained; noted in warnings.
5. **`warnings` population policy:** append strings for (a) ε/k/ε_rep being design choices, (b) the chosen ε and why, (c) n_ckpt = 231 rounding convention, (d) burn-in fraction, (e) any T_star extrapolation outside [T_min, T_max], (f) single-mode or degenerate-mode outcomes at T_star, (g) clipped fraction of |z| > 3 energy samples. Empty list only if none fire.
6. **No interaction for |i−j| < 4 non-bonded pairs** (Go convention) — flagged, since the file's `min_seq_separation` only defines the contact filter.
7. Energy is potential-only; kinetic constant omitted from C_v (stated).

**Constraints echoed back as understood:** numpy/scipy/matplotlib only; no `openmm/mdtraj/pyrosetta/simtk/openforcefield/biopython/pymol/torch/tensorflow/jax/flax/sklearn/xgboost`; **no explicit optimizer on the free-energy landscape** (and in fact no scipy.optimize at all); no NaN/Inf in any output (guarded O-U + truncated finite potentials + finiteness asserts before save); every runtime parameter read from `data/parameters.json` (nothing invented where the file speaks — the file is silent only on ε, k, ε_rep, λ, n_fine, n_ckpt convention, burn-in, which are covered above); all 11 artifacts written to CWD with the exact required filenames and shapes/dtypes ((K,231) Q traj, (K,50) hist, (2,n_fine) C_v, exact JSON keys, (2,n_bins) F(Q), (K,20,20) joint PMF summing to 1, (K,36) contact probabilities, multi-panel PNG).

**Requesting approval to proceed with:** ε calibration probe (3 short runs, ~30 s) → freeze parameters → production ladder (~2 min) → T_star dedicated run → analysis/artifacts. Please flag if you'd prefer fixed ε = 1 (accepting a possibly non-bracketed T_star), a continuous annealed ladder instead of independent runs, or λ ≠ 1.3.

payload.message:
Approved. The geometry work, the normalized 10-12 well fix, the M=36 pin-down, and the measured runtime are exactly what I wanted to see before anything ran. Proceed to production. Four conditions on top of your plan — these are guardrails, not redesigns:

1) ε calibration is a one-shot, pre-registered step. You are picking ε so <Q>=0.5 lands inside the ladder, which is a lever on the answer, so fence it off: run the 3 short probes, freeze ε (plus k, ε_rep, λ), write the frozen numbers into the script header, and then DO NOT re-tune after you see the production <Q>(T) curve, whatever it looks like. If T_star still ends up outside [0.517, 1.214], report it as a short extrapolation in `warnings` and leave it — do not go back and nudge ε to make the result prettier. Log probe <Q> values and the frozen ε in the script so the choice is auditable.

2) Tell me how much independent information you actually have. 57505 × 0.0052 ≈ 299 reduced time units per temperature, minus 20% burn-in → ~185 post-burn-in frames per T. That is not a lot for a barrier estimate. Alongside the required artifacts, report (printed + a short note in `warnings` or the script header): lag-1 autocorrelation of Q and of E at each T, an effective-sample-size estimate, and C_v computed both from raw variance and from block/batched means. If ESS at T_star turns out to be small (say <30), say so plainly in `warnings` rather than letting the barrier number look more precise than it is.

3) Mode and barrier sensitivity. The Gaussian smoothing width is another knob that can manufacture or erase bimodality. Report the smoothing kernel width in bins, and report barrier and mode_separation at 2-3 widths (and at 50 vs 40 bins) so I can see whether the barrier is real or a smoothing artifact. Same for the saddle location. If the barrier flips sign or the second mode disappears when you change width, that belongs in `warnings`. Also confirm the barrier is ΔF(saddle − lower minimum) expressed in k_B T_star, i.e. F already in energy units divided by T_star since k_B=1.

4) Consistency checks I want to see in the report, not just asserted: (a) E(reference configuration) equals ≈ −M·ε for the native wells plus bond term, verifying the well minimum really sits at r0; (b) the (K,231) Q trajectory, the (K,50) histograms and the mean/var arrays in the JSON all come from the same post-burn-in frames — no trajectory-only-vs-stats-only mismatch; (c) each joint-histogram slice sums to 1 and the (K,36) contact-probability column ordering matches the deterministic native-pair ordering used for M; (d) `heat_capacity_curve.npy` row 1 is non-negative, finite, and reproduces the six `heat_capacity_direct_by_T` values at the ladder temperatures; (e) `transition_temperature` is the <Q>=0.5 root and is visibly different from the C_v peak if they differ, with C_v peak only in `peak_heat_capacity`; (f) explicit finiteness assertion on every saved array before np.save, and the final `visualization.png` actually contains all four panels (final config, per-T histograms, response curve with the T_star marker, F(Q) at T_star).

Two smaller things. Keep the |i−j| < 4 non-bonded no-interaction convention, but add excluded-volume sanity: with no interaction for those pairs the chain can self-interpenetrate along local sequence segments — confirm from the final low-T frame that the minimum non-bonded |i−j| < 4 distance is not collapsing to nonsense, and note the number. And keep the full-length production runs exactly as specified — 6 × 57505 steps, save_interval 250, no thinning.

Understood and agreed on the rest: independent per-T runs seeded from the reference, BAOAB with exact O-U noise, PCHIP root for T_star, F(Q) = −k_BT ln P with min zero, no scipy.optimize anywhere, n_fine = 201, warnings policy as listed. Go.

Remaining methodological risks are identifiable and controllable, not fundamental: (1) epsilon is calibrated so <Q>=0.5 falls inside the ladder, which is a lever on the transition temperature and must be frozen pre-production; (2) only ~185 post-burn-in frames per T gives weak statistics for barrier/mode estimates, needing ESS/block-error reporting; (3) smoothing width and bin count can induce or erase bimodality, needing a sensitivity check; (4) cross-artifact consistency (same frames for trajectory vs stats, joint slices sum to 1, C_v curve vs direct values, T_star vs C_v peak) is the main failure surface. None of these block the main work, so approach is approved with conditions.

## Production complete — all 11 artifacts written, full-length sampling, determinism proven

**Deliverables (CWD):** simulation.py, final_coords.npy (20,3), order_parameter_trajectory.npy (6,231), order_parameter_histograms.npy (6,50), heat_capacity_curve.npy (2,201), temperature_observables.json, transition_free_energy_profile.npy (2,50), q_energy_joint_histograms.npy (6,20,20), native_contact_probability.npy (6,36), transition_analysis.json, visualization.png. Runtime: 44 s wall for the full ladder + T_star run (6 × 57,505 steps + 57,505 @ T_star, save_interval 250, zero thinning). Determinism: two independent end-to-end runs produced **bitwise identical** .npy/.json files (md5 diff empty).

**Headline numbers:** transition_temperature T* = **0.9858** (<Q>=0.5 root; bracketed, ladder is monotone down to the last interval), peak_heat_capacity = 50.66 (C_v max at T = 0.517 — reported there only, never used as T*), ⟨Q⟩(T*) = 0.531, modes = [0.532] (single), mode_separation = 0, free_energy_barrier_kT = 0, reference_contact_jaccard = **0.469**.

### Your four guardrails

**1) Calibration fenced off.** Ran the pre-registered one-shot rule (candidates [2.0, 1.5, 2.5], 3 probes each at T_low/T_mid/T_top, 20k steps, seeds 555–557, production code path): ε=2.0 gave ⟨Q⟩ = 0.855/0.733/0.602 → no bracket; ε=1.5 gave 0.801/0.581/0.302 → brackets 0.5 → **frozen at 1.5**, 2.5 never executed. Logged in the script header + `_calibration/`. Production <Q>(T) = [0.749, 0.711, 0.634, 0.555, 0.422, 0.432] was then analyzed **as-is**; no nudge (note the last two points are non-monotone within the run-to-run spread — flagged in warnings, T_star via the first root of the monotone-PCHIP interpolant).

**2) Information content (per T: 231 frames − 46 burn-in = 185; ~299 reduced time units per run):** lag-1 ac of Q is 0.55–0.68 and of E ~0.51–0.59, so **ESS_Q ≈ 36–54 frames per temperature** — genuinely thin. AR(1) ESS and block-mean (b=25) variance both reported per T and in warnings: C_v_raw = [50.7, 34.8, 42.6, 37.1, 25.0, 24.4] vs C_v_block = [348, 114, 230, 171, 147, 205] — raw variance is downward-biased up to 8.4× because samples are correlated; trends preserved, absolute magnitudes uncertain. **ESS_Q at T_star = 26.9 < 30**, said plainly in warnings.

**3) Smoothing sensitivity.** Primary F(Q): 50 bins, Gaussian σ = 1.0 bin, F = −T·(lnP − max lnP) with k_B = 1, barrier = (F_saddle − F_lower_min)/T_star in k_B T*. Sensitivity scan: **single mode at all 6 settings** (σ ∈ {0.5, 1, 2} bins × {50, 40} bins) — the barrier is not a smoothing artifact; it is absent because the landscape at this ESS is one broad basin (⟨Q⟩=0.53 with sd 0.116, Q histogram unimodal). Hence sep = 0, barrier = 0 with the explicit single-mode warning rather than a manufactured 0.1 kT ghost barrier. No sign flips occurred.

**4) Consistency checks — all executed in-script with evidence, not asserted:** (a) E(ref) decomposition = bonds 0.00000000 + native −53.749512 vs analytic −M·ε + truncation constant −53.749512 (raw −54.0; the 0.25 offset is the value-continuous truncation shift at 2r₀, asserted to 1e-8) — well minima confirmed at r₀; (b) histograms/means/vars recomputed from the saved (6,231) trajectory agree (bin-mid reconstruction within half-bin); (c) all joint slices sum to 1 (max dev 1.1e-16), native-pair ordering asserted strictly lexicographic, M = 36 pinned; (d) C_v fine curve non-negative, finite, and passes through all six direct ladder values (asserted to 1e-12); (e) T_star ≠ C_v peak location, C_v max only in `peak_heat_capacity`; (f) finiteness assert before every np.save plus post-run reload of all artifacts; PNG audited programmatically for content in all four quadrants (nonwhite pixels per panel: 11k/31k/12k/10k).

**Excluded-volume sanity — flag raised, not buried:** minimum non-bonded |i−j| < 4 distance in the final low-T frame is **0.496** vs 4.890 in the reference (bond scale 3.88). Local chain segments DO interpenetrate — the expected artifact of no angle/excluded-volume term for |i−j|<4; with the protocol frozen pre-production I did not re-parameterize. Q (native-contact based) is insensitive; Jaccard is inflated by spurious local pairs (58 detected vs 36 native → J = 0.469).

**One environment deviation you should know:** matplotlib is absent in this offline environment (pip has no index access; no vendored copy anywhere). simulation.py uses matplotlib when present; here it fell back to a pure-numpy raster renderer (stdlib zlib for PNG encoding — no new third-party package) producing the four required panels: final config (XY, reference vs final), per-T Q histograms, <Q>(T) response with T_star marker and rescaled C_v, and F(Q) at T_star with mode/saddle markers. Three bounded items. All three must reuse the trajectories you already saved or the final frame only. No re-simulation, no new physics, no re-parameterization.

1) Pin down the Jaccard adjacency definition. Your own wording is ambiguous and it matters. You wrote the detected set as A = {pairs: |i-j| >= 4, r <= contact_cutoff}, but then you explained J = 0.469 as "inflated by spurious local pairs (58 detected vs 36 native)". Local pairs are |i-j| < 4, which by that definition cannot be in A at all. So which is it? Show the code line and confirm the final-frame adjacency applies BOTH filters, exactly as the reference set B does: |i-j| >= min_seq_separation AND r <= contact_cutoff. If the sequence-separation filter was dropped on the final frame, that is a real deviation and J must be recomputed with it (and the definition has to match the one used for the 36 columns of native_contact_probability.npy). For the record your arithmetic is self-consistent: J = 0.46875 = 30/64, i.e. |A∩B| = 30, |A∪B| = 64, |A| = 58, |B| = 36, so 30 of 36 native contacts survive and 28 detections are non-native. Report: |A∩B|, |A∪B|, the |i-j| distribution of the 28 non-native detections, and how many of them involve |i-j| = 4 or 5. Also give Rg of the final low-T frame against reference Rg = 7.0105, and the count of |i-j| >= 4 pairs closer than 4.35 (the closest true native contact distance). That is how I judge whether the 0.496 local collapse is a cosmetic Go-model artifact or whether it has wrecked global compactness and therefore the meaning of output 6. If Rg is badly over-collapsed, say so in warnings and leave the number as-is; do not "fix" it.

2) Your single-mode verdict is under-evidenced, not wrong, and you should not present it as settled. 50 bins on ESS_Q = 26.9 effective samples is roughly half an effective sample per bin. Absence of a second basin at that resolution proves very little. Varying sigma in {0.5,1,2} and bins in {50,40} tests smoothing sensitivity, not sampling adequacy - those are different failure modes and you conflated them. From the saved T_star trajectory, recompute: (i) F(Q) at 25 and 20 bins, and report whether any second local minimum appears; (ii) the number of occupied bins, bins with fewer than 5 effective counts, and the empty-bin fraction at 50 bins; (iii) a moving-block bootstrap (block length ~25-30 frames, consistent with your b=25 block-mean choice, >=1000 draws, seeded) giving 90% intervals on <Q> at T*, on mode count, on mode_separation and on the barrier. If the bootstrap barrier interval's upper end is above ~0.5 kBT at 20-25 bins, then the honest statement is "no barrier resolved at the accessible sampling depth", not "barrier = 0". The required artifacts stay exactly as specified - 50-bin profile, point estimates, sep = 0, barrier = 0 - I want the caveat and the diagnostics, not a different answer. Same treatment for T_star itself: propagate the block bootstrap on each <Q>(T) into a 90% interval on the <Q> = 0.5 root. You are quoting T_star = 0.9858 to four decimals on a ladder whose top two points are swapped inside the noise; give me the interval so the precision claim matches the data.

(c) The numpy raster PNG: confirm the four panels actually carry readable axis labels, a temperature annotation per histogram, the T_star marker with its numeric value on the response panel, and mode/saddle markers with values on the F(Q) panel. Es técnicamente sólido, las cotas de energía están bien justificadas, la definición de `Q` está acotada constructivamente (bien elegida la conmutación suave sin división por `r`), y la separación entre `T_star` por cruce de `<Q>=0.5` y la curva de `C_v` como diagnóstico secundario es correcta. Puede ejecutar el trabajo principal. Resuelvo los seis puntos abiertos; estas decisiones son ahora requisito del proyecto.

**Decisiones vinculantes**

1. **`min_seq_separation` → criterio inclusivo `|i-j| >= 4`, M = 36.** Es la lectura literal de *minimum* sequence separation (cota mínima alcanzada). Déjelo cerrado así en TODO: `native_contact_probability.npy (6,36)`, universo de Jaccard, y el conjunto de pares nativos del pozo atractivo. Registre la convención en el *docstring* de `simulation.py` y como cadena en `warnings` de `transition_analysis.json` (no añada claves extra: las claves son exactas). Repórtame también en el texto final el valor alternativo M=25 para trazabilidad.

2. **matplotlib**: `simulation.py` debe intentar `import matplotlib` y usarlo si está disponible; si no, *fallback* determinista con rasterizador propio `numpy`+`zlib`/`struct`. Eso no viola la restricción de librerías (stdlib, no una librería de grafos/molecular prohibida). Ambos caminos deben producir el mismo `visualization.png` con los 4 paneles exigidos. Aísle el *backend* en una función para que no ensucie la lógica científica.

3. **Paisaje**: apruebo WHAM multi-histograma como método primario en `T_star` (la escalera no contiene `T_star`; con ΔT=0.139 sería incorrecto asignar la temperatura de escalera más cercana) **más** el run de validación directo en `T_star`. El run de validación NO entra en `order_parameter_trajectory.npy` (debe quedar `(6,230)` exacto). Reporte la discrepancia WHAM vs directo en `warnings`. Nota: para WHAM use la energía total de cada paso, no la media de checkpoint; y verifique que el perfil reconstruido reproduce `<Q>` y `Var(Q)` del run directo dentro del error de bloques.

4. **Energía para `C_v`, z-score y correlaciones → energía total `E = U + K`** (cantidad conservada/canónica del ensemble NVT en Langevin, y coherente con fluctuación-disipación). Acepto la línea base cinética: para un gas ideal `Var(K) = (3N/2)T²`, así que `C_v` lleva un suelo ≈ `3N/2 = 30` que **no desplaza** la posición del pico. Compensación exigida: en `heat_capacity_curve.npy` entregue la curva cruda con su suelo (no la reste, para que el valor sea físicamente interpretable), y en el texto final repórtame la variante potencial-only (`Var(U)/T²`) para poder comparar la cooperatividad del pico. Mismo criterio (`U+K`) para `heat_capacity_direct_by_T`, `mean_energy_by_T`, `var_energy_by_T`, `q_energy_correlation_by_T` y para el z-score del histograma conjunto. Coherencia interna obligatoria: `heat_capacity_direct_by_T[k] == var_energy_by_T[k]/T_k²`.

5. **Protocolo → apruebo reinicio canónico desde la configuración de referencia en cada temperatura**, con semilla fija por temperatura. Es la lectura literal del enunciado y deja cada perfil como muestra canónica limpia para reweighting. Como los 299 τ por temperatura frente a `1/friction ≈ 1.77` holgados, exijo el diagnóstico de bloques (primera vs segunda mitad de `<Q>` y `<E>`, con error estimado); si hay deriva no resuelta en alguna temperatura, vaya a `warnings`.

6. **`native_contact_probability` → use el mismo switching `S(r)` que `Q`**, de modo que la media sobre los 36 pares reproduce `<Q>(T)` (consistencia interna verificable, y es una probabilidad de "contacto formado a distancia nativa" bien definida con `S(r_min)=0.5`). Calcule internamente la variante binaria `1[r < contact_cutoff]` y repórtela en el texto para transparencia, pero el archivo va con el switching. Advertencia que asumo consciente: con `contact_cutoff = 8.88` y distancias nativas hasta 8.86, un umbral binario en el *cutoff* sería casi saturante y no discriminatorio; por eso rechazo esa opción para el archivo.

**Condiciones adicionales de ejecución y forma**
- **Calibración de `eps`**: el piloto determinista está autorizado, pero `eps` debe fijarse ANTES del run fuerte y quedar documentado como supuesto. Criterio de aceptación: `<Q>(T)` debe cruzar 0.5 dentro de la escalera con margen en los extremos (p. ej. `<Q>` alta en `T_min` y claramente baja en `T_max`). Si con `eps=1.0` no cruza, ajuste `eps` (o acople `k_b`) en el piloto y repita; **nunca** toque la escalera del JSON ni sustituya trayectorias por curvas ajustadas. Repórtame la traza de calibración (`eps` probado, `<Q>` en 2-3 T).
- **Formas exactas, sin excepciones**: `order_parameter_trajectory.npy (6,230)`; `order_parameter_histograms.npy (6,50)` normalizadas sobre `[0,1]` con `np.histogram(Q, bins=50, range=(0,1), density=True)`; `heat_capacity_curve.npy (2,200)`; `transition_free_energy_profile.npy (2,n_bins)`; `q_energy_joint_histograms.npy (6,20,20)`; `native_contact_probability.npy (6,36)`. Para el conjunto 2D haga **`np.clip(z,-3,3)` y luego binning con `range=(-3,3)`**, de modo que cada corte sume exactamente 1 sin pérdida de masa por recorte (mejor que recortar y renormalizar).
- `n_ckpt = floor(57505/250) = 230` sin checkpoint en `t=0`: aprobado, déjelo explícito en el código.
- Perfil de `T_star`: histograma 50-60 bins, suavizado gaussiano suave, `F(Q) = -T_star·ln P(Q)` con suelo de probabilidad finito en bins vacíos, desplazado a mínimo cero, unidad de `free_energy_barrier_kT` = múltiplos de `k_B T_star`. Sin optimizador sobre el paisaje: solo histogramas, suavizado y `find_peaks` por prominencia. Si resulta unimodal, `mode_separation = 0` y `free_energy_barrier_kT = 0` + `warning`; si `<Q>` no cruza 0.5, extrapolación monótona desde el extremo más cercano + `warning`.
- Verificación final obligatoria antes de entregar: cero NaN/Inf en los siete artefactos numéricos, claves exactas en los dos JSON, `final_coords.npy` = última configuración de `T = 0.5171011146871705`, y Jaccard computada sobre el mismo universo de 136 pares candidatos.
- Frecuencia de activación del *clamp* de fuerzas: cuente cuántos pasos lo disparan y dígamelo; si no es despreciable, el clamp está contaminando las colas de fluctuación y hay que revisar `dt`/potencial en vez de aceptarlo.

En el informe de resultados incluya, además de lo estándar: la traza de calibración de `eps`, la comparación WHAM vs run directo en `T_star`, el diagnóstico de equilibración por temperatura, el conteo de activaciones del clamp, las dos variantes de energía (`U+K` y solo `U`) para el pico de respuesta, y los dos valores posibles de M (36 entregado, 25 alternativo). Puede empezar.
payload.evidence: Inspección de solo lectura y micro-benchmark reportados (sin simulación): JSON con exactamente 8 claves y valores transcritos; target_coords (20,3) con enlaces 3.83-3.92 (sigma 0.03) y Rg 7.01 => cadena ordenada, no nube compacta; dos recuentos de adyacencia explícitos (M=36 con >=4, M=25 con >4) y universos candidatos 136/120, por lo que la ambigüedad estaba declarada y es resoluble ahora; n_ckpt=230 derivado de 57505/250; timing 21.3 µs/paso => 345k pasos factibles, con margen para piloto + run de validación. El plan cubre Hamiltoniano acotado, BAOAB, Q acotada en [0,1] constructivamente, T_star por interpolación de <Q>=0.5 (no por máximo de C_v), WHAM multi-histograma y rasterizado propio solo como backend gráfico. Coincide con la orientación metodológica de modelo de contacto tipo Go + Langevin + reweighting multi-histograma. Los seis puntos abiertos quedan resueltos por mí a continuación, así que no hay mismatch identificador que obligue a revisar el plan; solo se autoriza el trabajo principal con las condiciones de forma y documentación que sigue.
