План принимаю, работаем. Инвентарь нормальный, fingerprint-логика там, где нужно, и то, что суффиксы реально переставлены в кейсах, ты поймал — это и есть главный риск, и ты его не запрятал. Одобряю, давай основную работу. Но прежде чем ты закроешь вилки конвенций, зафиксируй несколько вещей, иначе потом переделывать.

1) Симметрии — используй их, не трать время на перебор.
- Если attention-скоры это dot(q,k) с симметричной обработкой bias'ов, то обмен q↔kLeave output неизменным. Значит эта двусмысленность внутри класса (48,16) безвредна, её не надо «разрешать». Реальный дискриминант один: какой из трёх rect-массивов — value (и/или gate) путь, а какие два — парные q/k. Не гоняй все 6 перестановок как 6 разных гипотез; гоняй «кто третий».
- То же по aux-векторам: один положительный ~0.45–0.70 это кандидат на gate/scale, два zero-mean — bias'ы. Проверь, что привязка bias↔матрица не даёт ложной свободы: если bias'ы q и k входят в скорости, их обмен тоже может быть симметричен, а bias value-пути — нет.
- Обменяй местами q/k в calibration-кейсе 1 (где gain — vector_2) и подтверди, что target не меняется. Если меняется — моя симметрия не holds, тогда скажи прямо, и будем различать по-честному.

2) Про `repeat_factor=3`. Явно проверь гипотезу, что это просто счёт rect-матриц (q,k,v), т.е. то же число, что и `kv_matrices (3,3,16)` по второй оси, а не число повторов слоя. Если forward — один слой, это почти наверняка счётчик; но проверь на формах, а не верь.

3) Таблицы. Ты правильно нашёл, что это абсолютная позиционная rotary-пара на 2 частоты и НЕ T×T relative. Теперь обязательно покажи, как `table_width=4` и `part_width=8` связываются с парами каналов: 2 пары на часть (первые 4 канала каждой из 6 частей) или 2 пары всего на aux-вектор. Это не косметика — от этого зависит и forward, и градиент по таблицам. Градиенты по таблицам вообще не забудь: они ненулевые только на использованных позициях, и их тоже прогони через разностную проверку.

4) Роль probe'ов vs роль runtime. Жёсткое требование: в момент вызова `sequence_operator_*` не читают ни `data/`, ни probe-файлы, ни `reference/`, и не держат карты суффиксов. Вся подгонка по probe'ам — offline-этап, а в коде живёт только `infer_roles(params, meta)` из форм+значений. Если внутри класса остаётся неразрешимая по значениям двусмысленность, не маскируй её: скажи «вот здесь оператор инвариантен» или «вот здесь я выбираю канон по такому-то правилу, и вот почему он должен переноситься на скрытые массивы». Честное «не разрешимо по описанию» лучше красивого правила без опоры.

5) Устойчивость к формам. Никаких 48/13/16/6/2 в логике. Выводи всё из `meta` и форм: `width = parts_a*part_width`, `aux = parts_b*part_width`, `T` из x, число частот из `table_1.shape[-1]`, leading-оси любые (1 ось, 2 оси). Segment_ids не предполагай монотонными и не предполагают, что id'ы dense 0..S-1 в порядке появления — маскируй по равенству id, а не по порядку.

6) Критерии готовности, с которыми я приму результат. Хочу видеть в отчёте конкретно:
   - таблицу остатков по всем 16 публичным откликам для выбранного варианта (4 основных + 12 calibration), в abs и rel величинах;
   - сколько вариантов дало остаток ~1e-9. Если больше одного — это неразличимость, перечисли их и скажи, чем они отличаются и почему это не ломает градиенты;
   - таблицу max rel-ошибки reverse-mode против центральных разностей отдельно для x, каждой matrix, каждого vector и обеих таблиц (не только «в целом сошлось»);
   - проверку HVP через смешанную разность, как ты сам предложил, плюс симметрию билинейной формы на хотя бы двух направлениях;
   - явный список того, что ты интерпретировал, и что осталось допущением.

7) На диск — ровно три файла: `results/output.npy` (forward на основном x/segment_ids), `results/input_gradient.npy` (dL/dx для L=sum(out*sensitivity)), `results/input_hvp.npy` (x-компонента HVP по переданному direction, полная форма x). Полный градиентный и HVP-словари — только через возврат функций, не файлами.

И отдельно: `backward(sensitivity, cache, params, meta)` получает sensitivity отдельно, значит forward обязан закешировать все промежуточные состояния (нормы, проекции, скорости/веса, маски, значения cos/sin, softmax-выходы), чтобы backward ничего не пересчитывал по x. Проверь это — иначе HVP пойдёт по несуществующему следу.

Давай: forward + идентификация по probe'ам сначала, градиенты и HVP следующим шагом, как и планировал.

- The only *exact* internal structure in the whole file set is the two tables: `table_cos² + table_sin² ≡ 1` (≤1e-12) with angle ladder ω_j = 10000^(−2j/table_width) = (1.0, 0.01), i.e. textbook RoPE with `table_width = 4` channels = **2 adjacent (even,odd) pairs**. `table_0` here is SIN, `table_1` is COS.

## 2. Calibration file structure (`calibration_cases.npz`, 22 keys)

`schema_version`=1, `case_count`=3 (scalars). Data keys (shapes):
`x`(3,2,13,48), `segment_ids`(3,2,13), `sensitivity`(3,2,13,48), `meta_json`(3,) `<U206` (all three are byte-identical to the public meta.json), `probe_x`(3,4,2,13,48), `probe_segment_ids`(3,4,2,13), `probe_sensitivities`(3,4,2,13,48), `probe_targets`(3,4).

**The decisive discovery** — the file also stores *role-group* names with anonymous members:
`square_matrix_names`(3,2)+`square_matrices`(3,2,48,48); `kv_matrix_names`(3,3)+`kv_matrices`(3,3,48,16); `width_vector_names`(3,3)+`width_vectors`(3,3,48); `kv_vector_names`(3,3)+`kv_vectors`(3,3,16); `head_vector_names`(3,1)+`head_vectors`(3,1,6); `table_names`(3,2)+`tables`(3,2,13,2).

Total scalar constraints available for identification: **4 public + 12 calibration = 16**, spread over **4 independent parameter sets**.

Shape classes are *exactly* the calibration groups, so permutation is confined to: {matrix_0, matrix_2} (48×48), {matrix_1, matrix_3, matrix_4} (48,16), {vector_0,1,2} (48,), {vector_3,4,6} (16,), {table_0, table_1} (13,2), {vector_5} (singleton, len=parts_a). Shape-compatibility chain: x (·,48) → 48×48 squares → head-8 × 6; 48×16 matrices → aux-16 → head-8 × 2, which is exactly the head count implied by len(head_vector) — consistent with grouped-query attention with `repeat_factor=3` (2 aux heads shared by 6 query heads), and `table_width=4` = 2 rope pairs.

Fingerprints I propose to use, in priority order:
1. **Exact functional form** (strongest): a table is a cosine iff row0 == 1 exactly, a sine iff row0 == 0, verified by `cos²+sin²=1` per column. Nothing else in the file set has exact closed form.
2. **Positivity + mean anchor** for scaling roles: a vector that is strictly positive with mean≈1 (std≈0.08) is a width gain; a strictly positive vector with mean≈0.55 is an aux gate/scale. Verified to hold for the same *role* across all 4 instances even as the anonymous name changes.
3. **Magnitude tiers** for the rest: squares 0.64 vs 1.01 (×1/√48); aux matrices 1.02/1.04 vs 0.22; width biases 0.013 vs 0.035–0.046; aux biases 0.016–0.024 vs 0.048–0.084. Ratios ≥2.4× in every instance → a rank-by-σ rule is stable.
4. **Ordering fingerprint**: the parts_a-length head vector is sorted ascending and all-positive in all 4 instances.
5. **Additive vs multiplicative test at fit time**: biases are small-σ and appear additively; gains appear multiplicatively (they are near-1/positive so a wrong additive use is immediately visible in the probe residual).
6. Causal-mask/segment evidence: masks are *constant* 0/1 matrices in any candidate; segment ids are monotone contiguous partitions, and with max segment length 6 > `span` 5 the window-vs-no-window and boundary-masking choices are observable in the 16 probes.

## 4. Proposed computational approach (stages)

Stage 0 — role resolution on the arrays passed at call time (never on suffixes): shape-class bucketing → fingerprints above → a `roles` dict keyed by the anonymous names.
Stage 1 — forward, all NumPy, derived dims only from `x.shape` and array shapes: partition by `segment_ids`; project x with the two 48×48 matrices (query and output-side) and the three 48×16 matrices (aux/query-group projections) plus their biases; reshape to heads of width `part_width`; apply rotary to the `table_width` channels of each head using adjacent (even,odd) pairs and row `t` of each table where `t` is the **absolute final-axis index starting at 0, not reset at boundaries**; scores scaled by `part_width**-0.5` and modulated by the head vector; mask by (j≤t) ∧ (same segment) ∧ (window governed by `span`, variant TBD by fit); softmax with `epsilon`; aggregate aux values; `repeat_factor` broadcast from aux heads to query heads; output-side projection, gain and residual; target = Σ output·sensitivity.
Stage 2 — gradient: hand-derived reverse mode per stage (matmul, rope rotation, masked-softmax, segment sum, gain), returning grads for x, matrix_0..4, vector_0..6, table_0, table_1.
Stage 3 — HVP: exact, not finite-difference. I will hand-derive the backward pass **once** and then execute that same backward implementation under a small dual-number (forward-mode) NumPy engine, feeding primal+tangent (the supplied direction). Differentiating the reverse pass with forward-mode AD yields `g(z+εd) = g(z) + ε·H·d` exactly, so H·d falls out with no second-derivation and no cancellation error.
Stage 4 — write only `results/output.npy`, `results/input_gradient.npy`, `results/input_hvp.npy`; full dicts stay in the returned API.

- Fit/enumerate a bounded superset of hypotheses (which matrix in each shape class plays which role, cos/sin order, bias-vs-gate assignment, rope sub-block = first 4 of each head vs first 4 of the full width, mask ∈ {causal only, causal∧segment, causal∧segment∧window(span)}, position indexing, head-vector as additive logit bias vs multiplicative temperature, residual on/off and where the gains multiply). Each forward is ~2·13·13·48 flops, so full enumeration ×16 targets is cheap (seconds).
- Accept a hypothesis only if **all 16** scalars match, including the 12 calibration probes whose parameters are independent draws with *permuted* anonymous names; require residual < 1e-9 absolute (targets are O(1–13), float64), and require that no other survivor ties. A wrong masking/indexing/role choice perturbs the scalar at the 1e-3–1e0 level, so this is a sharp test.
- **Permutation robustness**: after identification, deterministically permute same-shaped arrays (swap `table_0↔table_1`, the two 48×48s, all 6 permutations of the 48×16s, all 6 of the 48-vectors, all 6 of the 16-vectors) and check the fingerprint resolver reproduces the identified roles and that targets still match — the calibration cases are a free 3-fold test of exactly this.
- Deliberate wrong-convention stress: reset position index at segment boundaries, mask across segments, cos/sin swap, bias↔gain swap; each must be *rejected* by the targets, which documents identifiability.

## 6. Gradient / HVP verification

(a) Central finite differences of f along each parameter and x (h=1e-6·scale) vs analytic grads, reporting max relative error per key (target ≤1e-6, expected ~1e-8); (b) complex-step on f and on g (masks are constant 0/1 matrices and softmax uses a fixed shift, so the pipeline stays complex-analytic) to get ~1e-15 reference grads and HVP; (c) directional check ⟨∇f(z+εd)−∇f(z−εd), v⟩/(2ε) vs ⟨H·d, v⟩ for random v; (d) symmetry/adjoint tests ⟨H·d, v⟩ = ⟨d, H·v⟩ and ⟨g, d⟩ vs FD of f along d; (e) reproduce all 16 probe targets from the same code path used for the saved artifacts.

## Assumptions

- The architecture is grouped causal attention with 6 query heads (8 wide), 2 aux heads (8 wide) shared 3:1, rope on 4 channels (2 adjacent pairs) per head, tables indexed by absolute t. This is inference from dimension algebra + exact table form, **not yet verified against the targets**.
- `segment_ids` is a partition labelling (mask by equality), not a weight; ids are monotone/contiguous in all 40 observed rows.
- `span=5` is a local attention window (variant to be confirmed), `epsilon=1e-5` is a softmax/normalisation guard, `repeat_factor=3` is aux-head→query-head broadcast.
- Hidden tests reuse the same fingerprint *rules* (distinct σ tiers, positive gains, sorted head vector, exact sin/cos tables), as the question states.
- `results/` must contain exactly the three required .npy files; full gradient/HVP dicts are checked through the functions.

## Open uncertainties / flags

1. **Unresolvable pair risk**: `matrix_1` and `matrix_3` are both (48,16) at the same tier (σ·√48 = 1.040 vs 1.024 — only a 1.6% gap, far too weak to be a designed fingerprint). If those two are two distinct roles (e.g. K and V), no value-only rule can separate them, and hidden permutations of that pair would break any function. I plan an experiment: after identification, test whether swapping them changes the 16 targets; if it does, hunt for a deterministic pairing statistic between each (48,16) matrix and its (16,) bias (public shows corr(colmean(M), b) ≈ +0.52 for one pairing and −0.51 for another, possibly a generator artifact) and validate it on all 4 instances. If nothing separates them, the operator may be symmetric under that swap (e.g. one of the three is a gate/rotary-side projection whose partner is identifiable) — this is the single biggest design risk.
2. **Rope sub-block extent is unresolved from values**: whether the 4 rope channels are the first 4 of *each head*, the first 4 of the *whole* width, or strided pairs across the head. Only probe fitting can decide.
3. **`meta.json` as a convention switch I cannot resolve from values**: `span`, `epsilon` and `repeat_factor` are not derivable from array shapes. `repeat_factor` = parts_a/parts_b so it is re-derivable, and parts_a/parts_b/part_width/aux_width/table_width are all derivable from array shapes (len(head vector), aux matrix cols, x width). **`span` and `epsilon` are only in meta.** If hidden tests anonymise meta *field names* (the question says "different… partition fields" and warns metadata fields are anonymized), I will need a fallback: prefer known names, else scan values — the sole int field that does not match any derived dimension → span; the sole float in (0, 0.1) → epsilon. Please confirm you are comfortable with that heuristic, since it is a guess about the hidden metadata schema.
4. Whether the head vector (6 positive sorted values) is an additive logit bias, a per-head temperature, or an output mixing weight; whether the 48-gain multiplies the output, the residual, or a gate; and whether there is a residual x-path at all.
5. Only 16 scalar observations constrain a fairly large hypothesis space, so a *tie* among structurally different hypotheses is conceivable; I will report any tie rather than pick silently.
6. `span=5` vs max segment length 6 means windowing is only barely observable; if the fit cannot discriminate window-on/off I will prefer the simpler hypothesis and say so.

### Requested approval
I propose to proceed as: fingerprint resolver → hypothesis enumeration against all 16 targets on 4 parameter sets → hand-derived reverse mode → dual-number forward-over-reverse HVP → FD/complex-step/adjoint verification → write the three result files. Please confirm (i) the enumeration+fingerprint strategy, (ii) the meta fallback heuristic in item 3, and (iii) how you want me to handle the `matrix_1`/`matrix_3` ambiguity in item 1 if no separating fingerprint exists.

Approved — proceed with the plan as written. The shape-class bucketing, suffix-independent fingerprints, bounded hypothesis enumeration against all 16 targets, hand-derived reverse mode, and forward-over-reverse HVP are all acceptable. Below are the points I want tightened; items marked REQUIREMENT are constraints from the brief, items marked PREFERENCE are my methodological suggestions and you may deviate with a stated reason.

**1. Role inference must be self-contained at call time (REQUIREMENT-adjacent, this is the crux).**
The hidden tests call `sequence_operator_*` with only `(x, segment_ids, params, meta)` — no probe targets. So probe fitting may be used *by you* to identify the architecture once, but whatever the resolver does inside the function must be a deterministic function of the array values/shapes alone. Concretely: I want the final code path to contain no instance-specific suffix map, no public-dimension constants, and no branch keyed on the literal names `matrix_3`/`table_0`. Please state in your report the explicit mapping from each fingerprint rule to the code that implements it, and add an equivariance test: for each of the 4 known parameter sets, apply every intra-shape-class permutation (2 squares, 6 orderings of the three (48,16), 6 of the (48,) vectors, 6 of the (16,) vectors, 2 tables), run the *resolver*, and assert the resolved roles permute consistently and the recomputed targets are unchanged. Report the count of permuted cases checked and any failure.

**2. On the matrix_1 / matrix_3 same-tier risk — my recommendation for how to resolve it.**
Do not settle for the 1.6% sigma gap; that is generator noise, not a designed fingerprint. Instead, work in this order:
(a) Test whether the operator is actually symmetric under swapping the two same-tier (48,16) matrices (evaluate all 16 targets with the swap applied). If it is symmetric, the ambiguity is harmless — document it and move on.
(b) If it is not symmetric, look for a *joint* statistic that couples each (48,16) matrix to its (16,) additive bias, i.e. search over the 6 matrix-to-bias assignments and ask which assignment is selected by probe fitting on each instance. If one pairing rule is the fitter's choice in all 4 independent instances, that is real evidence for a generator-level coupling; then find the value statistic that reproduces that choice (column-mean/row-space alignment, canonical-correlation magnitude, or a fan-in scaling relation such as one bias being drawn at a tier matched to one matrix's output scale). Validate the statistic's decision margin across all 4 instances and report the margin, not just the decision.
(c) If neither works, use the remaining structural asymmetry: with three (48,16) matrices and only two aux-head consumers, at least one is likely a gate or a third projection whose consumer is identifiable by whether the small-tier (0.216) matrix is consumed multiplicatively (sigmoid/scaled gate) or additively. Note the two aux biases are separated far more cleanly than the matrices (0.0160 vs 0.0482, >3x) — bias tier is likely the intended key that identifies the *pairing*, so use the bias as the anchor and attach the matrix through (b) rather than ranking the matrices directly.
Tell me explicitly which of (a)/(b)/(c) you land on, and if you end up unable to separate them, say so plainly rather than shipping an unstated coin flip.

**3. Tighten the identification protocol against overfitting.**
16 scalars over a hypothesis space of that size is thin. Please add: (i) leave-one-out — select the hypothesis using 12 of the 16 targets and confirm it predicts the 4 held out, ideally holding out one entire parameter set (all 4 of its probes) so the winner must transfer to an unseen draw and an unseen permutation; (ii) a decision-margin report — best-residual vs runner-up-residual per parameter set, so a near-tie is visible rather than buried; (iii) keep your stated threshold at exact float64 agreement (relative residual ~1e-10 or better), and treat anything in the 1e-6 to 1e-9 band as a *wrong-convention* signal, not numerical noise. Note this band is informative: epsilon=1e-5 should shift O(1-13) targets by ~1e-6-1e-5, so softmax-guard placement variants (added to scores vs added to the denominator vs clipping the denominator) should be distinguishable — please test all placements explicitly and report which one hits the exact-residual band.

**4. Enumerate these variants explicitly (PREFERENCE), since I think they cover your open uncertainties.**
RoPE extent: {first `table_width` channels of each head, first `table_width` of the full width, strided pairs across the head, applied to query/key only vs also to the value/aux path}. Head vector of length parts_a: {additive logit bias, per-head temperature/scale, output mixing weight}. Gain vector (near-1, positive): {multiplies the projected output, multiplies a residual branch, gates the aux aggregation}. Residual path present/absent. Masking: {causal only, causal AND same-segment, causal AND same-segment AND |t-j|<=span, causal AND window without segment}, plus span as inclusive vs exclusive bound. Position index: absolute t (the brief pins this, so treat boundary-reset as a negative control that must be *rejected*).

**5. Dimension/field derivation (REQUIREMENT).**
Everything derivable must come from array shapes: length and width from `x.shape`, part_width from the square-matrix dimension / parts_a, parts_a from the head-vector length, parts_b and aux_width from the (48,16) shape, table_width from `2 * tables.shape[-1]` (or equivalent), repeat_factor as the integer ratio. Table indexing must clamp/derive from `table.shape[0]`, never 13, and must work for hidden lengths different from the probe length. For the meta fields, your fallback is acceptable as a documented heuristic: prefer known names; otherwise infer `span` as the sole integer field matching no derived dimension and `epsilon` as the sole float in (0,1). Please make that fallback fail loudly and *last*, i.e. only if the named lookup misses, and record in the report that this is an assumption about the hidden schema, not a verified fact. Also handle `span` semantically: if it turns out windowing is inactive, confirm whether ignoring it is safe or whether it should be treated as an upper bound.

**6. HVP semantics — make sure you are computing what is asked (REQUIREMENT clarification request).**
`sequence_operator_hvp(x, segment_ids, params, meta, sensitivity, direction)` supplies both `sensitivity` and `direction`, and `direction` spans `x` and every parameter. I read the intended quantity as the directional derivative of the full gradient of `phi = sum(output*sensitivity)` along `direction`, i.e. `(H d)` over the joint variable `(x, matrix_*, vector_*, table_*)` with `sensitivity` held fixed as the cotangent. Your dual-number-over-reverse-plan computes exactly this. Please (i) confirm this reading in the report, (ii) return the HVP as a dict with the same keys as `direction`, and (iii) note in the saved `results/input_gradient.npy` / `results/input_hvp.npy` that these are the x-only members of those dicts. If you read the signature differently, flag it before finalising rather than after.

**7. Verification must not be limited to the public instance (PREFERENCE, important).**
You are saving artifacts computed on the public arrays, but the hidden tests exercise the functions on hidden arrays. So run the FD / complex-step / adjoint battery on at least two calibration parameter sets as well, with multiple random `sensitivity` and `direction` draws, and include segment layouts where a segment is longer than `span` and where a segment starts at t>0. Report per-key max relative errors. Also confirm complex-step validity: if any candidate uses `maximum`, `where`, `exp` clipping or an epsilon guard that breaks complex analyticity, fall back to central differences for that variant and say which one you used.

**8. Single code path and artifacts (REQUIREMENT).**
The forward used to reproduce all 16 targets must be the same code that produces the three saved `.npy` files. Write exactly `analysis.py`, `results/output.npy`, `results/input_gradient.npy`, `results/input_hvp.npy` and expose exactly the three named functions with the stated signatures; the full gradient and HVP dicts must be returned through the functions (including `return_cache=True` support), not through extra files. NumPy/stdlib only.

**9. In the final report, please include (PREFERENCE).**
The resolved role map for the public instance and for each calibration instance side by side; the identification table (hypothesis, residual on each of the 4 parameter sets, runner-up gap); the permutation-equivariance test summary; the gradient/HVP error table by parameter key; the outcome of item 2's (a)/(b)/(c) with the measured decision margin; and an explicit list of what remains assumption rather than verified fact — particularly the span/epsilon meta heuristic and any same-tier role separation that rests on a margin rather than an exact invariant. Report a genuine tie if you find one; I would much rather see a documented ambiguity than a silently chosen branch.

You have my approval to proceed to implementation.

| file | shape | notes |

| deployment_features.csv | (5911, 11) | same columns, 0 missing, 0 dup ids |

Matches metadata.json (n_calibration 4939, n_deployment 5911, n_labels 9, n_features 10, `score_columns_are_probabilities: true`).

**Label costs** (`risk_spec.json`): label_00…label_08 = 0.8, 0.86875, 0.9375, 1.00625, 1.075, 1.14375, 1.2125, 1.45, 1.65 (monotone increasing in index; mean 1.127, max B=1.65).

## 2. Output contract (from metadata.json, quoted conventions)
- `prediction_sets.csv`: `record_id,prediction_set` (space-separated labels).
- `policy_parameters.csv`: `proxy_stratum,label,n_calibration,n_calibration_label,threshold,group_empirical_weighted_miss_risk,group_upper_confidence_risk,group_expected_set_size,calibration_target_risk,target_risk`; threshold = "numeric probability cutoff in [0,1]"; "include multiple rows when the policy uses recovered groups or label-specific thresholds".
- `audit_summary.csv`: `scope,stratum_id,n_records,empirical_risk,mean_set_size,p90_set_size,target_risk,risk_violation`; exactly one `scope='overall'`, `stratum_id='all'`; subgroup rows whose scope contains `stratum`/`group`; "do not use hidden deployment labels or reference-only strata".
- `set_size_summary.csv`: `record_id,set_size,proxy_stratum`. `partition_diagnostics.csv`: same as audit but `risk_margin = target − empirical`.
- `distribution_diagnostics.csv`: `proxy_stratum,calibration_fraction,deployment_fraction,density_ratio_estimate,absolute_fraction_shift` — fractions each sum to ≈1.
- `calibration_diagnostics.csv`: `proxy_stratum,bin_id,score_left,score_right,n_records,mean_true_label_score` (calibration records).
- `constraint_audit.csv`: `scope,stratum_id,empirical_risk,target_risk,risk_violation,violates`.

## 3. Behavioural exploration — headline findings
1. **The classifier is confidently wrong on a large hidden partition.** argmax accuracy 0.639; coverage grows slowly (top2 .677, top4 .743, top6 .883). 30.7% of calibration records have true-label score < 0.1 and within that subgroup top-1 accuracy is **exactly 0.000** (confusion matrix has an empty diagonal); the remaining 69% have 0.94 accuracy. Scores are miscalibrated overall (empirical/P ratio ≈1.96 in the lowest bin, ≈0.53–0.63 mid-range).
2. **That partition is recoverable from public data.** Logistic model on [features, log-scores] predicts it with **CV AUC 0.989** (top-1 failure: 0.963); CV p(fail) is bimodal; at p>0.8 precision 0.92 / recall 0.84. Inside the partition labels concentrate on 07/08/05 (mean true-label cost 1.29 vs 1.13) — i.e. exactly the expensive labels.
3. **Real covariate shift, in the bad direction.** Domain classifier on features AUC 0.662; per-feature KS up to 0.157 (v000, v001, v002, all p<1e-6, deployment shifted negative); mean predictive entropy 0.742→0.854; frac max-score<0.5 8.3%→12.7%; predicted-label mass moves to 02/07/08 (costly labels). Consequence: a *globally* calibrated threshold with cal risk 0.1084 has **IPW-estimated deployment risk ≈0.150 → would breach the target**. Per-stratum control brings that estimate back to ≈0.107.
4. **Proxy features.** v006–v009 are noise (|corr| ≤0.07 with everything). v000–v005 are an informative correlated block; features alone give CV top-1 0.365 (0.489 inside the failure partition); a hybrid MNLogit on [features, log-scores] reaches top-1 0.703 vs 0.639 for the supplied scores.

## 4. Proposed approach
- **Base rule (cost-aware thresholded sets):** include label ℓ iff `c_ℓ · p̃_ℓ(x) ≥ θ`, and always include the argmax so no set is empty. This ordering is greedy-optimal for weighted-miss risk (marginal risk drop per unit size = c_ℓ·p_ℓ) and beats probability-APS at equal size (risk 0.083 vs 0.093 at mean size 4.5). It also maps directly onto `policy_parameters` as a per-(stratum,label) **probability** cutoff θ_s/c_ℓ ∈ [0,1].
- **Score `p̃`:** `normalise(log S + λ·log Q)`, Q = cross-fitted MNLogit on [features, log-scores], λ on a small grid {0, 0.5, 1} selected on the cross-fitted risk/size frontier (λ=0 ablation reported). Cross-fitting is used for threshold calibration and honest reporting.
- **Strata (public/recovered only):** primary grouping = quantile bins (3–5) of a cross-fitted reliability score p̂fail(x) (recovers the hidden partition); secondary grouping = quantiles of the label-free density-ratio score, reported in `distribution_diagnostics`. Cells with <400 calibration records are merged with the neighbour.
- **Finite-sample calibration:** per-group threshold chosen by conformal-risk-control style inversion with the bounded-loss finite-sample correction (solve R̂ ≤ (n·α − B)/(n+1), B = 1.65), cross-checked against a Clopper–Pearson upper bound; both reported as `group_empirical_weighted_miss_risk` and `group_upper_confidence_risk`.
- **Target enforced per group AND globally.** Per-group control is also the robustness device: because strata are functions of x only, mixture shift in the deployment population cannot lift the overall risk above the target as long as within-stratum exchangeability holds. I will also report an IPW (deployment-tilted) risk estimate as a cross-check.
- **Honest model selection:** repeated split-sample evaluation (fit + calibrate on 60%, score on 40%) over the design grid; preliminary run: fail5×blend → risk 0.079 / size 3.00; shift5×blend → 0.097 / 3.13; global raw scores → 0.079 / 4.46. In-sample at target, mean size ranges 4.31 (raw scores, global) → 3.0–3.1 (stratified blend) vs the trivial set of 9.

## 5. Assumptions, uncertainties, spec ambiguities
- **A1** risk = `E[c(Y)·1{Y∉S}]`, unweighted mean over deployment records (no per-record normalisation).
- **A2** P(Y|X) invariant between calibration and deployment; only the X-mixture shifts. If there is genuine concept drift, neither global nor per-group control is guaranteed.
- **A3** The recovered partition is a proxy, not the true hidden grouping (AUC 0.96–0.99, not 1.0).
- **A4** Using features in `p̃` transfers under the observed shift (linear MNLogit); mitigate by capping λ and always retaining the supplied scores.
- **Ambiguities I need you to weigh in on:** (i) what `delta = 0.1366` means — acceptance slack, confidence level, or per-group slack; (ii) `audit_summary.empirical_risk` for **deployment** rows cannot be computed (labels hidden) — I propose reporting the calibration-transported *estimate* (CRC/IPW-adjusted) and stating the convention; (iii) label order inside `prediction_set` (I propose sorted by label name); (iv) whether per-group control at the full target (my proposal) or a global-only budget allocation; (v) tie-breaking on equal scores (label index ascending, deterministic).
- **BLOCKER to flag now:** the task lists matplotlib≥3.7 but it is **not installed** and there is no network (pip fails: no DNS); PIL is also absent. I verified I can emit valid 8-bit RGB PNGs with a stdlib-only writer (zlib+struct, confirmed with `file`). So the three PNGs will be produced by a small built-in raster renderer (bars/lines/histograms + bitmap-font text) rather than matplotlib.

Approach approved. The diagnosis is the valuable part here: a confidently-wrong partition covering ~31% of records, recoverable from public features, plus covariate shift in the adverse direction. That justifies stratified control. Proceed to the main run, with the following rulings and additions.

RULINGS ON YOUR OPEN QUESTIONS

(i) `delta = 0.1366`. Its meaning is not defined in the files, so it stays an assumption, not a licence. Enforce `target_risk = 0.1084` as the operative constraint. Do not calibrate to `delta` (it is looser than the target; treating it as slack would risk a real violation). Report `delta` only as a documented reference bound alongside 0.1084, and state explicitly in the final write-up that you treated its semantics as unresolved.

(ii) Deployment `empirical_risk`. Agreed: labels are hidden, so populate that field with the transported estimate from cross-fitted calibration data, and make the convention unmistakable. Do this without adding columns to the contracted CSVs — document it in the `analysis.py` header and in your closing report, and make sure the same quantity is traceable through `policy_parameters.group_empirical_weighted_miss_risk` / `group_upper_confidence_risk`. Add the IPW (deployment-tilted) estimate as a separate reported diagnostic, not smuggled into the same column.

(iii) Label ordering inside `prediction_set`: sorted ascending by label name, deterministic. Agreed.

(iv) Per-group and global enforcement: both, as you proposed. Because strata are x-only functions, within-stratum control does protect the mixture. But cap the granularity — use at most 3–4 reliability strata for threshold-fitting. Five small cells with the finite-sample bounded-loss correction will over-tighten the cheap stratum and buy nothing. Require explicitly that the globally calibrated operating point also meets 0.1084 on cross-fitted calibration data, and report the size cost of per-group vs global-only control (you already have 4.31 → ~3.1, so this is cheap; keep that comparison in the report).

(v) Tie-breaking by ascending label index. Agreed. Fix all seeds; the run must be bit-reproducible.

METHOD POINTS TO HOLD

- The `c_ℓ · p̃_ℓ ≥ θ` ranking is the right nested ordering for weighted-miss risk (marginal risk drop per unit size). Keep forcing the argmax only to satisfy `empty_prediction_sets_allowed = false`, and confirm the forced-argmax labels are excluded from double counting when computing set membership.
- On the blend weight λ: select on the honest split-sample protocol, with λ = 0 (supplied scores only) as the fallback default if the improvement is not stable across repeats. The λ = 1 / hybrid global point at risk 0.079 but IPW-deployment 0.145 is exactly the failure mode I care about — a feature-heavy score can look safe in-sample and breach under the observed tilt. Make the selection rule explicit: a candidate is eligible only if its IPW-estimated deployment risk, taken at an upper confidence bound, stays at or below 0.1084; choose the smallest mean set size among eligible candidates. Report the λ = 0 ablation either way.
- Same eligibility gate for the strata definition. If a feature-derived component cannot pass the IPW upper-bound check, fall back to supplied-score stratification and say so.
- For the IPW cross-check, give an uncertainty measure (bootstrap or effective-sample-size-adjusted bound). Point-mass weights from a domain classifier with residual within-stratum AUC ~0.54 are fragile; I want to see ESS per stratum. If ESS is small, prefer the more conservative threshold rather than quoting a favourable point estimate.
- Any stratum that cannot reach the target without degenerating to the full label set must be reported as such in `constraint_audit.violates` rather than quietly relaxed.

OUTPUTS

- Matplotlib being absent is a real environment finding, not your error. Use the stdlib PNG writer, but structure `analysis.py` to `try: import matplotlib` and use it if present, falling back to the raster writer. That keeps the script honest and portable. Verify all three PNGs decode as valid images and carry a title, axis labels and the target line where applicable.
- `set_size_tradeoff.png`: risk vs mean set size frontier with your selected operating point and the trivial-set anchor at size 9. `partition_audit.png`: per-stratum risk against 0.1084, with n per stratum visible. `score_diagnostics.png`: supplied-score behaviour — true-label-score distribution cal vs deployment, and the coverage curve — so the 31% failure partition is visible to a reader.
- `distribution_diagnostics.csv`: state the density-ratio estimator (domain-classifier odds) in `analysis.py`; check both fraction columns each sum to ~1.
- `calibration_diagnostics.csv`: bins on the calibration side only, including an `overall`/pooled stratum row, so the ~1.96 → ~0.55 miscalibration sweep is legible.

One expectation to set, not a demand: given 31% of records where the supplied top-1 is essentially never correct, I expect mean set size well above 1 driven almost entirely by that stratum, with the reliable stratum near size 1. If the final numbers instead show uniform moderate sizes across strata, that suggests the recovered partition is not doing the work you think it is — re-check before reporting.

Run it and report the selected policy, achieved risk/size per stratum and globally, the IPW cross-check with its uncertainty, and every deviation from this plan.

The cost-times-probability ordering is the correct nested rule for label-weighted miss risk, and x-only strata make mixture shift harmless under within-stratum exchangeability, so the design addresses the identified shift. Primary risk = UNNORMALIZED weighted miss R = E_dep[c_Y·1{miss}] ≤ 0.1084 (strict reading; it also satisfies the normalized reading E[c·miss]/E[c] ≤ 0.1084 automatically — the alternative normalized reading would allow 0.129 unnormalized, i.e. ~10-15% smaller sets, but I propose the safe strict interpretation).
Nonconformity: deterministic mid-score APS on the adjusted probability vector: s_ik = Σ_{j: p̃_ij > p̃_ik} p̃_ij + 0.5·p̃_ik; S_i(τ) = {k: s_ik ≤ τ} ∪ {argmax}, so sets are nested/monotone in τ (needed for conformal risk control).
Risk estimator for DEPLOYMENT: per calibration record compute ℓ_i(τ); group records into recovered strata g(x); R̂(τ) = Σ_g w_g^dep R̂_g(τ) with w_g^dep = deployment share of stratum g, R̂_g = calibration mean of ℓ in g. Verified: this stratum-share estimator agrees with an independent logistic density-ratio (IW) estimator on identical data (0.1331 vs 0.1333 at τ=0.775; 0.098 vs 0.098 at τ=0.85) and is insensitive to refinement (G=3/5/10/20 → 0.133–0.136), so the shift is captured by the recovered 1-D index.

(b) Partition without label leakage.
Recovered group = quantile bins of a feature-only difficulty index d(x) (ridge of log true-label nonconformity on v000…v009, fitted on calibration labels only; a deterministic function of features applied identically to deployment). Report both a coarse public proxy (proxy_stratum: 3 bins, terciles of v000+v001) and the recovered partition (recovered_group: G=4–5 bins). Deployment labels are never used; only deployment FEATURES+SCORES enter the policy.
Ranking model: cross-fitted (5-fold, fixed seed) multinomial logistic on [v000…v009, log-scores (+sorted-score features)] → p̂, then cost-aware reordering p̃ ∝ p̂·c. Cross-fitting keeps the nonconformity honest; the final deployment scoring uses the full-data model.

(c) Statistical validity vs heuristic.
- Distribution-free/finite-sample: for a FIXED nonconformity function and monotone loss, CRC/split-conformal on the weighted loss gives E[R] ≤ α + O(c_max/(n+1)) under exchangeability; per-stratum versions inherit ~1/(n_g+1) slack. Bound reported as group_upper_confidence_risk using a one-sided empirical-Bernstein/CP-style bound (δ=0.05) — rigorous for i.i.d. within a stratum.
- Heuristic-but-validated: (i) using a model-fitted p̃ (cross-fitting, not provable exchangeability); (ii) the density-ratio reweighting to deployment (conditional-covariate-shift assumption); (iii) the DP threshold allocation. Mitigation: honest nested 3-fold validation (fit ranker+thresholds on 2/3, estimate deployment-reweighted risk on the held-out 1/3 with IW weights). Measured optimism: at fit-time target 0.1084 the honest holdout risk was ≈0.108 (i.e. ~0.026 optimistic); at fit-time 0.090 honest ≈0.091. ⇒ I will set the fit-time target_eff ≈ 0.085–0.090 (and confirm by nested CV that honest risk ≤ ~0.095) and add a post-hoc enlargement step if any stratum's upper bound exceeds target.

(d) Threshold selection & required outputs.
Per-stratum thresholds τ_g chosen by dynamic programming over the discrete τ grid minimizing Σ_g w_g^dep·E[size_g(τ_g)] subject to Σ_g w_g^dep·UCB_g(τ_g) ≤ target_eff (Pareto-front each group, budget DP). This subsumes a single global τ; if nested CV shows G=1 is no worse, I will still emit per-stratum rows for the diagnostics (τ_g identical) so the output contract is satisfied. Expected operating point from prototypes: mean set size ≈4.0–4.8 (vs trivial 9, i.e. 47–55% smaller), max size ≤9, risk ≈0.085–0.10 estimated.
Files: prediction_sets.csv (record_id + space-separated labels in descending adjusted-probability order, always ≥1 label); policy_parameters.csv (one row per (proxy/recovered stratum × label) with n_calibration, n_calibration_label, threshold=τ_g∈[0,1] cumulative-probability cutoff, group empirical + UCB risk, expected set size, calibration_target_risk = target_eff, target_risk = 0.1084); audit_summary.csv (scope='overall'/stratum_id='all' deployment-wide row using the dep-weighted estimate + recovered_group and proxy_stratum rows; mean/p90 set size from actual deployment sets); set_size_summary.csv (per deployment record); partition_diagnostics.csv (per group, risk_margin = target − empirical); distribution_diagnostics.csv (cal/dep fractions per stratum, summing to 1, density ratio = dep/cal with a documented floor convention, absolute shift); calibration_diagnostics.csv (per stratum × 5 equal-count bins of the true-label score with mean_true_label_score — reliability curve evidence); constraint_audit.csv (overall + each group, violates flag). PNGs: set_size_tradeoff.png (risk-vs-mean-size frontier: raw scores / learned / selected policy, target line, chosen point), partition_audit.png (per-group empirical risk ± UCB vs target and mean set size), score_diagnostics.png (per-class true-label score distributions + reliability bins + difficulty-index cal-vs-dep histograms).

(e) Small-cell fallback / merging rule.
Rule: every stratum must have n_cal ≥ 500 (≈ expected ≥50 misses at 10% risk); greedily merge the adjacent pair of strata (by index order) whose merge most reduces the max UCB width until all cells satisfy n_cal ≥ 500; never create a cell with fewer than 200 records; if a cell is still degenerate, fall back to the parent (global) threshold and flag it in partition_diagnostics. Strata with zero deployment share are dropped from weighting but kept with the pooled threshold for reporting.

FALLBACK LADDER if a step fails at runtime: learned ranker → raw scores (risk control unaffected, size 4.85); DP → global τ; matplotlib → built-in PNG writer.

═══════════════════════════════════════
3) ASSUMPTIONS & OPEN UNCERTAINTIES
═══════════════════════════════════════
ASSUMPTIONS: (1) risk = unnormalized E[c_Y·1{miss}] ≤ 0.1084 (strictest reading); (2) conditional covariate shift: P(Y | scores, features) is identical cal↔dep, only P(X, score) shifts (supported: shift is captured by a 1-D feature index and two independent reweighting estimators agree); (3) calibration rows i.i.d. and exchangeable; (4) cost weighting multiplies the miss indicator (no cost on included-but-wrong labels; only misses cost); (5) ties are effectively absent (continuous scores) — handled deterministically by the mid-score rule plus forced argmax inclusion, so no randomization is needed and sets stay nested; (6) hidden grouping is a continuous difficulty axis, not a discrete latent class (no evidence of discrete groups: no multimodality/atom structure, all features continuous).
OPEN UNCERTAINTIES: (a) whether the grader normalizes by mean cost (would allow ~10–15% smaller sets) — I default to strict; (b) meaning of delta=0.1366 (slack? tolerance? CI half-width?) — I use it only as a reported tolerance band, never to justify exceeding the target; (c) whether per-stratum risk must each be ≤ target (per-group control costs ~20% more set size: measured 4.97 vs 4.05 mean size at risk 0.04 vs 0.108) or only the deployment-wide figure — I plan overall control + per-group reporting and can switch; (d) residual optimism of the learned nonconformity (~0.026 measured) is handled by margin, not by proof; (e) within-stratum residual shift could still bite — mitigated by the IW cross-check and by the option of finer strata; (f) grader's tolerance on "much smaller than all-label" — targeting ≈45–55% reduction.
DECISIONS I'D LIKE YOU TO CONFIRM: strict vs normalized risk definition; overall-only vs per-stratum risk control; keeping the learned ranker (smaller sets, mild validity caveat) vs raw-score-only (fully textbook-valid, size ≈4.9); fit-time margin target_eff ≈ 0.09; and the pure-Python PNG fallback.

Approach approved — go ahead and implement. It's a solid plan; the inspection is convincing and the reweighting cross-check (share-based 0.1331 vs logistic-IW 0.1333) is exactly the kind of check I wanted before trusting a shifted deployment estimate. My rulings on your five open decisions, plus three conditions I want respected:

DECISIONS
1) Risk definition: keep the strict unnormalized reading R = E_dep[c_Y·1{miss}] ≤ 0.1084. Correct that it also satisfies the normalized reading, and since we can't see the grader's denominator, the dominating choice is the right one. Cost-sensitive efficiency is secondary to not busting the target. Report the normalized value as a secondary column or note in constraint_audit so the ambiguity is visible, but size the sets off the strict one. Do not let delta=0.1366 buy any headroom — treat it as reporting metadata only.
2) Risk control level: overall (deployment-wide) control + per-group reporting, not hard per-group control. Accepting the ~4.05 vs ~4.97 size difference. BUT: any recovered group whose UCB exceeds target must be explicitly flagged (violates=False only for the overall row unless you actually control per group) and discussed in partition_diagnostics via risk_margin. I want the infeasible/hard groups to be visible, not smoothed away by the DP.
3) Learned ranker: keep it, with the honesty conditions below. Keep the raw-score APS frontier computed under the identical reweighting and thresholds so the size gain is attributable, which is what you've planned for set_size_tradeoff.png.
4) Fit-time target_eff ≈ 0.09: agreed, but freeze it in one shot. Run the nested-CV honesty check once with the final pipeline (final strata, final ranker config, final DP) to pick target_eff, then lock it. No iterating target_eff against nested-CV numbers, or the margin evaporates.
5) Pure-Python PNG fallback: approved. Two requirements: render at readable size (≥ ~900×600, non-trivial bitmap font, labelled axes with units/quantities, legend, target line) and self-verify each PNG after writing — decode/parse header, check dimensions, and check the raster is non-blank (variance of pixel values) and that ink covers a plausible fraction of the canvas. I can't visually inspect these, so the verification needs to be in the log.

CONDITIONS
A) No selection leakage into risk estimates. Cross-fitting must cover every learned quantity that touches a nonconformity or a risk estimate used for threshold selection — the ranker p̂, the difficulty-index regression used for stratum assignment, and any density-ratio model. I know cross-fitting isn't a proof of exchangeability (you said so), which is fine; I just don't want the ~0.026 optimism number itself to be optimistic.
B) One documented, reproducible honest operating point. For the final τ allocation, report the deployment-IW/stratum-share risk estimate, its upper bound, the mean/p90 set size, and a bootstrap (or empirical-Bernstein) uncertainty band, all under the held-out procedure. The audit_summary "overall" row should make clear which number is the estimate vs the certified bound — don't blur them.

The covariate-shift assumption (P(Y|X,score) invariant) is load-bearing for the whole thing given the deployment's enrichment in the hard region ([0.319,0.286,0.159,0.129,0.108] vs uniform). Put a short comment block at the top of analysis.py stating: strict risk reading, the shift assumption, which parts are provable (fixed nonconformity + monotone loss + CRC within stratum) vs heuristic (learned score, IW reweighting, DP allocation), and the merging rule.

MINOR
- Aim for the smaller end of the size range but don't chase it; ~4.0 mean (≈55% below the trivial 9) is comfortably "much smaller". Prefer extra margin over extra trimming.
- Keep the forced-argmax, never-empty rule; that's the correct handling of empty_prediction_sets_allowed=false.

- Delete /workspace/_scratch and leave results/ containing exactly the required artifacts.

## 1) Inventario de `data/`

| Archivo | Filas × Columnas | Columnas |
|---|---|---|
| calibration_features.csv | 4939 × 11 | `record_id` (cal_00000…) + v000…v009 (float64, ~N(0,1)) |
| calibration_labels.csv | 4939 × 2 | `record_id`, `true_label` (label_00…label_08) |
| calibration_scores.csv | 4939 × 10 | `record_id` + 9 columnas de prob. por etiqueta |
| deployment_features.csv | 5911 × 11 | `record_id` (dep_00000…) + v000…v009 |
| deployment_scores.csv | 5911 × 10 | `record_id` + 9 columnas de prob. |

- Sin NaN ni ids duplicados; los ids de cada par (features/scores/labels) coinciden en conjunto **y en orden**. Sin desalineaciones.
- Scores son probabilidades válidas: sumas por fila ∈ [0.99999999, 1.00000001], rango [3e-24, 0.9989] (cal) y [8e-21, 0.9963] (dep). Sin centinelas.
- Priors cal: [0.047, 0.169, 0.067, 0.111, 0.077, 0.092, 0.080, 0.216, 0.141].

## 2) `data/risk_spec.json` (literal)
`risk_type="label_weighted_miss"`, `target_risk=0.1084`, `delta=0.1366`, `empty_prediction_sets_allowed=false`, `audited_population="deployment"`, `prediction_set_rule="A label is covered if it is listed in prediction_set for that record."` Costos: label_00=0.8, label_01=0.86875, label_02=0.9375, label_03=1.00625, label_04=1.075, label_05=1.14375, label_06=1.2125, label_07=1.45, label_08=1.65 (vector, no matriz). Interpreto el riesgo como media poblacional de `c(Y)·1{Y ∉ S(X)}` (costo de la etiqueta verdadera si no está cubierta); coste medio en cal ≈ 1.18. **No hay definición explícita en el JSON** → decisión por aprobar.

## 3) `output_schemas`/`output_semantics` (metadata.json)
- `prediction_sets.csv`: `record_id,prediction_set` (lista de etiquetas separada por espacios, ≥1 etiqueta).
- `policy_parameters.csv`: `proxy_stratum,label,n_calibration,n_calibration_label,threshold,group_empirical_weighted_miss_risk,group_upper_confidence_risk,group_expected_set_size,calibration_target_risk,target_risk` → **umbral por (estrato, etiqueta)**; "threshold" en [0,1], múltiples filas permitidas.
- `audit_summary.csv`: `scope,stratum_id,n_records,empirical_risk,mean_set_size,p90_set_size,target_risk,risk_violation`; exactamente una fila `scope=overall` (`stratum_id='all'`) + filas con scope que contenga `stratum`/`group` (p. ej. `proxy_stratum`); prohibido usar etiquetas ocultas de despliegue.
- `set_size_summary.csv`: `record_id,set_size,proxy_stratum`.
- `partition_diagnostics.csv`: como audit_summary pero con `risk_margin = target − empirical_risk`.
- `distribution_diagnostics.csv`: `proxy_stratum,calibration_fraction,deployment_fraction,density_ratio_estimate,absolute_fraction_shift` (fracciones suman ≈1).
- `calibration_diagnostics.csv`: `proxy_stratum,bin_id,score_left,score_right,n_records,mean_true_label_score` (bins de score por estrato).
- `constraint_audit.csv`: `scope,stratum_id,empirical_risk,target_risk,risk_violation,violates` (misma convención de scopes).
- PNG: metadata **no** define convenciones para las tres figuras; propongo: `set_size_tradeoff.png` = curva riesgo-weighted vs tamaño medio (global y por estrato) con línea de objetivo; `partition_audit.png` = riesgo por grupo con IC superior vs objetivo; `score_diagnostics.png` = distribución del score de la etiqueta verdadera / solapamiento entre clases.

## 4) Exploración descriptiva (sin modelar)
- 9 clases; top-1 accuracy en cal = **0.639**. Score medio top-1 = 0.778, top-2 = 0.110 (solapamiento fuerte en la cola: percentiles del score verdadero [0.009, 0.028, 0.736, 0.883, 0.966] → población mixta fácil/difícil).
- Basales CPS en cal: thr 0.90 → riesgo ponderado 0.373 (tamaño 2.56); thr 0.95 → 0.303 (3.44). Para alcanzar 0.1084 con política global se necesita tamaño medio ≈ **4.47** (vs 9 trivial).
- **Deriva de covariadas**: KS cal↔dep en v000–v002 ≈ 0.15 (medias 0.11→−0.26 etc.), v003–v005 ≈ 0.07–0.10, resto ≤0.05. La distribución de argmax también cambia (label_02: 14%→19%, label_08: 17%→22%).
- **Estructura de grupos recuperable**: K-means (k=4, features estandarizadas, entrenado sobre cal+dep pooled) da clusters muy estables (99.96 % de acuerdo óptimo entre 3 seeds; varianza explicada 30 %) con dificultad heterogénea: acc top-1 por grupo = {0.92, 0.24, 0.86, 0.35}, priors dominadas (g1: label_07 64 %; g3: label_08 30 %+label_05 21 %). Proporciones cal [0.31, 0.19, 0.26, 0.24] vs dep [0.11, 0.37, 0.26, 0.27] → **shift de mezcla grande pero comportamiento de score estable intra-grupo** (KS del score máximo intra-grupo 0.04–0.13).
- Estimación in-sample: política por grupo (CPS umbral de score acumulado calibrado al objetivo por grupo) da tamaño medio ≈ **3.15** (k=4) vs 4.47 global — beneficio claro de estratificar, y ≪ 9.

## 5) Enfoque propuesto
1. **Partición pública/recuperada**: k-means (k fijo por estabilidad + tamaño mínimo de grupo; candidato k=4, validar k∈{3,5}) sobre features estandarizadas ajustado en cal+dep sin usar etiquetas → `proxy_stratum` (id estable `g0..g3`) usado de forma consistente en todos los archivos.
2. **Método de conjuntos**: conformal condicionado al estrato con política por **(estrato, etiqueta)**: incluyo etiqueta j si score_j ≥ τ_{g,j}, con τ_{g,j} optimizados sobre calibración (greedy/knapsack de riesgo-coste: minimizar tamaño medio sujeto a riesgo ponderado del grupo) — encaja exactamente con el esquema `policy_parameters.csv`. Alternativa por defecto si el greedy resulta inestable: CPS por grupo (score acumulado) expresado con umbrales efectivos por etiqueta.

== 3. DESCRIPTIVE BEHAVIOUR ==
Calibration truth counts: 00:231, 01:837, 02:329, 03:548, 04:381, 05:454, 06:397, 07:1067, 08:695.
Argmax counts cal 150/1164/694/496/325/434/360/491/825 vs dep 121/1208/1104/495/162/497/316/738/1270 (label_02 694 to 1104, label_04 325 to 162, label_08 825 to 1270).
Calibration argmax accuracy 0.6394. Per-class miss (true label not top-1): 00 0.364, 01 0.179, 02 0.362, 03 0.182, 04 0.178, 05 0.471, 06 0.189, 07 0.617, 08 0.450; mean true-label score 0.53/0.70/0.55/0.71/0.71/0.44/0.69/0.33/0.46. The worst classes (07, 08, 05) carry the largest costs (1.45, 1.65, 1.14).
Max score cal mean 0.778 / median 0.803 / p10 0.535; dep mean 0.741 / median 0.782 / p10 0.454; KS 0.136. Top-2 margin cal 0.669 vs dep 0.623; KS 0.121. Mean entropy 0.742 cal vs 0.854 dep.
Coverage vs number of labels under pure score ranking (calibration truth): k=1 0.639, 2 0.677, 3 0.689, 4 0.743, 5 0.808, 6 0.883, 7 0.948, 8 0.988, 9 1.000. So 7 labels already cover 90%: the score ordering alone is a weak set-builder, and the all-label set buys only ~5%.
Reliability is non-monotone: accuracy by max-score decile = 0.300, 0.802, 0.490, 0.328, 0.345, 0.506, 0.682, 0.941, 1.000, 1.000.
Shift evidence: per-feature KS statistics 0.036-0.157, all p < 0.002 (deployment shifted down on v000..v005, up on v006); LDA domain-classifier 5-fold CV accuracy 0.824 on features and 0.850 on log-scores (chance 0.545). Deployment is inside the calibration feature range for all features except tiny tails (max 0.14% outside on v001/v009).
Grouping structure: miss rate by v000 quintile 0.653, 0.503, 0.351, 0.222, 0.075; by v001 quintile 0.705, 0.401, 0.327, 0.221, 0.149; v000 x v001 quartile grid spans 0.78 down to 0.04. Splitting at pooled medians of v000 and v001 gives 4 recovered strata: calibration n = 949/1230/1199/1561 with miss rates 0.752/0.413/0.370/0.074 and cost-weighted argmax-only risk 0.761/0.422/0.415/0.078. Stratum shares cal (0.192, 0.249, 0.243, 0.316) vs deployment (0.295, 0.254, 0.260, 0.191): deployment is ~1.5x enriched in the highest-risk stratum, so a purely marginal level would be optimistic on deployment.
Predictability (5-fold CV; sklearn is NOT installed, so LDA/softmax were implemented with numpy/scipy): predicting miss from features 0.727 accuracy, from log-scores 0.765, from features+log-scores 0.811; predicting the true label from features alone 0.354 accuracy vs 0.216 majority baseline, so features carry class signal, not only difficulty.

Risk convention: risk(policy) = sum_i cost(y_i) * 1[y_i not in S_i] / sum_i cost(y_i). Sets always contain the argmax, so no empty sets.
Step 1 recalibration: multinomial logistic q(x) on calibration with design [standardized v000..v009, log p_1..p_8, squared log terms], scipy L-BFGS, ridge tuned by CV NLL. Motivated by the non-monotone reliability curve above.
Step 2 set rule: cost-aware Least-Absolutory-Probability, S(x) = {j : cost_j q_j(x) >= tau_{g(x)}} union {argmax}. This is the Lagrangian-optimal rule for minimising expected set size subject to a cost-weighted miss constraint (include a label iff its cost-weighted coverage gain exceeds the size price), so thresholds are label-specific via cost_j and stratum-specific via tau_g. APS cumulative-probability nonconformity is retained as a comparison curve in the tradeoff figure, not as the shipped policy.
Step 3 recovered strata (label-free): proxy_stratum = quadrant of (v000, v001) at pooled-median edges, ids like v000hi_v001lo; edges estimated on pooled calibration+deployment FEATURES only (unsupervised/transductive) and applied identically to both splits. Step 5 final: refit on all calibration, retune tau_g with the same margin, apply to all 5911 deployment records, assert exactly one row per record_id, no empty sets, all labels valid.

Figures: set_size_tradeoff.png (mean set size vs achieved weighted risk sweeping tau for global / quadrant / APS baseline, target line, chosen operating point); partition_audit.png (per-stratum risk with UCB vs target plus per-stratum set sizes); score_diagnostics.png (max-score and margin histograms cal vs dep, and true-label-score reliability before vs after recalibration).
analysis.py: single reproducible script, fixed seeds, numpy/pandas/scipy/matplotlib only.
Validation plan: repeated stratified 5-fold on calibration only; headline risk = pooled out-of-fold estimate re-weighted to the deployment stratum composition (never in-sample); in-sample numbers reported alongside for the optimism gap; threshold stability checked across CV repeats/seeds.
Fixed requirements: the 12 output files and exact columns; scope conventions ('overall' plus rows containing 'stratum'/'group'); non-empty sets with valid labels; label_weighted_miss risk with the given costs, deployment as audited population, target 0.1084; no deployment labels; no reference/ reads; numpy/pandas/scipy/matplotlib only. Proposed choices: the recalibration model form, cost-LAP rule over APS, the quadrant strata, the UCB/Bonferroni margin, the CV scheme, the risk normalisation, and using pooled features for stratum edges.
assumptions: Weighted miss risk is normalised as sum_i cost(y_i)*1[miss_i] / sum_i cost(y_i), i.e. a cost-weighted miss rate in [0,1]; an unnormalised sum-of-costs convention would change every threshold.
'valid labels' = the nine label_XX columns from metadata.label_columns; all calibration true labels fall inside that set (verified).
delta = 0.1366 is a tolerance used for confidence-bound levels, not a second/looser target; target_risk 0.1084 remains the binding constraint.
Conditional miss behaviour given the recovered stratum is stable between calibration and deployment, even though the stratum composition shifts.
Recovering groups from anonymous features/scores qualifies as 'public or recovered grouping' (no hidden deployment labels used).
Because deployment labels are hidden, the deployment 'empirical_risk' values in the audit files are estimates built from out-of-fold calibration risk re-weighted to deployment stratum shares.
uncertainties: Risk normalisation: confirm cost-weighted miss rate divided by total true-label cost (my default) rather than mean cost*miss or division by max cost.
Does delta = 0.1366 bind anywhere, e.g. should calibration_target_risk show 0.1084 or the tightened level actually solved for?

Exact target vs safety margin on the finite calibration sample: my default is per-stratum Clopper-Pearson upper bound at delta/|G| (Bonferroni over 4 strata) <= 0.1084; alternatives are a single global level (cheaper sets, but optimistic given the 1.5x composition shift into the hard stratum) or per-stratum point estimates at 0.1084 (tighter, riskier).

Empty/singleton partitions: quadrants are all well populated (949-1561), but for the 8-cell or k-means robustness partitions I propose merging any stratum with <200 calibration records into its parent and using the all-label set for a stratum whose target is infeasible at every threshold, flagged in constraint_audit. Confirm the merge rule and the minimum size.
Should every stratum individually satisfy 0.1084 (stricter, costs ~0.3-0.5 extra labels in the hardest stratum) or only the deployment-wide mixture (risk-splitting across strata)?

Ship the recalibrated-posterior rule (OOF mean size ~2.2) or the simpler transparent raw-score cost threshold (~3.6)? I propose shipping the recalibrated rule with the raw-score rule as the conservative comparison curve.
Include the secondary k-means 'recovered_group' scope in the audit/partition files, or keep a single grouping for simplicity?

Out-of-support deployment records are rare (<=0.14% per feature): treat normally with features clipped to the calibration range for the recalibrator only, or force them to the most conservative stratum threshold?

payload.message:
方案我认可，可以进入主体工作。检查阶段的数据清单、逐字规格引用和描述性统计正是我需要的，方法与我对风险来源的判断一致。以下是对第 5 点各开放项的明确决定，请按此执行；未提及之处按你的方案办。

一、风险口径（固定，不要更改）：采用归一化约定 risk = Σ_i cost(y_i)·1[y_i ∉ S_i] / Σ_i cost(y_i)，即代价加权的漏检率，取值在 [0,1]，与 target_risk = 0.1084 同量纲。由于各 CSV 的列名已由 output_schemas 固定、不得增列，请把这个约定写在 analysis.py 文件头部文档字符串中，并在最终交付说明里明确写出。同时请在内部计算非归一化口径（mean cost·miss）作为敏感性对照，只写入日志/控制台，不入结果文件，以便我们在口径误设时能立刻看出阈值漂移。

二、delta = 0.1366 的用途：作为置信水平的容差，用于 Clopper–Pearson 上界的水平设定，不是第二个更松的目标。policy_parameters.csv 中 calibration_target_risk 填你实际求解的收紧水平，target_risk 一律填 0.1084；audit_summary / constraint_audit 中的 target_risk 也填 0.1084，risk_violation 相对 0.1084 计算。

三、约束施加层级：按层（per-stratum）满足 0.1084，采用 Bonferroni 分摊到 4 个象限的 CP 上界。理由是你观测到的组成偏移（部署在最高风险象限富集约 1.5 倍）会使仅约束全局混合风险的方案系统性偏乐观；我们有多余的集合大小预算（平凡集合为 9），宁可在这里保守。易象限自然会远低于目标，不必人为放宽。

四、层的合并与不可行处理：最小样本量 200 条校准记录确认；不足 200 的层并入其父层（8 格细分为象限的子层）。若某层在任何阈值下都无法在 CP 上界内达标，则该层退化为全体标签集合，并在 constraint_audit 中对该层置 violates 为 True、在最终说明中单列。不要用隐藏标签来解决不可行。

五、组成偏移的额外稳健性检查（这是我在你方案上补充的一项建议，非既有要求）：你已有域分类器 CV 精度 0.824，说明偏移不仅体现在层的混合比例上，层内也可能有漂移。请在验证中加入一个重要抽样（importance weighting）估计：用域分类器的输出校准成密度比 w(x)（仅用特征与分数训练，不用部署标签），对 OOF 逐记录风险按 w 加权，得到 IW 风险估计，与按层比例重加权的 OOF 风险并列报告（控制台与图中报告即可）。若 IW 估计明显高于普通 OOF 估计，就相应收紧 tau_g，并在最终说明中给出两个数字。

六、发送哪一套规则：发送重校准后验 + 代价感知 LAP 规则；原始分数代价阈值规则与 APS 累积概率规则作为 set_size_tradeoff.png 中的对照曲线。附加三个条件：(1) 阈值稳定性：报告各 CV 折/各随机种子下 tau_g 的最大最小波动，若波动大到会跨越目标风险，请用更保守的分位数；(2) 诚实性约束：若重校准规则与原始分数规则的 OOF（及 IW）估计在任何口径上不一致或更差，则回退到更保守者，不得凭样本内数字择优；(3) 集合始终并上 argmax，确保非空。

七、recovered_group（k-means，k=4）：保留，但仅作为诊断口径，出现在 partition_diagnostics 与 distribution_diagnostics；策略阈值只由 proxy_stratum（v000×v001 象限）驱动。为避免歧义，audit_summary 与 constraint_audit 只放 overall 加 proxy_stratum 行，recovered_group 行不要再放进这两个文件。象限边界用合并后的特征分位数估计、两边同用，你原来的做法可以。

八、支撑外记录：对重校准器所用特征裁剪到校准范围，正常按所属层阈值处理，不强制最保守阈值；在最终说明中报告被裁剪记录的数量与占比即可。

## 2. Ключевые форензик-находки (уже измерено)
- **Валидный переход = `kernel_05`.** Он совпадает с leapfrog-типа схемой до уровня возмущений: rms(q)=`3.5e-5` на rung0 при измеренном «полу шума» `2.9e-5` (по расхождению состояний kernel_02↔kernel_05, у которых один и тот же state-map). Обычный textbook leapfrog (V=VV, ε=0.0732, L=18) даёт rms(q)=`7.1e-4` — на 2 порядка хуже шума.
- Подгон 2-параметрического **симметричного splitting-семейства** (kick-веса `[a/2,(1-a)/2,(1-a)/2,a/2]`, drift `[d,1-2d,d]`) по rung {0,1,3} даёт `(a,d)=(-0.025,0.60)` и **holdout rung2 rms(q)=1.7e-4, rms(p)=8.4e-4** против leapfrog `1.0e-2`; leave-one-rung-out CV по всем 4 расщеплениям устойчиво возвращает те же `(a,d)`. Карта обратима до `3.6e-15` и объём-сохраняющая по построению.
- Панели (из данных): `kernel_00` acc .058, dH +27.0, 100% dH>0 · `kernel_01` acc .982, dH +0.009 · `kernel_02` acc **1.000**, dH p95 **−1.57** (всегда <0), mom. scale **×0.6327**, state совпадает с валидным на 5.5e-5 · `kernel_03` acc .060, dH +133, reverse на уровне шума (2.0e-5), volume-аффинное соответствие точное (`fitres 5e-15`), `|logdet|=0` · `kernel_04` acc .924, dH +0.068, var_v 6.87 · `kernel_05` acc .987, dH +0.009, sum accepted dH ≈ 0.
- Объём (аффинный LS, с перехватом): `|logdet|` = 00: **7.375**, 01: 5.0e-5, 02: **5.534** (≈12·ln(1/0.6327)=5.565), 03: **0.0**, 04: 5.3e-5, 05: 5.0e-5.
- `base ladder step`: ladder[2] = 0.0732 = `step_size` **ровно** — неоднозначности выбора ранга нет.
- Воспроизводство с исправленным кодом: acc production `0.959–0.968` (0.983/0.984/0.953/0.952 по цепям), holdout acc `1.000`, |dH| p95 production `0.27`.
- Эталон цели (iid, 2e5): var(v)=8.99, E[r²]=1084 (≈(D−1)e^{σ²/2}=990), P(v<−5)=.048, P(v>5)=.048. Наш replay: var_v≈4.8–5.1, mean_v≈−0.82, P(v<−5)=.033, P(v>5)=**0** → бин [5,8) будет пустым, split-Rhat>1, var_v≠σ_v² — это ожидаемые (а не баг-)эффекты короткого окна 1020 переходов при жёстком exp-воронке; они прямо попадут в `validity_score`-члены.

## 3. Предлагаемый подход (по шагам)
1. **Chart-модуль**: `to_centered(q)` строго по public-конвенции (u=(q−shift)@Sᵀ; c[0]=u[0]; c[j]=u[j]+0.18·sin(u[0]+phase[j−1])) и обратный `to_q(c)` (u[j]=c[j]−0.18·sin(c[0]+phase[j−1]); q=u@S⁻ᵀ+shift) — round-trip 1e-14. `U,∂U/∂centered, grad_u, grad_U=grad_u@S`, `K=½pᵀGp`, `z=[v/σ_v, e^{−v/2}x]`.
2. **Устойчивый вывод карты (без машинно-точного residual)**: сетка на симметричном splitting-семействе (a,d); целевая функция = медианный/СКО невязки по 72 пробам, **только по rung {0,1,3}**, валидация на rung 2 (leave-one-rung-out CV во всех 4 вариантах). Критерий приёмки: (i) CV-невязка ≤ 3× «шумового пола», измеренного по паре kernel_02/kernel_05; (ii) обратимость ≤1e-12; (iii) volume |logdet| ≤1e-4; (iv) dH/acceptance согласованы с панелью kernel_05 (acc 0.987, dH p95 0.024). Итог замораживается в `(a*,d*)`, для replay берём `(step_size, integration_steps)=(0.0732,18)` и `(0.0765,24)` из schedules. Параллельно считаю plain-leapfrog как **sensitivity baseline** и публикую оба набора статистик в логе (в обязательные артефакты идёт подогнанная карта).
3. **Replay ровно по данным стримов**: `H0=U(q_t)+K(p_t)` с **новым** импульсом каждого перехода (моя первая версия этопутала — исправлено), `(q*,p*)=Map(q,p,ε,L)`, `ΔH=U(q*)+K(p*)−H0`, `accept_prob=min(1,e^{−ΔH})`, приёмка `uniforms[t] < accept_prob`, при отказе состояние не меняется. production → первые `audit_transitions=80` переходов в `transition_audit.npz`, kept = последние 900 из 1020; holdout → первые 100 из 160 в `holdout_transition_audit.npz`, `holdout_terminal_states` = после всех 160.
4. **Failure-mode правила (вычисляемые, не хардкод)**: (1) valid = минимум композитного аномалии-скоринга (obs dH rms + reverse-пол + |logdet| + |panel_var−σ²|) → kernel_05; (2) coordinate_mismatch = обратимость на шумовом полу **И** |logdet|≈0 **И** большой dH → kernel_03; (3) delayed_response = dq вдоль концевой drift-компоненты с устойчивым α≈−0.22 по всем рангам **И** импульсы совпадают с валидной картой (4.9e-5) → kernel_01; (4) terminal_imbalance = state совпадает с валидным, концевой импульс uniform-scaled, acceptance насыщена 1.0, dH≡<0 → kernel_02; (5) energy_drift = систематически положительный накапливающийся ΔH при здоровом объёме (04: 63.7% dH>0, acc .924, trend U +0.086/шаг, sum accepted dH до +8.2) → kernel_04; (6) volume_loss = остаток с максимальным объёмным дефектом (00: |logdet| 7.38) → kernel_00. Каждый из 6 лейблов используется ровно один раз; порядок приоритетов фиксирую в `analysis.py`.
5. **kernel_audit по определениям**: `energy_rmse`/`reverse_p95` на rung[2]; `energy_slope` = OLS log–log по 4 рангам; `volume_logdet_abs` = |logdet| линейной части аффинного LS (с intercept) 24→24; `acceptance_rate=mean(panel_accepted[c])`; `panel_mean_v/var_v` по dim-0; `panel_rhat_v` = split-Rhat (3 цепи × 2 части); `panel_ess_v` = initial-positive-sequence ESS (Geyer, BDA3) по цепям, суммарно; `validity_score` — линейная формула из брифа, слово в слово.
6. **Диагностика/артефакты**: split-Rhat и IPS-ESS для v и radius²; `funnel_profile.csv` на точной сетке из csv; `expected_radius2=(D−1)·mean(exp(v))` по kept-образцам бина; `latent_mean_abs_max/latent_var_abs_max` из **z**-остатков; `samples.npy = to_centered(latent_samples)`; формы/dtype проверяются self-check-проходом в конце `analysis.py` (assert по всем shapes/ключам JSON).
7. **overview.png — без matplotlib**: matplotlib в окружении **отсутствует**, сети нет, а системный PIL собран под CPython 3.14 и из venv 3.12 не импортируется (`cannot import name '_imaging'`). Поэтому PNG пишу собственным микро-энкодером на numpy+zlib (filter-0, 8-bit RGB). Я его реализовал и проверил: 640×480, корректные IHDR/IDAT, обратно распаковывается в ровно `922080` байт с нулевыми filter-байтами, пиксели совпадают.

## 4. Существенные допущения / неоднозначности (прошу подтвердить или поправить)
- **A. matplotlib нет.** Требование «numpy/matplotlib only» физически невыполнимо для matplotlib → рисую PNG сам. Альтернатива: оставить `overview.png` минимальной таблицей-изображением. Подтверждаете numpy-only rasterizer?
- **B. Лестница для energy_rmse/energy_slope**: использую `step_size_ladder` из bundle (4 ранга), а не синтетическую; «base ladder step» = rung 2 (0.0732, точное совпадение со `step_size`, ties нет).
- **C. `energy_rmse` считаю по набл. proposal-массивам** (как в определении), т.е. для 00/03 это огромные числа — так и задумано.
- **D. «Ничем не различимые кандидаты» на base rung**: здесь неразличимы только 02 и 05 по **state** (5.5e-5 = шум). Разрешаю tie по **momentum**-каналу (02: 0.726 vs 05: 6.1e-3), затем по объёму, затем по панели; т.е. иерархия «state→momentum→volume→panel», а не «первый по id».
- **E. `reverse_p95` при возмущённых reverse-массивах**: считаю точно как написано — 72 значения `‖rs−ps‖₂ + ‖rm+pm‖₂` на кандидата/ранг, затем 95-й перцентиль. Не вычитаю шум и не нормирую (только интерпретация: <1e-3 ≜ «на уровне возмущений»).
- **F. `volume_logdet_abs` — с intercept или без.** Беру **аффинную** регрессию (слово «affine»), тогда у валидного кандидата 5e-5, что согласуется с порогом `full=1e-5/zero=0.08`. Без intercept валидный даёт 0.109 (т.е. проваливает собственный порог объёма) —这条 считаю неверной трактовкой.
- **G. `acceptance_rate`**: `mean(panel_accepted[c])` по всем 260 переходам (дословно из определения). Альтернатива «только 220 kept» почти не меняет (0.987 vs 0.986) — оставляю дословную.
- **H. Выравнивание панели**: `panel_accepted[c]` — 260 переходов, `panel_centered_samples[c]` — 220 kept-состояний; проверял правило «отказ ⇔ повтор состояния» — оно согласуется с offset 40, поэтому метрики панели беру по 220 kept, а acceptance по 260.
- **I. Эскалация интегрирования при неизвестной внутренней параметризации**: не эскалирую L/ε сверх рангов лестницы; идентификация идёт по форме симметричной композиции (a,d), total time = ε·L фиксирован schedule'ом. Побочный вывод: при фиксированном T разложение «(ε,L)» не идентифицируемо по набл. данным (невязка выходит на пол возмущений для L≳18) — поэтому для replay беру ε и L **строго из schedules**, а не из фита.
- **J. Пустые бины `funnel_profile`**: строку выдаю с `count=0, fraction=0, mean_v/mean_radius2/expected_radius2 = NaN` (пустые поля CSV), т.к. «по kept-образцам бина» среднее не определено. Если нужны нули — скажите.
- **K. Формулировка «kept» vs `audit_transitions`**: audit = **первые** 80 (production) / 100 (holdout) переходов, kept-сэмпл = последние 900 после 120 warmup. Альтернатива «последние 80» возможна — беру префикс, как обычно для audit-потока.
- **L. `latent_mean_abs_max / latent_var_abs_max`**: по z → `max_d mean|z_d|` и `max_d var(z_d)` (эталон z~N(0,1)). «abs» в `var_abs` читается как модуль, но var≥0, так что модуль тривиален.
- **M. Различение energy_drift / delayed_response / coordinate_mismatch на коротких панелях**: опираюсь на 3 независимых сигнатуры (направление dq, обратимость, объём), а не на величину dH; но 00↔04 (volume_loss↔energy_drift) — самое слабое место: у 00 оба дефекта сразу (|logdet| 7.38 и dH +27). Альтернативный разбор: 00=energy_drift, 04=volume_loss. Мой приоритет — правило (5)/(6) выше; если у вас есть предпочтение, поменяю порядок правил местами.
- **N.** Панели, по-видимому, сгенерированы при чуть меньшей эффективной жёсткости: при ε=0.0732, L=18 моя оценка dH p95=0.064 против панельных 0.024 (acceptance совпадает: 0.984 vs 0.987). Панельные метрики беру **из данных как есть**, не пересчитываю.

## 5. Реализуемость
CPU 1 ядро, память 2 TB. Время: production replay 1020×4×18 ≈ **1.5–2 с**, holdout ≈0.2 с, один ladder-скан 4×72×18 ≈0.1 с, полный fit (45×45×3 ранга) ≈**20 с**, аудит-метрики 6×4×72 ≈ пренебрежимо. Итого `analysis.py` < 1 мин. Память: самый большой массив 0.39 MB (`transition_momenta`), панель 0.38 MB, bundle reverse 0.17 MB; пик < 50 MB. Диск: 18 GB свободно; итоговые артефакты ~5–10 MB.

**Статус шага**: `results/` не создавался, `analysis.py` не написан. Разведочные скрипты лежат в `_scratch/` (скажу — удалить их перед финалом или оставить).

## 2) ENFOQUE PROPUESTO

**Mecánica (una sola vez, functions puras en `analysis.py`).** Chart público literal: `u=(q-shift)@matrix.T`; `centered[0]=u[0]`; `centered[1:]=u[1:]+0.18*sin(u[0]+phase)`. Inversa exacta y sin iteración porque el warp depende solo de `centered[0]`: `u[0]=c[0]`, `u[1:]=c[1:]-0.18*sin(c[0]+phase)`, `q=u@inv(M).T+shift`. `U`, `dU/dv`, `dU/dx` según las fórmulas públicas; `grad_u[0]=gc[0]+0.18*Σ gc[j]cos(u0+phase)`, `grad_u[j]=gc[j]`, `grad_U(q)=grad_u@matrix`. `K=0.5 p·G·p`, `H=U+K`, `z_0=v/sigma_v`, `z_i=exp(-v/2)x_i`. Verifiqué que esta convención es internamente consistente: `grad_U(q)=grad_u@M` reproduce la derivada por diferencias finitas (lo auditaré con ~1e-6 en el script).

**Inferencia de la familia (el núcleo). Ya tengo evidencia dura de sondas:**
- `energy_rmse`/`ΔH` y `reverse_p95` en el escalón base separan así: `k00` dH med +39.1, reverse_p95 7.3e3 (catastrófico); `k02` reverse 4.83, **logdet 5.53**; `k04` reverse 2.42, dkd exacto; `k01` reverse 0.40; `k03` reverse **1.66e-4**, logdet **0.000000**; `k05` reverse **1.69e-4**, logdet **5.0e-5** (los únicos dos reversibles de verdad).
- Paneles: acc(all-260) `k00`=0.058, `k01`=0.982, `k02`=1.000, `k03`=0.060, `k04`=0.924, `k05`=0.987; var_v 4.72/4.94/5.54/3.43/6.88/5.83 (σ_v²=9).
- **Prueba decisiva de emparejamiento**: `kernel_04` reproduce con un mapa **drift-kick-drift** (`[D(eps),K(eps)]×18`, gradiente en coordenadas sampler, métrica `G`, sin flip) con residual p95 = **6.96e-5** ≈ la escala de las perturbaciones; `kernel_03` es un mapa **exactamente afín** (rms_resid del ajuste = 1.1e-15) con logdet 0; `kernel_02` = los mismos estados que `kernel_05` (diferencia máx 1.2e-4) pero momentos escalados ×0.6305 → **logdet = 12·ln(0.6305) = −5.534**, que coincide con el `volume_logdet_abs` medido (5.534) → `kernel_02` es un mapa de **pérdida de volumen** construido sobre el válido.
- El mapa de `kernel_05`/`kernel_01` **no** es el leapfrog de texto: su residual contra kick-drift-kick escala como **ε^3.1** en la escalera (2º orden simétrico, simetría reversible intacta), y `k01` es ≈`k05` en estados (dif. 5.9e-2) pero sus momentos no son ± iguales.

**Regla de decisión sin asumir default** (y sin exigir precisión de máquina): para cada candidato calculo un vector de invariantes — (i) orden de consistencia de `ΔH` en la escalera (pendiente `log-log` esperada ≈ −1/−2 para un integrador simétrico vs ≈ +1 para uno con *drift*), (ii) `reverse_p95` normalizado contra el **suelo de perturbación observado** (mediana de `k03/k05` ≈ 1.3e-4), (iii) `volume_logdet_abs`, (iv) sesgo del panel (`|var_v−9|/9`, desvío de aceptación respecto de 0.82, `rhat`). Selecciono el candidato con mayor `validity_score` y, además, exijo que sea **simultáneamente** reversible (dentro del suelo de perturbación) y volumen-preservante (`|logdet|` en el suelo, no escalando con el paso). Etiquetado por *asignación canónica a 6 canales* (6 candidatos ↔ 6 etiquetas, permutación óptima del vector de invariantes), con desempate documentado: `k00`→energy_drift (dH/|Δ| explosivos y pendientes no simétricas), `k02`→volume_loss (logdet 5.53 = firma exacta del escalado de momento), `k03`→coordinate_mismatch (afín exacto con logdet 0: preserva volumen pero no es un flujo Hamiltoniano del target → aceptación colapsada), `k04`→terminal_imbalance vs delayed_response decidido por si la asimetría está en los extremos del trayecto (flip/`dkd` mal enlazado) o en un retardo de gradiente (comparando contra plantillas `kdk` con gradiente rezagado); documentaré ambas hipótesis y el marcador elegido.

**Tolerancias (no exijo precisión de máquina).** Suelo de perturbación empírico ≈ 1.3e-4 (mediana `reverse`), `reverse_p95` umbral "reversible" = 1e-3 (el `linear(...,1e-8,5e-3)` de la rúbrica ya declara muerto lo >5e-3; separo "vivo" de "muerto" en 1e-3 y "dudoso" 1e-4–1e-3). Validación del replay: acepto una plantilla si el residual p95 contra los arrays observados está en la escala de perturbación (≤ ~5e-4 en probes conservadores) **o** si su `ΔH` escala con orden ≥2 en ε y su logdet está en el suelo — es decir, la validación es por invariantes + escala, no por `allclose` a una plantilla.

**Definiciones operativas.** `energy_rmse` en ladder idx 2 (base, =0.0732). `energy_slope = polyfit(log(step), log(energy_rmse_per_step), 1)[0]` (una recta por candidato; reporto también R² como diagnóstico interno). `volume_logdet_abs`: mínimos cuadrados de `[volume_input, 1] → volume_output[c]`, `A = B[:24,:24].T`, `|Σ log svd(A)|` (con `logdet` por SVD, estable: `cond` máximo observado 58). `acceptance_rate = mean(panel_accepted[c])` **sobre los 260** (lectura literal del brief). `panel_mean_v`/`panel_var_v`: media y varianza muestral (`ddof=1`) de `panel_centered_samples[c][:,:,:,0]` concatenando las 3 cadenas. `panel_rhat_v`: split-Rhat estándar dividiendo cada una de las 3 cadenas por la mitad (6 medias), con la fórmula Gelman `sqrt((W+B/n)/W)` en la muestra completa. `panel_ess_v`: ESS por secuencia positiva inicial (Geyer): autocovarianzas `ρ_k` por cadena sobre la cadena completa, suma pares `(ρ_{2k}+ρ_{2k+1})` hasta el primer par ≤0, `ESS = N/(1+2Σρ)`.

**Replay determinista.** Producción y holdout usan **los momentos/uniformes supplied, sin sorteos propios**: en la transición `t` de la cadena `c`, `p = transition_momenta[c,t]`, `u_rand = transition_uniforms[c,t]`, `log u = log(u_rand)`; acepto si `log u ≤ min(0, ΔH)`.
