== 2. МЕТОДИЧЕСКИЙ ПЛАН ПО АРТЕФАКТАМ ==
Модель (рабочая гипотеза): H = −J Σ_{<ij>} cos(θ_i−θ_j), J=1, k_B=1, периодические ГУ, квадратная решётка, β=1/T.

MC-протокол на каждую (L,T): θ из соответствующего slot (детерминированный старт + seed от scan_token); стадии обновлений по control (локальный Метрополос, proposal N(0, 1.13) рад, 1 local + 2 reflection + 2 cluster повторов за проход), warmup 113, sampling 116 проходов, stride 1. R независимых сидов (предлагаю R=24) на каждую (L,T) — они же джекнайф-блоки.

- obs_matrix_a, Upsilon(L,T): отклик на фазовый сдвиг (twist) Υ = (N/(2T))·∂²F/∂φ² при φ→0, вычисляемый через термодинамическую интеграцию между φ=0 и φ=2π/L (4 twist-конфигурации), с поправкой на ветвление (winding): все разности оборачиваются в (−π,π] (branch-safe), плюс контрольный расчёт по формуле линейного отклика Υ = (1/(N T))[⟨Σ_bond cos Δ⟩ − β⟨W²⟩], где W — суммарный ток по направлению (это и есть «winding/branch correction»). Усреднение Υ_x, Υ_y.
- obs_matrix_b, плотность дефектов: вихри по плакетам q_p = (1/2π)Σ_□ wrap(Δθ) ∈ {0,±1}; ρ_v = ⟨Σ|q_p|⟩/N.
- obs_tensor_c: радиальные профили G(r)=⟨s_i·s_{i+r}⟩ по оболочкам (r ∈ probe_axis, L=104) для 4 температур из focus_probe_rows.
- obs_matrix_d, η(T): логарифмическая производная по двум БОЛЬШИМ размерам. Основной оценщик — two-size ratio при фиксированной доле x=r/L: G_L(r) = r^{−η} f(r/L) ⇒ η(T) = ln[G_{L1}(x L)/(x L)^{−η}...] реализую как η = ln[G_{L2}(r)/G_{L1}(r·L1/L2)]/ln(L2/L1) на паре (86,104) в окне fit_window_probe=[7,24]; как перекрёстную проверку — log-log наклон G(r) vs r в том же окне для L=104. В obs_matrix_d кладу (T, η(T)).
- obs_matrix_e, xi_2nd/L: ξ² = [1/(4 sin²(k_min/2))]·(S(k_min)/S(0) − 1), k_min = 2π/L (второй момент, по усреднению S по k-оболочкам); нормировка такова, что ξ/L ≤ ~0.5 в КТ-фазе (тест корректности).
- obs_matrix_f, χ = N⟨|m|²⟩/T.

Маршрут 1 (Weber–Minnhagen, основной = «residual sweep»): для каждой T и каждого кандидата L_min ∈ {32,50,68} (все, оставляющие ≥3 размера) подгоняю единый nuisance-сдвиг C в Υ(L,T) ≈ (2T/π)[1 + 1/(2(log L + C))] (стабильный 1D-поиск/золотое сечение по C ∈ [−log L_min + 0.5, +20]) и храню относительный L2 остаток по выбранным размерам → полный температурный трек на кандидата. `residual_sweep_best_axis_a_values` — T, минимизирующая остаток (пересечение с 2T/π с учётом лог-поправок); `selected_residual_sweep_min_axis` — кандидат с наиболее устойчивым минимумом; `preferred_transition_temperature` = WM-оценка при выбранном L_min (она же phase_summary.transition_temperature_estimate), `preferred_offset_value` = C, `preferred_residual_value` = остаток; `residual_sweep_stability_spread` = разброс лучших T по кандидатам.
Маршрут 2 (log-поправка восприимчивости, «response sweep»): χ(L,T) ≈ A L^{7/4} (log L + C)^{1/8}, A и C фитируются (C — 1D-оптимизация с ограничением log L + C > 0) при каждом L_min → трек относительных L2 остатков, лучшие T/C/остатки → response_* ключи.
5 компонент конечноразмерных интерцептов (строго в заданном порядке, аргумент x = 1/log L в порядке scan_axis_b): (1) Weber–Minnhagen; (2) size-weighted raw NK (взвешенное по L² условие Υ_L(T)/T = 2/π по всем размерам); (3) βΥ-интерцепт (линейная экстраполяция Υ/T по x при каждой T, корень intercept(T) = 2/π); (4) ξ_2nd/L-интерцепт (fit ξ/L = a(T) + b(T)x; T* из смены знака b(T), a(T*) — универсальное отношение); (5) η = 1/4 (корень η(T) = 0.25 из obs_matrix_d). `transition_component_estimates/_uncertainties` — эти 5 значений; `transition_estimate_spread`/`consensus_transition_spread` — разброс (max−min) пяти оценок; `consensus_transition_temperature` — их медиана (с отдельной джекнайф-погрешностью).
Джекнайф: блоки = R независимых сидовых реплик (jackknife_block_count = R); все производные величины (T_c-оценки, остатки, интерцепты) пересчитываются при leave-one-block-out → SE = √((R−1)/R Σ(θ_i−θ̄)²). Неопределённости предпочтительного остатка и response-остатка — тем же методом.
phase_summary: `stiffness_jump_ratio_at_transition` = Υ(T*)/T* (интерполяция Υ/T по сетке T, НЕ нормированная на 2/π); `stiffness_jump_residual` = это − 2/π; `defect_density_span` = ρ_v(L=104, T_max) − ρ_v(L=104, T_min) (скаляр); `dimensionless_ratio_at_transition` = интерполяция `dimensionless_ratio_intercepts`(по T) в T* (не сырое ξ/L); `selected_profile_indices`=[3,5,6,8], `selected_profile_axis_a_values` = соответствующие T; `profile_fit_window`=[7,24].
overview.png: панели — Υ/T vs T с горизонталью 2/π; ρ_v(T); G(r) (log-log, L=104, окно 7–24); ξ/L vs T (пересечение размеров); χ L^{-7/4} vs T; η(T) с 0.25.
ВАЖНОЕ ОГРАНИЧЕНИЕ ПО ГРАФИКЕ: matplotlib ОТСУТСТВУЕТ, сети нет (pip install падает по DNS), PIL есть только в системном python3.14 (несовместим с нашим venv 3.12). Проверил рабочий обход: собственный PNG-энкодер на numpy+zlib (тест: файл 132 байта записан корректно). Планирую чистый numpy-рендерер (решётка, полилинии, подписи шрифтом 5×7, легенды) для overview.png.

== 3. ПРЕДПОЛОЖЕНИЯ И НЕОПРЕДЕЛЁННОСТИ (не снимаются файлами) ==
1) Идентификация модели: 2D XY на квадратной решётке с ПЕРИОДИЧЕСКИМИ ГУ и J=1 — вывод из форм банка, фаз (0..2π) и twist-структуры; прямо в файлах НЕ записано (альтернатива — планарный G/кубованная O(2) — маловероятна).
2) Единицы: J=k_B=1, T в единицах J/k_B; β=1/T. Control не задаёт β — принимаю β=1/T (в компоненте «βΥ-интерцепт» это Υ/T).
3) Взаимодействие только ближайших соседей; гамильтониан с −J cos; Υ в размерности d=2 без доп. L-множителей.
4) Роль probe_stride=5: неоднозначна (прореживание проходов либо к-точек). Предлагаю трактовать как шаг прореживания сохраняемых сэмплов для корреляционных профилей; на сетке probe_axis 1..50 это не влияет.
5) Seeds/число прогонов в control ОТСУТСТВУЮТ → задаю детерминированно: seed_r = hash(scan_token, L, T, r); R=24 (обсуждаемо).
6) Convention интерполяции для `dimensionless_ratio_at_transition`: линейная кусочная интерполяция по T сетки axis_a (сплайн не использую); та же конвенция для Υ/T в точке T*.
7) Метод неопределённостей: block-jackknife по репликам; внутрипрогонная автокорреляция не оценивается (stride=1 ⇒ сильная корреляция, поэтому блоки = независимые сида, а не соседние сэмплы).
8) Разделение «intercepts/slopes» в phase_fit_diagnostics: толкую как пер-температурные списки (n_axis_a) линейных экстраполяций по x=1/log L: `finite_size_intercepts/slopes` для Υ/T, `dimensionless_ratio_intercepts/slopes` для ξ/L. Если у вас иная конвенция (например, списки из 5 компонент) — скажите, это изменит форму двух пар ключей.
9) `setting_key`: выбираю "scan_761c69759dbb7959" (scan_token). Резерв: "pcal_scan_v5".
10) КТ-критерий: скачок 2/π (Nobel-значения 8/π не используется, т.к. контракт прямо требует Υ/T − 2/π).

== 4. ОСУЩЕСТВИМОСТЬ И Валидация ==
Жёсткость ресурсов: фактическое ограничение — 1 ядро (nproc=1), но расчёт дёшев. Замер (реальный микро-тест векторизованного sublattice-Metropolis): 0.2 мс/проход при L=32, 0.3 при L=68, 0.6 при L=104 ⇒ 229 проходов (113+116) при L=104 ≈ 0.14 с. Полная сетка 5×9 × (4 twist-геометрии) × R=24 сидов ≈ 10³–10⁴ с ⇒ ориентировочно 5–20 минут на одном ядре (память < 1 ГБ). R=24 можно поднять до 48 без риска; R=8 — при нехватке времени.
Предпрогоночные тесты корректности: (a) Υ/T → 2/π при T* (скачок) и монотонность Υ/L-скейлинг; (b) точность 2/π проверяю на заведомо упорядоченном пределе (низкая T ⇒ Υ/T близко к 1, sign-монотонно); (c) нормировка ξ_2nd/L: в сильно упорядоченном пределе ξ/L мала и растёт с T, значение в КТ-фазе ~0.2–0.6; (d) ρ_v ≥ 0 и ρ_v(T_max) > ρ_v(T_min) (⇒ положительный defect_density_span); (e) χ>0, χ растёт с L при T>T*; (f) G(r)→0, log-log наклон ∈ (−1, 0) при T*, η(T) монотонно растёт; (g) жёсткая проверка форм: (5,9),(5,9),(4,50),(9,2),(5,9),(5,9); (h) JSON-контракты: все обязательные ключи присутствуют, трек-списки выровнены по L_min-спискам, скалярность defect_density_span; (i) воспроизводимость — повторный прогон с тем же seed даёт идентичные .npy (бит-в-бит) и полный прогон-лог сидов.

ПРОШУ СОГЛАСОВАТЬ: (1) R=24 сидов-блоков и трактовку stage_plan как бюджета на реплику; (2) выбор scan_token как setting_key; (3) конвенцию intercepts/slopes (по-температурная vs 5-компонентная); (4) допустимость собственного numpy-PNG-рендерера для overview.png; (5) основную оценку η (two-size ratio при фиксированной r/L) с перекрёстным log-log наклоном.

计划审读完毕。方法论路线我认可，可以进入主计算。以下先确认我同意的判断，再给出若干需要在实现时锁定的约定与一处需要重点防范的风险。

一、予以确认的部分
1. 轴与探针的角色判定成立：scan_axis_a（9 点，0.819–0.928，单调）为温度 T；scan_axis_b = [32,50,68,86,104] 为线性尺度 L；probe_axis_a = 1..50 为最大格 L=104 的径向距离（r ≤ 50 < L/2），与 (n_axis_b,n_axis_a)=(5,9)、d=(9,2)、c=(4,50) 完全自洽。
2. 状态库角色判定成立：五个 slot 为逐 L 的初始位形（相位 θ∈(0,2π)，含量子化 2π/L 扭曲、winding ±1，两热三冷），因此连续角变量下转移矩阵/枚举不适用，蒙特卡洛是唯一正确路线；把该库作为确定性初始条件并借其指示 twist 几何，这一处理我同意。
3. 判据用 Υ/T → 2/π（而非 8/π），setting_key 取 scan_token "scan_761c69759dbb7959"（family_tag 作后备并写入说明），focus_probe_rows=[3,5,6,8] 与 fit_window_probe=[7,24] 直接取自 control 而不自行按邻近 T_c 挑选，均妥当。
4. 不确定度以独立种子副本为 jackknife 块（而非 stride=1 的强相关相邻样本），这是正确取舍。

二、请在实现中锁定（属我的方法建议，非对固定要求的替换）
1. 截距/斜率的形态约定，请采用「逐温度」解释：diagnostic_abscissa_values 为 x=1/log L 的 5 个值（严格按 scan_axis_b 次序）；finite_size_intercepts/slopes 为在 x=1/log L 上对 Υ/T 逐温度线性外推得到的 9 元表；dimensionless_ratio_intercepts/slopes 同理为 ξ_2nd/L 的 9 元表。五分量束（Weber–Minnhagen、size-weighted raw NK、βΥ 截距、ξ_2nd/L 截距、η=1/4）只体现在 transition_component_estimates / _uncertainties 中。如此 dimensionless_ratio_at_transition = 在 T* 处对 9 元 dimensionless_ratio_intercepts 作线性分段插值，直接满足契约；请勿改用最大格原始 ξ/L。
2. Υ 估计量的成本安排：主估计量请用单一的标准 winding／线性响应形式（回绕到 (−π,π]，两方向平均，并显式减 β⟨W²⟩ 项）；四套 twist 几何的热力学积分只作为 2–3 个 (L,T) 点上的交叉验证，不必在全部 5×9×24 点执行。把交叉验证的相对偏差作为附加诊断字段写入 phase_fit_diagnostics.json。这样可省约四倍机时，且仍保留对归一化约定（是否含 1/d、1/2 因子）的实证校验——这一点是契约隐含的关键风险。
3. equilibrium 风险（本次最主要的科学风险）：113 条热身 + 116 条采样是 control 给定的预算，请不要擅自扩大，但必须做可报告的检验：（i）把采样段分前后两半，记录 L=86、104 上 Υ/T、ξ/L、χ、ρ_v 的半段漂移；（ii）在 L=104、T 取 focus 行附近，额外用另一 slot（例如以冷启动替代热启动）跑一条链，证明观测值对初始位形不敏感。若最大格在 T* 附近 Υ/T 的半段漂移超过约 1–2%，不要静默加步数，而是把该偏差写入 diagnostics 与最终说明，再与我商议是否延长预算。
4. stiffness_jump_ratio_at_transition 的口径：请在 phase_summary.json 与最终说明中明示它取「最大格 L=104 的 Υ/T 在 T* 处按 T 网格线性插值」；stiffness_jump_residual 即其减 2/π。预期为有限尺寸下的少量欠冲量级；若算出 |residual| ≳ 0.15，请作为异常如实报告并附 Υ 估计量诊断，切勿事后归一化到 2/π。
5. 副本数：R=24 批准。若实际墙钟超出约 30–40 分钟，请优先降 R 至 16，而不要压缩热身；并把 jackknife_block_count 记为真正使用的 R。
6. overview.png：自建 numpy+zlib 编码器可以接受，但须（a）用系统 python3.14 的 PIL 实际解码一次以证明文件有效；（b）至少含 Υ/T（带 2/π 参考线与 T* 竖线）、ρ_v(T)、L=104 的 G(r) 双对数（含 7–24 拟合窗标记）、ξ/L 的尺度交叉、χ L^{-7/4}、η(T)（带 0.25 线）六个面板；（c）有坐标刻度、数值标注与图例，不可为无刻度的示意块。
7. 一致性硬要求：phase_summary.selected_profile_indices / selected_profile_axis_a_values 与 diagnostics 中同名键逐项相同；phase_summary.transition_temperature_estimate 必须等于 preferred_transition_temperature（即所选 L_min 的 Weber–Minnhagen 值），inverse_transition_temperature_estimate = 1/T*；defect_density_span 必须是标量 ρ_v(104,T_max) − ρ_v(104,T_min)；transition_estimate_spread 与 consensus_transition_spread 均取五分量极差，consensus_transition_temperature 取五分量中位数，并在 diagnostics 中给出各自 jackknife 不确定度；residual_sweep 与 response_sweep 的 min_axis 列表应覆盖所有仍余 ≥3 个尺度的候选（即 L_min ∈ {32,50,68}），且 traces 与各自 min_axis 列表等长对齐。

三、交付要求
一次性产出全部十项原生文件于工作目录，键名与相对路径严格采用契约文本；完成后请提交数值摘要（T* 及五分量、spread、preferred C 与残差、response 路由结果、2/π 检验、各 npy 形状自检）与自检清单结果，并附一段对平衡性与归一化约定的诚实评估。除契约所列内容外，不要额外扩展研究范围。

2) Statistics / jackknife: R = 20 independent replicas per (L,T) with independent seeds; replica r's sampling-pass mean = ONE jackknife block, so jackknife_block_count = 20 with statistically clean (independent) blocks. All observables get per-block means, giving jackknife error bars for every matrix and propagated uncertainty for every fit route. (This honours the prescribed per-chain protocol literally instead of secretly lengthening chains; total cost ~45x20 runs, single-core estimate 30-60 min - I will pilot-time it and report.)
3) Estimator definitions (all J=1, N = L^2, wrapped differences w(x) = ((x+pi) mod 2pi) - pi):
   * Helicity modulus (twist-curvature / current-current form, direction-averaged):
     Upsilon = (1/2N) sum_{mu=x,y} [ <S^mu_2> - (1/T) Var(S^mu_1) ], S^mu_1 = sum_i w(theta_i - theta_{i+mu}), S^mu_2 = sum_i cos(w(...)). This is Upsilon = (1/N) d^2F/dphi^2 for a per-bond twist phi, with dimensions of T, so Upsilon/T -> 2/pi at T_KT and Upsilon/T -> 1 at T->0 - matching the prescribed Weber-Minnhagen form Upsilon ~ (2T/pi)(1 + 1/(2(log L + C))).
     Cross-check: independent twisted-BC finite-difference free-energy estimate at (L=104, a few T).
   * Defect/vortex density: plaquette vorticity q_p = (1/2pi)[w(th_00-th_10)+w(th_10-th_11)+w(th_11-th_01)+w(th_01-th_00)] on periodic plaquettes; rho_v = <sum_p |q_p|>/N (vortices per lattice site, in [0,1]).
   * Second-moment correlation length: S(k) = (1/N)<|sum_j e^{i theta_j} e^{i k.r_j}|^2>; xi_2nd = [1/(2 sin(k_min/2))] sqrt(S(k_min)/S(0) - 1), k_min = 2pi/L averaged over the 4 symmetry-related modes; store xi_2nd/L. (Cheap direct projections onto the 5 needed modes instead of a full FFT.)
   * Susceptibility: chi = (1/N)(<|sum_j e^{i theta_j}|^2>) = (1/N)<M^2> (connected by symmetry), the L^(7/4)(log L)^(1/8)-scaling object.
   * eta(T): log-log least-squares slope of the largest-L (104) radial profile C(r) = <e^{i(theta_0 - theta_r)}> (FFT autocorrelation of e^{i theta}, min-image radial binning r=1..50, origins sub sampled with probe_stride) over the fit window; eta = -slope. Rows of obs_tensor_c = the 4 focus rows; obs_matrix_d = 9 rows (T, eta(T)) with eta from L=104 for every T.
4) Fit routes (all with jackknife propagation):
   * Weber-Minnhagen residual sweep (route 1 = preferred): for each L_min candidate, at every T minimise over C (bounded 1-D Brent/grid refinement, C restricted so log L + C > 0.5) the relative L2 residual of Upsilon(L,T) vs (2T/pi)(1 + 1/(2(log L + C))) over sizes >= L_min; store full-T residual traces, and per candidate (best T, best C, best residual). L_min candidates that leave >=3 sizes: {32, 50, 68} (index 0,1,2). Sweeps internally aligned with their L_min lists. T where the best residual is minimal = preferred_transition_temperature; residual_sweep_stability_spread = spread of best-T across candidates; selected_residual_sweep_min_axis = the selected L_min (largest-L_min candidate - most reliable asymptotics - unless you prefer argmin residual).
   * Susceptibility log-correction response sweep (route 6): for each L_min, at every T fit A and C in chi ~ A L^(7/4)(log L + C)^(1/8) (linear in A given C, 1-D search over C), store full-T relative-L2 traces and per-candidate best (T, C, residual); response_transition_temperature = best-T at the selected response L_min.
   * x = 1/log(L) intercept routes: (a) finite_size_intercepts/slopes = per-T linear fits of beta*Upsilon = Upsilon/T vs x over the 5 sizes, finite_size_transition_estimate = T where intercept(T) = 2/pi, finite_size_transition_residual = intercept(T_*) - 2/pi; (b) dimensionless_ratio_intercepts/slopes = per-T linear fits of xi_2nd/L vs x, dimensionless_ratio_transition_estimate = T where intercept(T) = R*, with R* determined from the consecutive-size xi/L crossing values inside the scan window; dimensionless_ratio_at_transition in phase_summary = interpolating dimensionless_ratio_intercepts at T_c (per the contract, NOT the raw largest-L value); (c) eta = 1/4 route = exponent_transition_estimate = T where interpolated eta(T) = 1/4, exponent_transition_residual = eta(T_*) - 1/4.
   * size route: size_transition_estimates = per-size raw crossing temperatures where Upsilon(L,T)/T = 2/pi (interpolated in T), size_weighted_transition_estimate = L^2-weighted mean of those that exist in the window.
   * Component bundle order (fixed, as required): [Weber-Minnhagen, size-weighted raw Upsilon/T crossings, beta*Upsilon intercept, xi_2nd/L intercept, eta=1/4]; transition_component_estimates/_uncertainties in that order, uncertainties from jackknife refits. consensus_transition_temperature = inverse-variance-weighted mean of the 5 components (jackknife-propagated), consensus_transition_spread = max-min, consensus_temperature_uncertainty = jackknife std of the consensus. transition_estimate_spread (summary) = max-min of the component bundle. preferred_transition_temperature = phase_summary.transition_temperature_estimate (same number, per contract). setting_key = scan_token "scan_761c69759dbb7959".
   * selected_profile_indices = [3,5,6,8], selected_profile_axis_a_values = scan_axis_a[[3,5,6,8]] = [0.88438, 0.89702, 0.90302, 0.92849], profile_fit_window = [7,24] (control-file pair, interpreted as inclusive probe-index bounds => r = 8..25).
5) Outputs: the 6 npy files with exactly the stated shapes (obs_*: (5,9), (5,9), (4,50), (9,2), (5,9), (5,9)), the 2 JSONs with the exact required key sets (no renamed/extra semantics), and overview.png built by a stdlib PNG writer: 6 panels - Upsilon/T vs T per L with 2/pi line; rho_v vs T; xi_2nd/L vs T (crossing); chi*L^-7/4 vs T; C(r) at the 4 focus T with the power-law fit; and the route estimates (component bundle + spread + T_c).

4. ASSUMPTIONS, OPEN UNCERTAINTIES, THINGS YOU MAY WANT TO OVERRIDE
=====================================================================
Cannot be determined from the files alone (flagged, with my default):

The required key name `selected_profile_axis_a_values` plus the mandated shape (n_focus_rows, n_probe) resolves it. Residual risk: if they were L rows, obs_tensor_c would be (4,50) with 4 of the 5 L values at fixed T - also possible shape-wise; my choice follows the JSON key semantics.

I recommend replicas (clean, and honours the prescribed chain length). Uncertainty: with only 116 passes/chain and critical slowing down near T_c at L=104, temporal blocks would likely underestimate the error; I will report an autocorrelation diagnostic.

## 1) Inspection of `data/task_input.json`

**Identity / structure.** Parsed with `encoding="utf-8-sig"`. Top-level keys: `task_id`, `units`, `cases`, `required_outputs`, `diagnostic_probe_rule`. Identifying key is **`task_id = "fluid-square-wake-2d-001"`**, `units = "dimensionless"`. **5 cases.** `required_outputs` matches the 5 paths in the contract; `diagnostic_probe_rule` confirms `x_probe = min(nx-1, square_center_x + 2*square_size)`.

| case_id | nx | ny | uin | re | square_center | size | n_steps | warmup | samp | nu=uin·D/re | tau=0.5+3nu | Ma=uin/cs | nSamples |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| re12p56 | 540 | 180 | 0.03 | 12.56 | (180,90) | 9 | 5000 | 1000 | 10 | 0.021497 | **0.564490** | 0.05196 | 400 |
| re23p06 | 540 | 180 | 0.03 | 23.06 | (180,90) | 9 | 5000 | 1000 | 10 | 0.011709 | **0.535126** | 0.05196 | 400 |
| re35p96 | 540 | 180 | 0.03 | 35.96 | (180,90) | 9 | 5000 | 1000 | 10 | 0.007508 | **0.522525** | 0.05196 | 400 |
| st_re60p00 | 540 | 180 | 0.03 | 60.00 | (180,90) | 9 | 5000 | 1000 | 10 | 0.004500 | **0.513500** | 0.05196 | 400 |
| st_re80p00 | 540 | 180 | 0.03 | 80.00 | (180,90) | 9 | 5000 | 1000 | 10 | 0.003375 | **0.510125** | 0.05196 | 400 |

Geometry is identical in all 5 cases; **only `re` varies** (so only `tau`). Every case yields **400 force samples** (steps 1000, 1010, …, 4990) ≥ 10 ✓.

**Modulo trap (confirmed by count):** `(step-warmup)%every==0` is also true for steps 0,10,…,990 (Python's modulo returns 0 for negative multiples). The filter must be `step >= warmup_steps AND (step-warmup)%every==0`, else you get 500 rows instead of 400.

**Edge proximity:** mask = x∈[176,184], y∈[86,94]. Gaps: left 176, right 355, below 86, above 85 cells. **No case touches an edge** — clipping never activates (min gap = 9.4× the body size). But see the asymmetry flag in §3.

**Mach:** cs=1/√3=0.57735 → Ma = 0.03/0.57735 = **0.0520** for all cases. Compressibility error is O(Ma²)≈0.3% — **low-Mach is not the concern.** The real numerical issue is that the contract forces **tau ∈ [0.510, 0.564]**, i.e. 2–13% above the inviscid limit tau=0.5 (omega→2), where BGK loses all dissipation of ghost modes. `x_probe = 198` in every case, 14 cells downstream of the trailing edge (x=184).

**Unused/dead metadata:** each case also carries `max_uin: 0.03` and `target_tau: 0.9`, which are *not* in the contract key list. `target_tau=0.9` is **unreachable** under the contract: nu(tau=0.9)=0.1333 would need uin=0.186 (Re=12.56) up to uin=1.185 (Re=80, Ma≈2). So `target_tau` must be treated as dead metadata, not used to rescale (see §3).

## 2) Proposed numerical approach (decision points)

**Environment facts that constrain the plan:** `numba` is **not installed** (ImportError) despite the declared requirement, and the box has **1 CPU core**. `/tmp` is wiped between calls; only `/workspace` persists.

- **Lattice/collision:** D2Q9, single-relaxation-time BGK at exactly the contract `tau=0.5+3nu` (Ladd post-collision/pre-streaming form). No change of operator unless BGK fails — and **I have already verified it does not**: with a correct lattice I ran BGK at the worst `tau=0.510125` with a bounce-back 9×9 square and the full inlet/outlet/wall stack for 1200+ steps, stable with ρ∈[0.9986,1.0071]. A no-obstacle control held u=0.0300 exactly and ρ within 0.5% of 1. So I will **not** use TRT/regularized/KBC. (For the record, TRT with the magic parameter Λ=¼ was tested and *diverged* here; it also violates "the contract `tau`".)
- **Initial condition:** deterministic uniform equilibrium `f_i = f_i^eq(ρ=1, u=(uin,0))` everywhere in fluid; solid nodes `f_i^eq(1,0,0)`. No RNG, no pre-settling, no extra warmup: exactly `n_steps` updates, statistics from the specified window only.
- **Inflow/outflow/walls:** inlet at x=0 imposes `u=(uin,0)` on the three unknown populations (ex>0) via **non-equilibrium extrapolation** (equilibrium part at the prescribed velocity + non-equilibrium part copied from column 1) — this is the variant I verified as stable and mass-consistent; over-specifying ρ=1 with a plain equilibrium inlet drained the domain to ρ=0.74 and blew up. Outlet at x=nx−1: **first-order convective BC** `f_k[-1]=f_k[-2]−uin(f_k[-2]−f_k[-3])` on the 3 unknown populations — verified non-reflecting and stable (zero-gradient and non-equilibrium outlets also passed). Top/bottom: **no-slip midway bounce-back** (default; see §3 for the open choice). Physical implication to report: no-slip walls make this a *confined channel* (blockage 9/180=5%) whose boundary layers grow downstream, so `cd` is systematically higher and more configuration-dependent than an unbounded-body reference; slip walls would keep the inflow uniform and lower `cd`.
- **Solid handling:** mask exactly `x∈[cx−half, cx−half+size)`, `y∈[cy−half, cy−half+size)`, `half=size//2` → x 176–184, y 86–94 (9×9=81 cells), clipped only if needed. No-slip via **midway (Ladd) bounce-back**, i.e. the no-slip surface sits at the mid-point of each fluid–solid link. This is deliberate: it makes the hydrodynamic side exactly `square_size=9`, consistent with `re=uin·square_size/re` and with the `square_size` in the cd/cl denominator. On-node bounce-back would instead give an effective side of `size−1=8` (≈10–15% drag difference at low Re) — a consequential choice, flagged in §3.
- **Force:** momentum exchange (Ma et al./Mei et al./Ladd) over fluid–solid links from **post-collision, pre-streaming** populations:
  `Fα = Σ_{x_f} Σ_{k: x_f+c_k∈solid} c_{k,α} [ f_k*(x_f) + f*_{opp(k)}(x_s) ]`,
  algebraically the same flux-jump as your `[f_i(x_f) − f̄_ī(x_s)]` once `f̄` is read as the post-reflection population (reflection reverses `c`). With midway bounce-back I add the standard **half-step (Mei/Ladd) correction** `(1/2)Σ c_{k,α}c_{k,β}∂_βρ` using a 5-point fluid density gradient, and will report its magnitude as a diagnostic (it vanishes for flat walls at uniform ρ and matters only at the corners). Then `cd=Fx/(0.5·uin²·D)`, `cl=Fy/(0.5·uin²·D)`, D=9.
  **Sign convention (explicit):** lattice +y = increasing row index; `cl>0` means force on the body **toward the top wall**; no axis flip anywhere.
- **Sampling & statistics:** step label = number of completed updates; samples at `step ∈ {1000,1010,…,4990}` (400 rows/case) → `fluid_force_series.csv`. `cd_mean = arithmetic mean of those 400 cd`. **`cl_rms = sqrt(mean((cl−mean(cl))²))`, i.e. fluctuation RMS about the mean** — not raw RMS. This matters here because the geometry is slightly asymmetric (nonzero mean cl), so the two definitions differ; I will record raw RMS in the report JSON too, but `cl_rms` in the CSV is the about-mean definition. Say the word if you want raw RMS instead.
- **Velocity extraction:** `fluid_centerline.csv` → y = `cy` = 90 (= ny//2, so both plausible readings coincide), all x=0…539 (exactly nx=540 rows); **cells inside the solid are reported as u=0.0** (no-slip solid, keeps the file finite and the row count exact). `fluid_transverse_profile.csv` at `x_probe=198` for y=0…179 (ny rows); this column is purely downstream of the body so no solid cells arise, but in-solid cells would likewise be written as 0.0. All fields sanitized: non-finite → 0.0 with a global guard that aborts loudly rather than writing NaN/Inf.
- **`converged` flag (auditable, not a constant):** True only if all of (a) no non-finite value and `max|u|<0.25` throughout the run; (b) relative drift of `cd_mean` between the first and second halves of the 400-sample window `< 2%`; (c) relative drift of the cd standard deviation between the two halves `< 10%`. Otherwise False, and the failing diagnostic is written into `fluid_report.json`.
- **Runtime:** 2.43e9 site-updates / 2.19e10 population updates total. Measured on this 1-core box: **16.3 ms/step** for collide+stream (collision-dominated at 13 ms), so ~82 s/case → **~7 min for all 5 cases**, comfortably one run. Memory is trivial (f is 9×180×540 float64 ≈ 7 MB). **Numba is unavailable**, so the fallback ladder if timing hurts is numpy-side only: preallocated buffers/in-place collision to cut temporaries, then force evaluation restricted to the 400 sampled steps (already planned). I would not change the physics to buy speed.

**Validation gates I will build in** (these already paid for themselves during planning): assert Σw=1, opposite-map involution, 9 distinct velocities; assert `Σf_i^eq=ρ` and `Σc_i f_i^eq=ρu` to machine precision; a uniform-flow regression that must stay at u=uin to 1e-12; inlet-vs-outlet mass balance.

## 3) Assumptions and open uncertainties (not silently resolved)

1. **`square_center` ordering** assumed `(cx, cy)` = (streamwise, transverse). Consistent: cx=180 puts the body at 33% of the chord with 355 cells of wake, and `x_probe` uses `square_center_x + 2·size`. Also note `x_probe` uses `cx`, *not* the mask's leading edge.
2. **`uin` is a lattice velocity** (lattice units, dt=dx=1), used identically as the BC value, in `nu=uin·D/re`, and in the dynamic pressure — assumed self-consistent.
3. **Wall treatment is genuinely underdetermined** (no-slip vs slip). Default no-slip; it changes `cd` measurably through blockage/boundary layers.
4. **Midway vs on-node bounce-back** changes the effective body size (9 vs 8 cells) and hence `cd` by ~10–15% at low Re. Default midway for dimensional consistency with the contract's `square_size`.
5. **Half-step force correction** included per your instruction; if you prefer the plain flux-jump sum, `cd` shifts by a few percent.
6. **`cl_rms` about-the-mean** (stated above, raw RMS also recorded).
7. **Geometric asymmetry, intrinsic to the contract mask:** walls at y=0,179 make the channel midplane y=89.5, while the 9×9 square spans y=86–94, centred on y=90 — it sits **0.5 cells closer to the top wall** (below gap 86 vs above gap 85). A nonzero mean `cl` is therefore physically expected, not a bug, and is also why about-mean vs raw-RMS `cl_rms` differ.
8. **`target_tau`/`max_uin` deliberately ignored** (unreachable, not in the contract key list). Flagging in case they signal that the task author intended a *different* `uin` than the one given — that would be a contract conflict; I follow `uin` from the case dict.
9. **Statistical adequacy — my biggest scientific concern:** shedding period ≈ D/(St·uin) ≈ 9/(0.14×0.03) ≈ **2100 steps**, so the 4000-step sampling window covers only ~1.9 periods, and the 1000-step warmup is only ~0.5 periods. Re=60/80 are near/above the square-cylinder instability threshold, so their `cd_mean`/`cl_rms` will carry real window noise and `converged` may legitimately be False. The contract forbids extending the window, so I will *report* this rather than fix it. The wake also never reaches the outlet within 5000 steps (355 cells / 0.03 ≈ 11800 steps), so the far-wake portion of the centerline is an undeveloped transient — legitimate output of the prescribed window, and worth stating in `method_summary`.
10. **Step-label convention** (state after k updates labelled k vs k−1) is a 1-in-5000 difference — negligible, but stated for auditability.
11. `fluid_report.json` extras (`cd_mean_avg` = mean of the 5 case `cd_mean`; plus convergence diagnostics) beyond the 4 required keys.

**No physics numbers are claimed yet** — the only quantitative results here are input parsing, the derived tau/Ma/sample table, the measured 16.3 ms/step cost, and the solver-validation probes. Awaiting your approval; the choices most worth your input are #3, #4, #5 and #6.

payload.message:
Approach approved. The inspection is thorough, the modulo/negative-step trap and the 86-vs-85 geometric asymmetry are exactly the kind of details I wanted surfaced, and your debugging provenance is honest and useful: since the earlier low-tau blow-up was traced to a malformed velocity set, a wrong incompressible equilibrium term, and a transposed wall index, I accept the conclusion that BGK at the contract tau is stable and that switching collision operators is unwarranted. TRT would also have violated the mandated single tau. Proceed to implementation and the full run.

Rulings on the four open conventions you flagged (these are researcher decisions, so record them as such in `method_summary`, not as contract text):

1) Walls: keep no-slip midway bounce-back on y=0 and y=ny-1. The contract's silent default plus its "clip the mask to the domain" language both point to a bounded domain, and bounce-back is the only option that is unambiguous in lattice units. Accept the consequence: this is a confined channel with 5% blockage and developing boundary layers, so cd is configuration-dependent and above an unbounded-body value. State that explicitly in `method_summary` so nobody reads cd as a canonical square-cylinder drag.

2) Bounce-back on the body: keep midway (Ladd). Your geometric argument decides it, and I checked it: fluid at x=175 against solid at x=176 puts the no-slip surface at 175.5, and 184 against 185 puts it at 184.5, giving a hydrodynamic side of exactly 9.0 = square_size, consistent with both `re = uin*D/re` and the `square_size` in the cd/cl denominator. On-node would give an effective side of 8 and silently mismatch the reference length. Keep midway.

3) Half-step force correction: drop it from the reported force. Report the plain momentum-exchange flux jump as the sole source of Fx, Fy. Reason: the contract defines Fx, Fy as the simulated solid-region momentum exchange with no correction term, and the Mei/Ladd density-gradient term is a second-order refinement whose magnitude is concentrated at the corners of a 9x9 box where a 5-point finite-difference gradient is itself crude. I do not want an unrequested offset of a few percent in cd. Keep computing the correction magnitude but only as a diagnostic written into `fluid_report.json`, so the choice is auditable rather than hidden.

4) cl_rms: keep RMS about the time mean, sqrt(mean((cl-mean(cl))^2)), in the CSV, and continue recording raw RMS in the report JSON. Given the half-cell asymmetry you identified, mean(cl) is expected to be nonzero, and the about-mean definition is the one that actually measures shedding strength — which is the point of a cl_rms column.

Additional requirements for the run and the deliverable:

- `analysis.py` must be fully self-contained and runnable from a clean workspace: do not import or depend on `/workspace/_scratch/bc4.py`, and do not write intermediates outside `./results/`. Carry the lattice-definition assertions (sum w = 1, opposite-map involution, 9 distinct velocities), the equilibrium conservation checks, and the uniform-flow regression into the script, but gate them behind a cheap startup self-test so they do not eat into the run budget.
- Do the full 540x180, 5000-step run for the first case (re12p56) as a stability gate and print rho range, max|u|, and inlet-vs-outlet mass imbalance; if it passes, run all five cases. Do not reduce the grid or the step count to save time — the numpy cost you measured is acceptable. If you hit genuine wall-clock trouble, the only permitted optimizations are numpy-side (in-place collision, preallocated buffers, force evaluated only on sampled steps). Any change to physics, tau, the time window, or the sampling rule is out of bounds.
- Enforce the sample rule as `step >= warmup_steps and (step - warmup_steps) % sample_every == 0` and assert 400 rows per case, plus assert exactly one summary row per case, 540 centerline rows, 180 transverse rows, and identical case_id sets across all four CSVs. Assert finiteness on every written column.
- Report `cd_mean` and `cl_rms` for the whole sampled window under the stated definitions, do not trim, re-window, or discard the re=60/re80 transients, and let `converged` be False where your stated drift criteria genuinely fail. I would rather see an honest False with the failing diagnostic in the JSON than a criterion quietly loosened.
- In `fluid_report.json`, include the four required keys plus: the per-case tau values, the conventions above (wall BC, midway bounce-back, plain flux-jump force, cl sign convention, cl_rms definition, step-label convention), the raw-RMS cl, the half-step-correction magnitude, the convergence diagnostics, and an explicit statement of the two window limitations you identified — roughly 1.9 shedding periods in the sampling window, and the fact that the wake needs on the order of 12000 steps to reach the outlet so the far-wake centerline is an undeveloped transient within the mandated 5000 steps.
- On `target_tau` / `max_uin`: your call to ignore them is correct, and your reasoning is sound since honoring tau=0.9 would require Ma up to ~2 and would contradict the explicit `nu = uin*square_size/re` formula. Follow the case-dict `uin`. Note the deviation in the report so it is visible rather than buried.

One thing I do not want to see: no cd/cl numbers in the implementation report unless they came out of the actual full-grid runs. Give me the executed results, the diagnostics and validation output, and the six artifacts.

## 1) Input audit — `./data/task_input.json`

2190 bytes, **no BOM** (decodes as plain UTF-8; I will still open with `encoding="utf-8-sig"` per the brief). Top-level keys: `task_id`, `units`, `cases`, `required_outputs`, `diagnostic_probe_rule`. **5 cases**, all 10 required keys present in every case, no renames, no missing keys, no duplicate `case_id`s, all sizes/steps are true `int`s, `square_center` is a 2-int list in every case.

| case_id | nx | ny | uin | re | square_center | size | n_steps | warmup | every | samples |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| re12p56 | 540 | 180 | 0.03 | 12.56 | [180, 90] | 9 | 5000 | 1000 | 10 | 400 |
| re23p06 | 540 | 180 | 0.03 | 23.06 | [180, 90] | 9 | 5000 | 1000 | 10 | 400 |
| re35p96 | 540 | 180 | 0.03 | 35.96 | [180, 90] | 9 | 5000 | 1000 | 10 | 400 |
| st_re60p00 | 540 | 180 | 0.03 | 60.00 | [180, 90] | 9 | 5000 | 1000 | 10 | 400 |
| st_re80p00 | 540 | 180 | 0.03 | 80.00 | [180, 90] | 9 | 5000 | 1000 | 10 | 400 |

Flags:
- **Two extra keys per case**: `max_uin: 0.03`, `target_tau: 0.9`. `target_tau` **contradicts the mandated formula**: it would imply `uin` = 0.186–1.185, whereas the contract's `nu = uin*size/re` gives τ = 0.510–0.564. I use the contract formula and ignore `target_tau` (it is not in the list of keys the brief tells me to read).
- **No clipping**: solid is x∈[176,184], y∈[86,94] in all cases; `half=4`, well inside.
- **≥10 rows**: all give 400. But there is a trap — in Python `(-500) % 10 == 0`, so a bare `(step-warmup)%every==0` yields **500** rows (steps 0,10,…,990 included). The rule must be `step >= warmup_steps and (step-warmup) % every == 0`.
- All 5 cases share identical geometry and `uin`; **only τ differs**. So this is a pure τ/Re sweep.

## 2) Derived quantities

| case | nu | tau | Ma | blockage size/ny | inlet→body | body→outlet | x_probe | probe status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| re12p56 | 0.021497 | 0.56449 | 0.0520 | 5.0% | 176 | 355 | 198 | inside (+13 from TE) |
| re23p06 | 0.011709 | 0.53513 | 0.0520 | 5.0% | 176 | 355 | 198 | inside |
| re35p96 | 0.007508 | 0.52253 | 0.0520 | 5.0% | 176 | 355 | 198 | inside |
| st_re60p00 | 0.004500 | 0.51350 | 0.0520 | 5.0% | 176 | 355 | 198 | inside |
| st_re80p00 | 0.003375 | 0.51013 | 0.0520 | 5.0% | 176 | 355 | 198 | inside |

`x_probe=198` is inside for all cases (would need `cx+2*size ≥ nx`, i.e. ≥540, to clip — never happens). `min()` still applied for generality.

Timing context that drives stability/statistics: convective time inlet→outlet = 540/0.03 ≈ **18000 steps ≫ n_steps=5000**, so nothing ever reaches the outlet; acoustic crossing is nx/c_s ≈ 935 steps (~5 crossings). Wake establishment is L/u = 300 steps, so warmup=1000 (≈3.3 body lengths) is defensible, but the field is **not** fully developed by step 5000 — so `converged` will honestly report that rather than be tuned to be true.

## 3) Proposed approach

**Model**: D2Q9, single-relaxation-time BGK with ω=1/τ, τ from the mandated formula, c_s²=1/3, weights `[4,1,1,1,1,¼,¼,¼,¼]/9`. (Confirmed required: my first probe used `[4,1,1,1,1,1,2,2,2]/9`, which sums to 16/9 and destroys isotropy — it exploded at step ~50. That was my bug, not the physics.)

**Init**: `f = f_eq(ρ=1, u=(uin,0))` everywhere; inside the solid mask u is set to 0 (`ρ=1`). No ramping, no settling.

**Boundaries**: inlet = Zou/He velocity (`ux=uin, uy=0`) with ρ_b from known populations (mass-consistent); outlet = zero-gradient extrapolation of the 3 unknown populations (justified above: the outlet is causally irrelevant within 5000 steps); top/bottom = node-based bounce-back on the boundary rows using a saved post-collision snapshot.

**Force route — I disagree with your lean, and I can justify it.** I plan **momentum-exchange on the solid nodes** (Ladd-style, `F = 2·Σ_links e_i f_i^post-collision(x_fluid)`), *not* the loop integral:
1. For a **stationary** body the reference-frame/moving-body formulation contributes zero body-velocity terms and collapses onto the bounce-back exchange sum, so "moving frame" buys nothing here.
2. The loop integral drops the unsteady `∂/∂t ∫ρu` term. Our run is explicitly **not** steady (see timing above), so a steady-form loop integral is biased at exactly the steps we must sample.
3. Momentum exchange is *exactly* conservative by construction, which is what makes it robust to tau≈0.51.
4. It is the literal contract wording ("`Fx, Fy` come from the simulated solid-region momentum exchange").

**However**, I will compute the control-volume excess-flux loop integral (2–3 cells off the surface) as an independent **cross-check only**, reported in `method_summary`, not published in the CSVs. Your concern about "awkward bounces" is legitimate in a different way: the effective hydrodynamic surface sits at the solid-node boundary, so the effective area is a little larger than `9×9` while the contract normalizes by `9×9`. That is a known, accepted half-way/node-based BB bias, and the contract's fixed denominator means it stays in `cd`; I'll state it rather than paper over it.

## 4) Consequential assumptions & open uncertainties

- **`Fx, Fy` definition**: discrete momentum the fluid loses to the masked solid cells per step, summed over links from fluid neighbours into masked cells — not the (undefined) momentum content of solid cells.
- **No rescaling of `uin`**: it is the physical inlet speed, lattice `Ma = uin/√(1/3) = 0.0520`, worst-case observed `uin = 0.03` (identical in all 5 cases, and `max_uin` confirms 0.03). Comfortably under the Ma≲0.1 incompressibility target.
- **Sampling**: 0-based `step` = index of the LBM update; rows published iff `step >= warmup_steps and (step-warmup_steps) % sample_every == 0` → exactly 400 rows, `step` = 1000…4990. Exactly `n_steps` updates, zero pre/post steps.
- **`converged` (proposed, published in `method_summary`)**: with sampled `cd_s` (n=400), W=n//4=100, `m_last`=mean(cd[300:400]), `m_ref`=mean(cd[200:300]), `drift=|m_last-m_ref|/max(|m_last|,1e-12)`; `converged = (n>=10) AND all_finite AND drift <= 0.02`. If the wake is still drifting at 5000 steps this will report **False** for some cases — that is a finding, not a bug, and I will not tune the threshold to hide it.
- **`cd_mean`=mean(sampled cd); `cl_rms`=√mean(cl²)** (raw RMS, includes DC; mean(cl)≈0 by symmetry for the steady cases).
- **Open uncertainty (important, from probing)**: my throwaway prototypes reached plausible velocity fields but `cd`≈13–15 at Re=12.56, versus the literature order `cd`≈1–2 for a square cylinder at these Re. I traced and fixed four of my own bugs (weights, ω form `feq+(1−1/τ)f_neq` — I initially wrote `feq+f_neq/τ`, which amplifies by 1.96 instead of −0.96, the combined-roll neighbour mask, and the Zou/He diagonal coefficient which must be `(2/3)ρu_x`). A residual ~10× magnitude error is still unexplained, and two candidate causes remain: a leaky wall BC (a no-body run still showed |v|≈0.06 vs uin=0.03, and ρ drifting to ~0.44, so mass is not conserved through my outlet) and a force-normalization/double-counting issue. So I am **not** claiming a working solver yet. First implementation milestone is a no-body gate (u≡uin, v≈0, ρ≈const to O(Ma²), zero force) and a two-route force agreement gate before any CSV is written.

## 5) Runtime strategy

`numba` is **not installed** (ModuleNotFoundError) and the box is **single-core**, so pure vectorised NumPy is the only option. Measured cost on the real 540×180 grid: **10.4 ms/step** roll-based, 10.8 ms/step gather-scatter → 5000 steps ≈ **52 s/case**, **≈4.5 min for all 5 cases**; arrays are 7 MB each, so memory is trivial. Finiteness: per-step `np.isfinite` guard; if a field ever goes non-finite I switch that case to a regularized (ghost-mode-filtered) collision at the same τ and record it in `method_summary`, rather than emit NaN — the contract's "keep outputs finite" is satisfied by construction plus that fallback, never by post-hoc clipping. No settling, no extra warmup, no relabelled samples.

No `analysis.py` or results file written this turn, as requested.

Comprobaciones:
- **Muestreo**: con índice de paso 0-based (s=0…4999) y `s≥warmup`, `(s-warmup)%10==0` → s=1000…4990 → **400 muestras por caso** (≥10 ✔, 2000 filas totales en `fluid_force_series.csv`). Con índice 1-based (t=1…5000) serían 400–401. Propongo **0-based, 400 filas**, y columnas CSV en el orden de entrada.
- **Clip**: `half=9//2=4` → 176…184 y 86…94, 81 celdas, dentro de 0…539 / 0…179 → **sin recorte** en ningún caso. `x_probe = min(539, 180+18) = 198` para los 5 casos (13 celdas tras el borde de salida). Bloqueo = 9/180 = 5%.
- **Riesgo de estabilidad**: τ−0.5 = 0.064, 0.035, 0.023, 0.0135, **0.0101** → los tres casos de mayor Re están muy cerca del límite BGK (ν_latt→0). Empíricamente confirmé que es un riesgo real (ver §2).
- **Discrepancia de metadatos**: `target_tau=0.9` es **incompatible** con la fórmula del contrato (τ=0.9 ⇒ ν=0.1333 ⇒ Re≈2.0 con uin=0.03, o uin≈0.89 con Re=60, Ma∼1.6). Usaré la fórmula del contrato (τ tabulada arriba) e ignoro `target_tau`/`max_uin`; lo dejo documentado en `method_summary`.
- Entorno: python 3.12, numpy 2.4.4, pandas 3.0.2, **numba NO está instalado** (aunque el contrato lo permite) y **solo hay 1 core** (`nproc=1`). → implemento **numpy puro vectorizado**, sin rama numba (no puedo probar código que no se ejecuta aquí).

## 2) Enfoque LBM propuesto (con evidencia de prototipos ya ejecutados)

**Esquema**: D2Q9 BGK. `f[i]` shape (9,ny,nx) float64; colisión fusionada con streaming (buffer único) ≈4.5–8 ms/paso; versión 2-buffer (necesaria para el BB "pull") ≈8–11 ms/paso. Medido de extremo a extremo: **5 casos × 5000 pasos = 110–120 s** (variante rápida) / ~2.5–4 min (variante pull). Nota operativa: las llamadas a shell de este entorno se cortan a 120 s, así que la ejecución final irá en segundo plano (`nohup`) con sondeo, o con `timeout_seconds` mayor.

**Sólido (sin-slip)**: máscara exacta del contrato; **bounce-back a nivel de enlace en formulación "pull"**: para todo nodo fluido `x` y dirección `j` cuyo vecino aguas arriba `x−c_j` es sólido, `f_j(x,t+1)=f_{j̄}^*(x,t)` (población post-colisión propia invertida). Esto es lo que probé que **conserva masa** en la interfaz. Inicialmente usé la variante "escribir en el nodo sólido", que **no** conserva masa (el "slab" sólido actúa como sumidero de masa/cantidad de movimiento) y producía un arrastre espurio: la cambié tras detectarlo.

**Influo/efluzo/paredes** (esto costó 3 fallos de inestabilidad localizados, todos reproducidos):
- Prueba empírica con cuerpo a τ=0.5101: **Zou–He de velocidad clásico revienta** (paso 279, en x=0); ZH con ρ fijada revienta (paso 581); la **condición de cierre exacta en v** para f6/f7 también revienta. En cambio, **inlet de velocidad de equilibrio/NEEM** (`f_i = f_i^eq(ρ=1,u=(uin,0)) + [f_i(x=1) − f_i^eq(ρ,u)(x=1)]` para i∈{1,6,7}) es estable en los 5 casos. Propongo **NEEM en el influo** (con ρ=1, u=(uin,0)), **extrapolación de gradiente cero en el efluzo** y **paredes superior/inferior libres de deslizamiento (espejo)**. Documento que ZH se probó y es inestable a τ→0.51: esto es física del esquema, no un "hack" de relajación.
- Campo inicial determinista exactamente como pide el contrato: `u=(uin,0)`, `f=f_eq(ρ=1,u)`, sin pre-settling; transitorio de arranque incluido en el warmup de 1000 pasos del contrato.

**Fuerza**: acumularé por enlace de interfaz la transferencia discreta de cantidad de movimiento
`Fx += Σ_enlaces 2·c_ix·f_i^*(x_f)`, `Fy += Σ_enlaces 2·c_iy·f_i^*(x_f)` (post-colisión, mismo nivel temporal; con BB espejo en punto medio la pared devuelve `f_i^*`, de ahí el factor 2), normalizado **exactamente** como `cd = Fx/(0.5·uin²·D)`, `cl = Fy/(0.5·uin²·D)`, D=`square_size`. Validación interna (no va a los CSV, solo al log): integral de contorno del tensor de flujo de momento discreto `Π_αβ=Σc_αc_βf_i` y balance global de flujo en influo/efluzo — en el prototipo pull ME(2q)=3.96 vs balance global 4.49 (≈13%, con flujo aún transitorio). `cl_rms` = RMS de `cl` en la ventana de muestreo; `cd_mean` = media de `cd` en esa ventana.

**Perfiles**: centerline = `ux[:, x]` para x=0…nx−1 en la fila `y=cy=90` (n filas = nx ✔); dentro de la máscara se escribe `u=0.0` (velocidad del sólido) para mantener finitud. Transversal en `x_probe=198`: `u=ux[:,198]`, `v=uy[:,198]` para y=0…ny−1 (ny filas ✔), con 0 en celdas sólidas.

**Finitud**: sin trucos de relajación; chequeos duros por caso (todos `isfinite`, `rho∈[0.9,1.1]`, `|u|<0.3`) y *fail-fast* con diagnóstico de la posición del primer `NaN`. Ya detecté con esto dos bugs reales (stencil D2Q9 mal escrito y BB desplazado una celda) y una inestabilidad de BC — sin esos chequeos habrían pasado como "resultados".

**`converged`**: criterio publicado en `method_summary`, calculado con los datos, no hardcodeado: `converged = True` ssi (a) todas las muestras finitas, (b) deriva de la media de `cd` entre la primera y la segunda mitad de la ventana `|mean₁−mean₂|/|mean| < 0.02`, y (c) estacionariedad de `cl`: `rms(cl)` de la 2ª mitad dentro de [0.5×, 2×] de la 1ª mitad. Con el transitorio de arranque del contrato (5000 pasos = solo ~17 tiempos convectivos D/uin) espero que esto dé **False** en la mayoría de casos — que es información honesta, no un fallo.

## 3) Riesgo científico abierto y decisiones que necesito de ti

Hallazgo incómodo y central: en todos mis prototipos el **cd resultante es prácticamente independiente de Re** (3.83–4.00 para Re=5→20; 4.40–4.43 para Re=12.56→80) e **idéntico para un cuadrado de 9 y de 18 celdas** (3.85 vs 3.90), y **no aparece desprendimiento de vórtices** ni con 20000 pasos (t*=67). Consecuencias probables, en orden de sospecha:
1. **Simetría exacta preservada**: el C.I. es exactamente simétrico y el esquema respeta la simetría, así que el modo antisimétrico inestable no tiene semilla → el estado simétrico-metaestable persiste. Casi seguro contribuye; se arregla con una semilla minúscula y documentada (**D3**).
2. **Enlaces diagonales en la BB** (esquina "staircase"): entran con peso completo en la ME y en el área proyectada efectiva (efecto enorme con D=9). Sensibilidad cuantificable (**D2**).
3. **ν efectiva sin calibrar**: mi test de Poiseuille dio ratios absurdos (u_máx numérico ≪ teórico) pero el test estaba contaminado por las columnas x de contorno; necesito un test limpio (Taylor–Green periódico) para verificar `ν_eff=(τ−0.5)/3`.

No quiero entregarte cd's "bonitos" sin esta validación, así que propongo un **umbral de validación antes de la corrida final**: V1 Taylor–Green (ν_eff), V2 Poiseuille periódico-x con forzamiento de Guo (no-slip + ν), V3 cilindro cuadrado Re=10/20/40 con semilla (tendencia decreciente de cd y Strouhal≈0.13 arriba de Re≈22). Coste estimado 10–15 min de ejecución.

**Decisiones que necesito (proposta marcada con ★):**
- **D1 fuerza**: ★ME "pull" 2Σc·f* como definición oficial + contorno/integral global como cross-check en el log | solo integral de contorno.
- **D2 enlaces diagonales**: ★incluirlos (conservación de masa) y reportar como sensibilidad la variante solo-cardinal | solo cardinales.
- **D3 semilla de simetría**: ★ninguna (respetar literalmente el C.I. determinista del contrato) y reportar el flujo simétrico transitorio como resultado | perturbación documentada ~1e−4·uin en v cerca del cuerpo (cambia `cl_rms` cualitativamente).
- **D4 paredes**: ★free-slip espejo (bloquea menos el wake) | no-slip.
- **D5 influo**: ★NEEM/equilibrio (ZH probado inestable a τ=0.51).
- **D6 converged**: la definición (a)-(c) de arriba ✔/ajustar umbrales.
- **D7 convenciones**: paso 0-based (400 filas), orden de filas = orden de entrada, `x=0…nx−1`, `y=0…ny−1`, sólido con `u=v=0`.
- **D8 `fluid_report.json`**: ★`units="lattice units (dimensionless)"`, `cd_mean_avg` = media **no ponderada** de los 5 `cd_mean`, `task_id` = el del input, `method_summary` texto con esquema, BCs, definición de fuerza, criterio de convergencia y las salvedades (target_tau inconsistente, sin semilla, BB a media celda ⇒ longitud efectiva ~10).

Asumo para continuar: la fórmula de τ del contrato manda sobre `target_tau`; "true steps" = conteo 0-based de actualizaciones; el cuadriculado es cuadrado y `c_s=1/√3`; no hay obligación de concordar con literatura (el contrato fija la ventana corta). Nada escrito en disco todavía: no hay `analysis.py` ni `results/`; todos los prototipos se ejecutaron en memoria vía heredocs (y `/tmp` no persiste en este entorno).

¡Buen trabajo de inspección y prototipado! El plan es sólido y defensible: D2Q9 BGK, bounce-back "pull" a nivel de enlace (conservación de masa demostrada), inlet NEEM con ZH descartado por evidencia empírica (no por preferencia), extrapolación de gradiente cero en eflujo, ventana de muestreo literal del contrato y *fail-fast* sobre finitud. Apruebo el enfoque y las decisiones D1, D2, D4, D5, D6, D7, D8 tal como las propones, con los siguientes cinco fijamientos metodológicos antes de que escribas nada en disco.

1) τ del contrato manda. Confirmo tu lectura: `tau = 0.5 + 3*uin*D/re` es la única fuente válida; `target_tau=0.9` / `max_uin=0.03` son metadatos incompatibles y se documentan como tales en `method_summary`, sin "arreglarlos" alterando ν. Reporta τ por caso tal como está en la tabla (0.56449 … 0.510125).

2) D3 la cambio: sí quiero semilla de ruptura de simetría, pero **dentro del campo inicial, no durante la corrida**. El contrato dice "start from your deterministic initial field" y prohíbe pre-settling/extra-warmup, no la forma del campo inicial. Un C.I. exactamente simétrico es un estado simétrico inestable sin excitación del modo antisimétrico, así que `cl_rms ≡ 0` y la señal de sustentación sería vacía, y tu propio síntoma (cd plano en Re=12.56→80) coincide con eso. Condición exacta que acepto: perturbación determinista y fija (sin RNG, o con semilla numérica dura), de amplitud del orden de 1e-4·uin en `v`, aplicada solo al campo inicial `f=f_eq(ρ=1, u)` en una región localizada cerca del cuerpo; cero perturbación adicional en cada paso, cero forzamiento posterior, cero filtrado de muestras. Decláralo explícitamente en `method_summary` como parte del C.I. (amplitud, forma, región) para que nadie lo lea como warmup oculto. Si aun así no aparece shedding en 5000 pasos, repórtalo como resultado: la ventana del contrato son solo ~17 tiempos convectivos D/uin y puede no cubrir la rampa lineal de la estela绝对; eso es información, no un fallo.

3) Validación ν_eff: exige solo **V1 (Taylor–Green periódico)** como umbral obligatorio antes de la corrida final — es barato y responde la única duda que contamina todo lo demás (`ν_eff=(τ−0.5)/3` con la formulación pull y tus BC). V2 y V3 (cilindro cuadrado con shedding/St≈0.13) quedan **opcionales**: ejecútalas solo si V1 pasa y el tiempo lo permite, y si lo haces, lanza la corrida en segundo plano como propones para esquivar el corte de 120 s. Reporta el resultado de V1 (decaimiento medido vs teórico, desviación %) en el log y una línea en `method_summary`. No uses V1 para recalibrar τ.

4) Fuerza: apruebo ME "pull" `2Σc·f*` como definición oficial con la integral de contorno y el balance global como cross-check en log, **pero quiero la discrepancia cuantificada por caso**, no solo en el prototipo: añade al log (no a los CSV) `cd_ME`, `cd_contour`, `cd_global_balance` y el % de desviación en la media de la ventana de las 5 corridas. Con D=9 y enlaces diagonales a peso completo, un 13–20% es sistemático y el lector tiene derecho a verlo. Mantén la normalización exacta `cd=Fx/(0.5·uin²·D)`.

5) Estabilidad y honestidad: en τ=0.5101 y 0.5135 no acepto ningún ajuste de relajación, filtro ni "settling" si algo revienta. Si aparece NaN/Inf en la configuración final 540×180, primero intenta solo variantes de BC de salida/inlet ya validadas sin cuerpo (NEEM en eflujo en lugar de gradiente cero), documenta el cambio, y si persiste, deja el caso marcado en `converged=False` y descríbelo en `method_summary` en vez de enmascararlo. Acepto que `converged` salga `False` en la mayoría de casos con tu criterio (a)-(c) — es el criterio correcto dado que el contrato fuerza a incluir el transitorio de arranque en la ventana de promedio; no endurezcas ni suavices los umbrales a posteriori para cosmeticar el flag.

Convenciones confirmadas: paso 0-based (400 filas por caso, 2000 en total), orden de filas = orden de entrada, `x_probe=198`, `u=v=0` dentro de la máscara en perfiles, `units="lattice units (dimensionless)"`, `cd_mean_avg` = media no ponderada de los 5 `cd_mean`, numpy puro (sin rama numba inexecutable).

Ahora sí: escribe el `./analysis.py` completo y ejecutable (sin placeholders), corre V1 y luego los 5 casos con la ventana exacta, y genera los seis artefactos en `./results/` con los nombres y cabeceras exactos del contrato. En tu siguiente entrega quiero: resultados por caso (`tau`, `cd_mean`, `cl_rms`, `converged`, nº de muestras), el diagnóstico de convergencia de las tres condiciones, el cross-check de fuerza por caso, el resultado de V1, cualquier caso con inestabilidad o sin shedding, y el `method_summary` final tal como queda escrito en el JSON. Nada de promedios extendidos ni pasos extra: solo lo que produzca la corrida.

## 1. Input inspection (`data/task_input.json`)

- 2190 bytes, **no BOM** (starts with `{`); I will still decode with `utf-8-sig` (handles both).
- Top-level keys: `task_id="fluid-square-wake-2d-001"`, `units="dimensionless"`, `cases` (**5 cases**), `required_outputs`, `diagnostic_probe_rule`.
- Per case the 10 contract fields are identical in kind, plus **two extra fields I will ignore**: `max_uin=0.03`, `target_tau=0.9`.

| case_id | nx | ny | uin | re | square_center | D | n_steps | warmup | every | nu=uin·D/re | tau=0.5+3nu | solid x | solid y | x_probe | samples |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| re12p56 | 540 | 180 | 0.03 | 12.56 | (180,90) | 9 | 5000 | 1000 | 10 | 0.0214968 | **0.564491** | 176–184 | 86–94 | 198 | 400 |
| re23p06 | 540 | 180 | 0.03 | 23.06 | (180,90) | 9 | 5000 | 1000 | 10 | 0.0117086 | **0.535128** | 176–184 | 86–94 | 198 | 400 |
| re35p96 | 540 | 180 | 0.03 | 35.96 | (180,90) | 9 | 5000 | 1000 | 10 | 0.0075083 | **0.522525** | 176–184 | 86–94 | 198 | 400 |
| st_re60p00 | 540 | 180 | 0.03 | 60.0 | (180,90) | 9 | 5000 | 1000 | 10 | 0.0045000 | **0.513500** | 176–184 | 86–94 | 198 | 400 |
| st_re80p00 | 540 | 180 | 0.03 | 80.0 | (180,90) | 9 | 5000 | 1000 | 10 | 0.0033750 | **0.510125** | 176–184 | 86–94 | 198 | 400 |

Regime flags:
- **All five cases are near-τ=0.5 BGK** (τ−0.5 ∈ [0.010, 0.064]) — i.e. low-viscosity, marginal-stability BGK. I explicitly verified stability (see §3 evidence).
- **Input is internally inconsistent**: `target_tau=0.9` cannot coexist with `re` under the contract formula (τ=0.9 ⇒ Re≈2.03). I follow the contract (`nu=uin*D/re`), so τ=0.510–0.564, and treat `target_tau`/`max_uin` as stale metadata.
- **Very coarse obstacle: D=9 cells** (10 effective with halfway bounce-back), Ma=0.03, blockage D/ny=5%.
- **No clipping**: mask 176–184 × 86–94 sits fully inside 0–539 × 0–179; nothing touches a boundary, so the clipping rule never fires (still implemented).
- **Geometry is 0.5 cells off-centre**: `half=9//2=4` ⇒ body spans y=86…94, centre 90, while the channel centre is y=89.5 ⇒ a half-cell asymmetry ⇒ small but genuinely non-zero `cl`/`cl_rms` even at low Re.
- Fetch distances are generous: inlet→leading edge 176 (≈19.5D), outlet margin 355 (≈39D); `x_probe=198` (never clamped).

## 2. Output volume under `(step-warmup)%every==0, step>warmup`
With 1-based step index (step = number of completed updates), samples are 1010, 1020, …, 5000 ⇒ **400 rows per case, 2000 total** (≥10 ✓). Per case: centerline 540 rows (2700 total), transverse 180 rows (900 total), summary 1 row (5 total). Case-id sets identical across files.

## 3. Proposed scheme — with what I already measured

**Lattice/collision.** D2Q9 + BGK, κ=τ, ν=c_s²(τ−½) ⇒ exactly the contract's τ. Adequate because Ma=0.03 (compressible-error O(Ma²)≈1e-3) and Re is low. Verified: equilibrium moments exact to 1e-16 (M0,M1,Π), acoustic pulse decays cleanly, mass conserved by streaming.

**Two bugs my probes caught (worth recording as validation gates):**
- `f_post = feq + ω(f−feq)` vs the correct `f − ω(f−feq)`: the wrong form is *anti*-relaxation for ω>1 (all our τ<1) and passes every fixed-point/conservation test, yet blows up any non-uniform field. Fixed form is stable; **acceptance test = decaying acoustic pulse + frozen uniform plug**.
- D2Q9 opposite-index array must be `[0,3,4,1,2,7,8,5,6]`; a shifted variant silently reflects into wrong directions.

**Solid/BC.** Exact contract mask (clipped), stored as a boolean; **simple halfway bounce-back**: for every wet node x and direction q with x+e_q solid, after streaming set f_{q̄}(x)=f_q^post(x). The wet set = {nodes not in mask}; this link set provably covers every solid→fluid leak path. Effective body = 10×10 (documented in `method_summary`).

**Channel BCs.** Zou–He velocity inlet at x=0 (u=(uin,0)); zero-gradient extrapolation at x=nx−1; **specular (free-slip) top/bottom**. Chosen because (a) input hints `max_uin=uin` ⇒ plug free stream, (b) the contract normalises by 0.5·uin²·D (unbounded-channel convention), (c) my full-way no-slip walls blew up when combined with ZH at the corners, while free-slip is stable and preserves plug flow.

**Force (validated).** Momentum exchange over boundary links, `F_α = Σ 2 e_{qα} f_q^post(x)`; `cd=Fx/(0.5·uin²·D)`. Evidence: this equals the *exact* discrete fluid-momentum loss per step (verified |ΔP_fluid + F| = 0 to machine precision) and gives Fx>0. I tested the textbook "Ladd/mixed" variant `Σ e_q(f_q^post+f_q^pre)`: it gives cd≈9.9–11.5 (absurd at τ≈0.5) → **rejected**. Outlet variant is irrelevant to results (extrapolation cd=3.109 vs characteristic 3.093) → keep the simple one.

**Stability/physics evidence (540×180, exact τ):** all τ from 0.51–0.9 stable ≥3000 steps; 5000-step runs finite, ρ∈[0.998,1.002], inlet/outlet flux 16.16/16.40 (mass drift +0.04%), cd≈2.9 (re12p56, settling from 4.7), cd≈0.9–1.6 with cl oscillating ±0.1 (st_re80p00, shedding present). So magnitudes are O(1) and the qualitative Re trend in `cl_rms` (0.019 vs 0.176) is right; **absolute cd is over-predicted at low Re (≈2–3 vs literature ≈1.3–1.9)** — inherent to a 9-cell body + simple BB + 5% blockage + a window still containing startup acoustics (wall acoustic period ≈624 steps explains the residual oscillation). I will not tune this away since the time window is fixed by contract.

**Sampling.** Centerline = row at `y=cy=90` (body centreline), all x; cells inside the mask get `u=0.0` (solid). Transverse at `x_probe=min(nx−1, cx+2D)=198`, all y (all fluid; nearest body cell is x=184).

**Performance.** **numba is not installed** (import fails) and the box has **1 CPU / 2 GB**. Pure numpy, (Q,nx,ny) layout, `np.tensordot` for moments + fused equilibrium (naive multiply-sum costs 19 ms/step; tensordot ≈10 ms): measured **10.5–12.4 ms/step ⇒ ~52–62 s per case ⇒ ~5 min for all 5**, peak memory ~30 MB. Guards: `np.divide(..., where=rho>1e-12)`, assert `max|u|<0.35`, per-100-step `np.isfinite` check that raises rather than writing NaN.

## 4. Assumptions / open questions (proposed defaults)
1. `square_center` = **(x,y)** → (180,90). 2. Centerline y-line = **cy=90**. 3. In-solid centerline cells → **u=0.0**. 4. Walls = **free-slip** (alternative: no-slip+ZH-compatible corner, costs stability). 5. Inlet = **uniform plug uin** (not Poiseuille). 6. Initial field = **ρ=1, u=(uin,0) everywhere, no pre-settling**. 7. `cd_mean`/`cl_rms` = **arithmetic mean and √mean(cl²) over exactly the 400 sampled rows**. 8. `converged` (explicit, not tuned): True iff ≥10 samples, all finite, max|u|<0.35 in the last 500 steps, and |mean(cd 2nd half)−mean(cd 1st half)| < 0.25·|mean(cd)|; this may honestly yield False for some cases. 9. Step index **1-based** (sample 1010…5000). 10. `units`/`task_id` copied from input; `cd_mean_avg` = mean of the 5 cd_mean; **may I add extra keys** (per-case nu/tau/x_probe) to `fluid_report.json`? 11. Sign: F = momentum **given to the body** (drag positive). 12. `_scratch/` probe scripts will be deleted before final delivery.

square_center is (x,y) with half=square_size//2 and a half-open x/y range, as stated in the contract.

План в целом принимаю, работать можно. Но три момента догони до того, как назовёшь результат — это не новые требования, а закрытие дыр, которые ты сам же оставил.

1) Численная обусловленность closed-form. У тебя r_amp ∈ [0.001, 0.333]. В стандартной закрытой формуле на n_eff есть члены вида 1/|r| и 1/|r|² (через cos φr), т.е. при r≈0.001 это 10⁶ в знаменателе и мусор в n при любом шуме фазы. Значит closed-form годится только как инициализация, а не как источник финальных величин: финальная n/z должна идти из подгонки прямой модели к комплексным t и r (scipy.optimize, наименьшие квадраты по амплитуде и unwrapped-фазе), с явным guard на |r|<порог и с проверкой пассивности |t|²+|r|²≤1 (покажи максимум этой величины по образцам — если где-то >1, это отдельная проблема нормировки, и её надо назвать, а не проглотить).

2) Критерий negative-index band ты так и не зафиксировал. Дай до подгонки, цифрами: по какой величине полоса (Re(n_eff)<0 или Re(ε)<0 И Re(μ)<0), верхний порог по Im (потери), минимальная ширина в нм и минимальное число точек, и считается ли полоса «robust» только если она есть в обеих ветках — у извлечения из closed-form и у выбранной семьи. Полоса, которая живёт только в одном из двух, — не полоса. И назови это заранее, чтобы не подгонять порог под красивый ответ.

3) Маппинг геометрия→параметры семьи. λ_mag ≈ 2·L_rod — это твоё допущение, а не факт из данных, так и маркируй его в conclusion.txt. Порядок работ держи такой: сначала поштучное извлечение по 6 calibration-образцам, потом низкоразмерная физическая связь (несколько параметров семьи против rod_length / gap / spacer / substrate_index), и вот именно этот маппинг проверяется leave-one-sample-out — не сама подгонка по своему образцу. H1 с rod_length=313.6 нм вне calibration-диапазона: явно посчитай и покажи extrapalation-distance (насколько он вне диапазона в единицах шага сетки длин волн / в долях L_rod) и признай экстраполяцию экстраполяцией в выводе, а не «предсказанием». Если BIC говорит за dual_resonance_plus_substrate_shift, убедись, что «substrate shift» привязан к substrate_index, а не выродился в свободный сдвиг на образец — иначе это не физика, а 6 бесплатных параметров.

Жёсткие рамки, которые не обсуждаются: одна выбранная семья объясняет всё четыре артефакта и её label (electric_only / electric_magnetic_dual_resonance / dual_resonance_plus_substrate_shift) присутствует в model_comparison, calibration_retrieval, heldout_prediction и negative_index_summary; held-out кривые — только прямой прогон выбранной семьи на заданной сетке 126 точек (1236.4491–1725.991 нм), никаких интерполяторов и никаких сурогатов «геометрия→кривая»; zero-width no-band — ровно процитированная конвенция, пустая полоса = нулевая ширина, без «почти полос»; схемные имена колонок — дословно из retrieval_notes.md.

В deliverable дополнительно принеси: число параметров каждой семьи и AIC/BIC в model_comparison, LOso RMSE отдельно по амплитуде и по фазе (обмотку считай wrapped-difference, а не сырой вычет), и в conclusion.txt — выбранный label, две-три причины отбора, и отдельно список того, что осталось допущением (нормировка на воздух, эффективная толщина без фактора заполнения, λ_mag↔L_rod, уровень шума). Не приукрашивай: если три семьи различаются в пределах шума так, что выбор неустойчив, — скажи это прямо в выводе и укажи, какой критерий решил.

Работай.

## 1) Inspección de `data/` (solo lectura; sin modelar)

**`data/calibration_samples.csv`** — 6 muestras × 8 columnas:
`sample_id, split, rod_length_nm, rod_width_nm, gap_nm, spacer_thickness_nm, substrate_index, slab_thickness_nm`
- Unidades: todas las geométricas en nm (`rod_length_nm`, `rod_width_nm`, `gap_nm`, `spacer_thickness_nm`, `slab_thickness_nm`); `substrate_index` adimensional.
- Rangos calibración: L 242.32–286.71, W 79.80–117.07, gap 36.64–74.43, spacer 16.38–39.31 nm; `substrate_index` ∈ {1.00, 1.22, 1.35, 1.46}.
- **`slab_thickness_nm` = 132.9091 nm, idéntico en las 6 de calibración y en las 3 held-out** (dato confirmado, no supuesto).

**`data/calibration_optics.csv`** — 756 filas = 6 muestras × 126 λ: `sample_id, split, wavelength_nm, t_amp, r_amp, phi_t_rad, phi_r_rad`.
- Mide **R y T en amplitud + fase** (no hay absorbancia A explícita; A = 1−|t|²−|r|² derivable).
- Rejilla de λ: 1236.4491 → 1725.9910 nm, paso ~3.9163 nm, **idéntica (byte a byte) para las 6 muestras** → se puede trabajar en la rejilla dada con merge/index, sin interpolar.
- **NaN: 0 en todas las columnas.** Energéticamente pasivo: max(|t|²+|r|²) ≈ 0.915 ≤ 1 → hay pérdida real en todo el rango.
- Fases en valor principal envueltas a [−π, π): `phi_r` sí salta (12 saltos > 3 rad entre puntos vecinos en el conjunto → hay wrapping real); `phi_t` no presenta saltos.
- Amplitudes: min(r_amp) ≈ 0.001 y 29.6 % de puntos con r_amp < 0.05 → **la fórmula clásica de Smith (arccos con división por |r||t|) está mal condicionada aquí** (y ambigüedad de rama de ±π). Esto empuja a ajuste de modelo directo frente a a ajuste de modelo directo frente a inversión algebraica.
- Sonda rápida de signo: con d = 132.9091 nm, φ_t/(k₀d) va de ~+2.10 (1236 nm) a ~+0.68 (1726 nm) decreciente. Es decir, **el signo de la convención de fase decide si el índice sale ~+2 o ~−2** → hay que fijarlo empíricamente (ver plan).

**`data/heldout_samples.csv`** — 3 muestras (H1, H2, H3), **solo geometría** (mismas 8 columnas que calibración, `split=heldout`); no pide ni trae óptica. Hay que generar para cada una las 126 λ completas de t, r, φ_t, φ_r, n_real, n_imag, z_real, z_imag.
- **Extrapolación**: H1 y H3 superan el `rod_length_nm` máximo de calibración (313.55 y 296.16 vs 286.71) y H1 está por debajo del gap mínimo (33.19 vs 36.64); H2 supera el `rod_width_nm` máximo (118.78 vs 117.07). Los `substrate_index` held-out (1.00, 1.35, 1.46) sí están dentro del set de calibración.

**Notas de entorno (importante):** en este workspace **matplotlib NO está instalado y no hay red** (`pip install matplotlib` falla por DNS); numpy 2.4.4, pandas 3.0.2, scipy 1.16.0 OK. Ver incertidumbres.

**No hay ninguna fórmula de recuperación ni convención de signo temporal (e^{±iωt}) fijada en notes** — solo el intervalo de envoltura [−π, π) y que d = `slab_thickness_nm` es el grosor efectivo. Tampoco hay regla de desambiguación de rama. (Aquí notes no contradice tu mensaje.)

**Idea central:** invertir por *ajuste directo de un modelo hacia delante*, no por inversión algebraica. Parametrizar la capa homogénea efectiva con permitividad/permeabilidad de tipo Lorentz/Drude y ajustar los **números físicos** de cada muestra a (|t|, |r|, φ_t, φ_r) simultáneamente; luego transferir *esos parámetros físicos* al held-out con una regresión lineal de baja dimensión sobre(features geométricas con motivación física — prohibida la interpolación de espectros).

Esquema de pasos:
1. **Preparación**: merge óptica+geometría, rejilla común de 126 λ; construir `t = t_amp·e^{iφ_t}`, `r = r_amp·e^{iφ_r}`; residual de fase envuelto módulo 2π (nunca `unwrap` como objetivo → evita el artefacto de ramas).
2. **Determinación de la convención de signo/rama**: probar ambas convenciones de propagación (t ~ e^{±i n k₀d}) y fijar la que dé parámetros físicos pasivos y estables (`n_imag ≥ 0` con la convención temporal elegida, espectros suaves, |z| coherente con las amplitudes). Esta decisión se documenta en `conclusion.txt` porque determina si hay banda negativa.
3. **Familias candidatas** (etiquetas exactas de notes):
   - `electric_only`: ε(ω) Lorentz/Drude (ε∞, ω_e, F_e, γ_e), μ = 1 → 4 params/muestra.
   - `electric_magnetic_dual_resonance`: ε(ω) y μ(ω) ambas Lorentz → 8 params/muestra.
   - `dual_resonance_plus_substrate_shift`: las 8 + término de carga dieléctrica del sustrato (Lorentz–Lorenz ~ (n_sub²−1)/(n_sub²+2)) sobre ε∞ y/o desplazamiento común de ω_e, ω_m → 9–10 params/muestra.
   - Forward model: matriz de transferencia de lámina de grosor 132.9091 nm + Fresnel → t, r, n = √(εμ) (rama pasiva), z = √(μ/ε).
4. **Objetivo y regularización**: mínimos cuadrados ponderados (`scipy.optimize.least_squares`) sobre [Δ|t|, Δ|r|, Δφ envueltos, y coherencia de energía]; pesos equivalentes en amplitud y fase; bounds físicos (ω>0, F≥0, γ>0, ε∞≥1), penalización de suavidad/rigidez frente a calibración de parámetros mal determinados, y **multi-start** por muestra para evitar mínimos locales de rama.
5. **Comparación y selección**: `calibration_rmse` (ajuste in-sample), `crossval_rmse` por **leave-one-sample-out** (5 muestras → mapa de transferencia → predecir la 6ª; mide transferencia real, no bondad), `phase_consistency_rmse` (solo residuales de fase envueltos), `num_parameters`. Regla de preferencia explícita y determinista: ganar por LOSO con margen, si no la familia más simple (penalización tipo BIC). Esta es la familia seleccionada que **produce también** calibration_retrieval, heldout_prediction y negative_index_summary.
6. **Transferencia held-out física (no interpolación)**: ajuste global de θ_s ≈ A·f(geometría) con f = {1, L, L/gap o W·L/celda, exp(−gap/λ_c), (n_sub²−1)/(n_sub²+2)}, ridge pequeño; θ̂(H) → forward model → 126 λ completas de t/r/φ/n/z. Sin `interp1d`, `np.interp`, `Rbf`, `PolynomialFeatures`, KNN, scikit-learn; alineación solo por merge/index en la rejilla dada.
7. **Resumen de banda negativa**: sobre el `n_real` recuperado en la rejilla dada, regla literal de notes (primer/último punto con n_real < 0). Compuerta de robustez documentada: se reporta banda solo si existen ≥ 3 puntos consecutivos con n_real < −tol (tol ≈ 0.02) y la banda se mantiene bajo perturbation LOSO/bootstrap; si no, **convención de cero ancho** con `min_n_real` y su λ. Incluye las 6 de calibración y las 3 held-out (columna `split`).
8. **Salidas**: los 4 CSV con esquemas exactos, `retrieval_diagnostics.png`, `conclusion.txt` (familia elegida, parámetros físicos, banda, limitaciones).

**Diagnóstico gráfico** (`results/retrieval_diagnostics.png`), 6 paneles: (1) |t| y |r| datos vs ajuste por muestra; (2) φ_t y φ_r datos vs ajuste (desenvueltos solo para visualización, puntos = datos envueltos); (3) n_real y n_imag vs λ de las 6 de calibración + 3 predichas, con línea n=0 y banda negativa sombreada; (4) z_real/z_imag; (5) barras calibration vs LOSO RMSE por familia (evidencia de selección); (6) dispersión parámetro físico vs geometría con la recta de transferencia y puntos held-out marcados como extrapolación.

## 3) Supuestos e incertidumbres

**Confirmado por los ficheros:** d = 132.9091 nm idéntico en todas las muestras; 126 λ comunes; 0 NaN; pasividad energética (max |t|²+|r|² ≈ 0.915); held-out solo geometría; 3 held-out; rangos geométricos y de sustrato arriba indicados; notes no fija convención de signo temporal ni fórmula de recuperación.

**Supuestos míos (a validar durante el ajuste):**
- El medio incidente es aire/aire (n=1) y la lámina se modela como medio efectivo homogéneo e isótropo; **incidencia normal, canal único de polarización** (no hay en datos información de ángulo, polarización ni canales cruzados). - Que la pérdida es volumétrica (parte imaginaria de ε/μ) y no solo dispersión/radiación; de lo contrario la passividad se impondría artificialmente.
- 6 muestras de calibración y 3 held-out es un muestreo pequeño: el error de selección por LOSO tiene varianza alta; la regla de preferencia será conservadora (prefiere familia más simple salvo mejora clara).

**Incertidumbre de entorno:** matplotlib no está disponible aquí y no hay red. Propuesta: `analysis.py` usa matplotlib si está disponible (el runtime declarado del benchmark lo incluye) y si no, un **escritor PNG propio determinista (numpy + zlib/struct)** con el mismo contenido de paneles, de modo que `results/retrieval_diagnostics.png` se genere siempre y yo pueda verificarlo localmente. Escribe ya `analysis.py` y los artefactos. Cuatro precisiones de método, y una duda resuelta:

**1) Signo/rama: usa un árbitro independiente de la propia fase.** La convención temporal no la fija notes, así que no la elijas solo por "estabilidad". Criterio determinista y verificable: `Im(n)` derivada de la atenuación de amplitud (escala `|t| ≈ exp(-Im(n)·k0·d)` módulo pérdidas Fresnel) NO depende del signo de `φ_t`; es por tanto el testador. Fija la convención y la rama `m` que den simultáneamente (a) `Im(n) ≥ 0` en toda la rejilla, (b) magnitud de `Im(n)` coherente con la que implica `|t|`, y (c) menor residual de fase envuelto. Reporta en `conclusion.txt` la tabla de las combinaciones probadas (signo × rama 0/±1) con esos tres números, y el valor de `min_n_real` global. Con 6 muestras tienen que dar todas la misma convención; si no coinciden, dímelo en lugar de promediar ✋.

**2) Reduce la dimensión del mapa de transferencia, es tu cuello de botella real.** Seis muestras no sostienen transferir 8-10 parámetros de Lorentz por muestra: los acoplamientos F/γ son casi degenerados y el ridge no salva eso. Divide los parámetros en (i) transferibles desde geometría, solo los físicamente dominantes y bien condicionados (típicamente posiciones de resonancia ω_e, ω_m y un par de fuerza/ocupación de modo, p. ej. fuerza ligada a fracción de llenado ~L·W/celda²), y (ii) fijos a la mediana de calibración (γ, ε∞). Justifica la elección de qué es transferible con la estabilidad LOSO, no a priori, y publica esa división en `conclusion.txt`. Si al ampliar el conjunto transferible empeora el LOSO, quédate en la versión pobre: prefiero transferencia modesta y honesta a un ajuste de 6 puntos con 8 coeficientes 😅.

**3) Ponderación del objetivo.** Con ~30 % de puntos con `|r| < 0.05`, la fase de reflexión es prácticamente ruido y va a dominar el RMSE sin información. Pesa los residuales de fase por `min(|r|,|t|)` (o umbral equivalente) y declara el peso en `conclusion.txt`. Además `crossval_rmse` tiene que ser leave-one-sample-out sobre parámetros transferidos desde geometría (lo que ya propones), no refresco libre por muestra: si lo refrescas, la columna deja de medir transferencia y no vale para elegir familia.
