## 1) Inspection report (all values read directly from `data/`)

**Shapes / dtypes** (all `float64`, C-contiguous, no masked/NaN values):
- `data/calibration.npz`: keys `q, qd, qdd, tau`, each `[76, 5]` → **N_cal = 76**, no NaN, no ±Inf, 76/76 unique rows in every array (no duplicates).
- `data/trajectory.npz`: keys `q, qd, qdd`, each `[15, 5]` → 15 test samples, no NaN/Inf, all rows unique.
- `data/task_info.json`: `n_dof = 5`.
  - `a = [0.9071, 0.8133, 0.6854, 1.1468, 0.5746]` (m, if SI)
  - `alpha = [0.0697, -0.7718, 0.0188, 0.5452, -0.2559]` (rad)
  - `d = [0.0, 0.0, 0.3458, 0.0, 0.0759]`
  - `theta_offset = [0.0504, -0.0598, -0.0815, 0.0726, 0.0283]`
  - `mass = [3.4056, 1.3274, 3.2672, 3.4571, 2.4956]`
  - `com`: **every link is `[c_i, 0, 0]`** (com purely along x_i; c = 0.4025, 0.3378, 0.2423, 0.7411, 0.3676)
  - `inertia_diag`: **isotropic per link** (xx=yy=zz): [0.5517, 0.1515, 0.1918, 1.8987, 0.3373]
  - `gravity_base = [0, 0, -9.81]`; `static_pose_index = 0`
  - `tolerances = {"torque_rel": 0.01, "forward_accel_abs": 1e-08}`
- Scales: |q| ≤ 1.05 rad, |qd| ≤ 1.0 rad/s, |qdd| ≤ 2.0 rad/s². τ: joint-rms = [112, 132, 91, 39, 21] N·m; overall τ rms = 89.7. Trajectory row 0 is **exactly q = qd = qdd = 0** → it is the static pose referenced by `static_pose_index=0`, so its true torque is pure gravity (nominal model gives [21.9, 30.4, −56.5, −33.4, −3.5]).

## 2) Data-organization diagnostics
- **Rows are not a time series.** `diff(q)/dt` never matches `qd` for any dt (best rel. error ≫1 for all dt in 1e−3…1); lag-1 autocorrelations of all arrays are ≈0 (|acf| ≤ 0.29). q/qd/qdd look like independent random excitations (kurtosis ≈1.8, amplitude ~1/1/2). ⇒ no sampling period is recoverable, and identification is purely pointwise; **no integration/continuity assumption is valid or needed**.
- **No time/row offsets.** Shifting `tau` by −4…+4 rows: rel-L2 = 0.312 at zero shift vs 0.74–0.80 for every shift. Shifting `qd`/`qdd` independently vs `q` (49 combos): identity best (0.3118).
- **No permutation / dropped-row / corruption trick.** Hungarian+ICP re-matching of τ rows to state rows diverges to 0.75–0.80. RANSAC (400 trials, 20-sample subsets) found only 1 inlier; Huber IRLS leaves median |resid| = 16 N·m — no clean inlier/outlier split, so no corrupted-row subset and no heavy-tail-only story.
- **No friction-relevant lag/order effect.** corr(res[k], pred[k∓1]) ≤ 0.25; augmenting the regressor with a lagged copy of itself gives exactly the reduction expected from 50 extra free parameters (0.312→0.261), i.e. pure overfitting. Acquisition order therefore carries no usable extra information.
- **No joint re-indexing.** Identity joint order is best of all 120 permutations; reversed chain, negated q, permuted τ columns all worse.
- **Nominal parameters are genuinely wrong** (not just noise): nominal-model torque vs measured τ gives rel-L2 **0.776**; projected onto the 30 best-conditioned regressor directions the data-vs-nominal discrepancy reaches **z ≈ 22σ** (σ̂ ≈ 31 N·m), 14 of 30 directions with |z|>3.
- **The big one:** with the *exact* linear-in-inertia-parameter regressor (50 params, verified against an independent COM-frame RNEA to 6e−14), the **in-sample least-squares residual floor is rel-L2 0.312** (rms 28 N·m), rank(Y)=40/50. I tried to beat this floor and could not:
  - 96 kinematic-assembly conventions (all orderings of Rz(θ)/Rx(α)/Tz(d)/Tx(a), α about x or y, standard vs Craig recursion, α→−α, α±π/2, a↔d, a→−a, d→−d, θ_offset on/off, cyclic rolls of the parameter arrays, reversed chain): everything lands in 0.22–0.34 → no convention fits exactly.
  - Extra physics terms (per-joint Coulomb `sign(qd)`, viscous `qd`, constant bias, rotor inertia `qdd`, `q|q|`, `qd|qd|`, `qd²`, `sin/cos q`): best greedy combination 0.312 → 0.264, which is ~what 20 extra free parameters buy by overfitting alone.
  - Free kinematics (nonlinear, concentrated LS): ±2 % → 0.315, ±5 % → 0.304, ±10 % → 0.286, ±25 % → 0.228; free θ-offsets alone 0.291 — no collapse to ≈0.
  - Physically constrained fits (m>0, |com| bounds, inertia bounds): **worse** (0.40–0.58), i.e. no *feasible* rigid-body model fits better than 40 %.
- **Noise-level calibration by simulation.** Generating synthetic data from the same regressor with additive iid noise: σ=30 → in-sample 0.40 / best CV 0.45; σ=10 → 0.146/0.19; σ=3 → 0.044/0.068. The observed in-sample 0.312 with best CV 0.425 sits at **σ ≈ 23–28 N·m (≈26–31 % of τ rms)**.
- **Prediction variance.** Repeated 5-fold CV on calibration: nominal 0.897, plain min-norm LS 0.82, ridge λ=10 **0.425**, ridge-toward-nominal λ=100 0.426, truncated k=15 0.430, generic per-joint ridge model 0.446. Split-half refits change the *test-trajectory* prediction by **16–19 % rel-L2**.

**Consequence I must flag:** under the "large additive noise" interpretation the achievable test-torque error is ~0.15–0.25 rel-L2 (simulation at matched noise gives ~0.20), i.e. at/below the 0.20 zero-credit line. Only a structural discovery (or a strong correct prior) can reach the 0.01 band. I could not find such structure in ~10 structural hypothesis families; I'd like your call on how to spend the remaining effort (see §4).

## 3) Proposed approach for the deliverable
1. **Model:** Newton–Euler RNEA, standard DH `A_i = Rz(q_i+θ0_i)·Tz(d_i)·Tx(a_i)·Rx(α_i)`, revolute joints, fixed base, gravity `gravity_base` — pure numpy, vectorised over samples. Validated already against an independent COM-based implementation (max diff 6e−14) and its linearity in the inertia parameters (2e−14).
2. **Parameterization:** τ is exactly linear in the per-link origin-based set {m_i, h_i = m_i c_i, I_i^O (6)}. I will build the exact regressor `Y ∈ R^{380×50}` by unit-parameter RNEA (no finite differences). **Estimate all identifiable inertia parameters; hold kinematics (a, α, d, θ_offset) at the given values** and **hold gravity fixed** (it is not separately identifiable anyway: the gravity torque is exactly in the span of the {m,h} columns, verified — a free gravity vector changes the LS fit by 0). Redundancy handled explicitly: rank(Y)=40, so 10 combinations are unidentifiable (joint-axis-invariant first-moment/inertia-product combinations, and the inertia components that never enter a revolute-joint torque); I will remove them by rank-revealing SVD/QR on the calibration regressor and parameterise only the identifiable 40-dim base space, with any remaining weak directions damped by regularisation.
3. **Identification:** ridge / truncated-SVD (Tikhonov) in the base space, λ chosen by repeated (3×5) K-fold CV *on the calibration data* predicting held-out measured torque; uniform weighting (matches the relative-L2 metric, which is dominated by proximal joints). Friction/bias columns enter only if CV shows a real gain (currently: no). Predictions can be bagged over resamples/folds to shave the ~17 % split-half variance.
4. **Outputs:** `tau_history.npy` = Y_test·p̂, `[15,5]` float64. Consistency check: build M(q) by RNEA with unit qdd (zero velocity, zero gravity) and β(q,qd) = RNEA(q,qd,0) with gravity; solve `qdd_est = M(q)⁻¹(τ_pred − β)` per sample (numpy `solve`), report `||qdd_est − qdd||_∞` over all 15×5 entries → `verification_data_1.npy`, shape `[1]`. Since τ_pred is exactly the same model's output, this should land at ~1e−12, well inside `forward_accel_abs = 1e−8`. `analysis.py` will use numpy + stdlib only, no CLI args, and will print the diagnostics (CV error, σ̂, rank, residual per joint) for the record.

## 4) Assumptions and open uncertainties
- **Assumed** SI units (rad, rad/s, rad/s², m, kg, kg·m², N·m) — nothing in the files states units.
- **Assumed** standard DH (`a`,`α`,`d`,`θ_offset`) with θ_i = q_i + θ0_i and link i's dynamics attached to frame i; modified/Craig DH was tested and is worse.
- **Assumed** the hidden reference is the *physical* robot's torque (per the task text), **not** the nominal-model torque. This matters a lot: if the reference were the nominal model, simply evaluating the nominal model would score perfectly and identification would be actively harmful. Evidence favours "physical" (nominal is 22σ off the data), but I flag it as the single highest-leverage uncertainty.
- **Assumed** `tau` is joint-side torque, and that any friction/sensor bias is not part of the hidden reference; I currently have no evidence either way because adding friction terms does not improve generalisation.
- **Not assumed:** any time offset, row shift, or ordering hypothesis is needed — I tested and rejected them.
- **Open:** the ~31 % residual floor (σ≈25 N·m). Options I'd like your steer on: (a) proceed with the CV-optimal regularised identification and accept ~0.15–0.25 expected error (likely partial/zero credit); (b) additionally exploit a strong structural prior — the nominal arrays' synthetic structure (com strictly along x_i, isotropic inertia ⇒ only 15 free numbers, positive masses, plausible magnitudes) which reduces variance a lot but fit quality (in-sample 0.36–0.52 so far, optimiser hitting bounds; worth a better global search); (c) spend more effort on a structural hunt for the missing physics (flexible joints / motor-side dynamics / non-DH generator convention), which so far has a poor hit rate; (d) hedge between the physical fit and the nominal model (e.g. blend), which trades expected score between the two hypotheses.

Plan approved — proceed to the main work. Your inspection is thorough and I agree with the core architecture: standard-DH Newton–Euler RNEA, exact linear-in-inertia-parameter regressor built by unit-parameter evaluation, gravity held fixed (correct, and provably redundant since the gravity torque lies in the {m,h} column span), kinematics held at nominal, rank-revealing SVD to remove the null directions, and the verification artifact built from M(q) via unit-qdd RNEA. Two points on your flagged uncertainties, then four refinements to fold in before you write `analysis.py`.

On the two options where you asked for a steer:

- Do NOT hedge/blend with the nominal model (your option (d) is off the table). The brief states the reference is the torque the physical robot requires, and you have shown the nominal parameters are ~22σ from the data. Blending costs real accuracy under the supported hypothesis and only buys a lottery ticket on a hypothesis the project text contradicts. Keep ridge-toward-nominal in the lineup purely as a CV candidate, not as a hedge.
- Spend a bounded but real effort on option (b), the structural prior, and I think your negative result there is likely an artifact of your parameterization rather than evidence against the prior. That is the highest-value remaining item.

Refinements to implement and report:

1) Re-cast the structural prior as a LINEAR subspace restriction, not a nonlinear bounded fit. In the origin-based parameter vector p = {m_i, h_i = m_i c_i, I_i^O (6 unique)}, "com along x_i" is exactly h_{i,y} = h_{i,z} = 0 and "diagonal inertia" is exactly I_{i,xy} = I_{i,xz} = I_{i,yz} = 0; isotropy adds the linear equalities I_{i,xx}=I_{i,yy}=I_{i,zz}. So each structural family is a fixed selection/constraint matrix S and you can solve min ||Y_test-free Sβ − τ|| with plain `numpy.linalg.lstsq` on Y·S — no scipy (which is not permitted anyway), no bounds, no local minima. Please run the same repeated K-fold CV over at least these nested families: full 50; general-com + diagonal-inertia (7/link = 35); com-x + diagonal (5/link = 25); com-x + isotropic (3/link = 15); and each of those with positivity checked post-hoc (report how often m>0 and I satisfies the triangle inequalities, and only impose non-negativity through a simple projected/active-set solve if a candidate violates physics). Report the CV table for all of them side by side with your existing ridge/truncation candidates. If a 15- or 25-parameter restricted model lands at CV comparable to ridge's 0.425, it should be preferred on variance grounds even though its in-sample residual is higher.

2) Characterize the noise before finalizing the estimator. From the unconstrained fit residual, report per-joint residual rms, residual rms relative to each joint's tau rms, and the per-sample (row) residual rms distribution. Your joint torque scales span ~5× (21 to 132 N·m), so if residual rms scales with joint magnitude, the noise is plausibly relative/per-joint and GLS row weighting (w_kj = 1/σ_j, estimated iteratively from residuals) is a genuine efficiency gain rather than decoration; if instead a handful of rows dominate, that resurrects a corrupted-sample story that your RANSAC may have missed because you seeded with 20-sample subsets of a 50-parameter model. Include the weighted variant in the same CV comparison, and state explicitly which weighting won.

3) Make the objective match the score. The hidden reference for the test trajectory is a torque trace, not a noisy measurement, so the quantity to minimize is the model-prediction error induced by parameter error at the 15 test states — not the residual against noisy calibration torques. Please (i) state this explicitly, (ii) re-run your matched-noise simulation reporting the test-state error against the noise-free true torque (not against noisy data) for the winning estimator versus the alternatives, and (iii) quantify your own uncertainty on the deliverable by bootstrap or bagging over calibration resamples: report the spread of the 15×5 `tau_history` prediction across resamples and the median relative-L2 spread, plus the bagged (mean-over-resamples) prediction as your candidate. Bagging the restricted/regularized estimator is essentially free and should reduce the 16–19% split-half spread you observed.

4) Keep the deliverable mechanics exactly as you proposed: `tau_history.npy` as `Y_test·p̂`, `[15,5]` float64; verification by M(q) from unit-qdd RNEA (zero velocity, zero gravity) and β(q,qd) with gravity, `qdd_est = solve(M, τ_pred − β)` per sample, `||qdd_est − qdd||_inf` over all 75 entries written to `verification_data_1.npy` as shape `[1]` float64. Since τ_pred is that same model's output, expect ~1e−12 versus the 1e−8 tolerance; please also confirm `static_pose_index=0` gives a pure-gravity row and report your fit's row-0 torque against the nominal [21.9, 30.4, −56.5, −33.4, −3.5], since that row is a clean, velocity-free gravity-only probe of your estimated {m,h}.

No further structural hunts beyond this: your convention, alignment, permutation, friction and free-kinematics sweeps were reasonably exhaustive and I accept the noise interpretation as the working conclusion. If after steps 1–3 the CV-optimal estimator still predicts the test trajectory with bootstrap spread ≳0.15, deliver it anyway with the diagnostics printed, rather than fabricating extra physics. Write `analysis.py` (numpy + stdlib only, no CLI args, self-contained and runnable from the workspace root) and the two artifacts, and report the CV table, noise diagnostics, bootstrap spread, chosen estimator, and the verification residual.

payload.answer:
## 1) Raw inspection (verified, not inferred)

**`data/task_info.json` conventions**
- `num_poses: 544`, `num_loop_candidates: 55`; pose row = `[x_m, y_m, theta_rad]`.
- `world_frame_anchor`: "pose 0 defines the world-frame anchor; keep outputs in same frame as `poses_initial.npy`" → pose 0 ko fix karna hai, free-float nahi.
- `edge_convention`: "relative measurement from pose i to pose j **in the local frame of i**" → measurement model `Z_ij = T_i^{-1} ⊞ T_j`, i.e. `t_meas = R_i^T (p_j - p_i)`, `dtheta_meas = wrap(θ_j - θ_i)`. Residual = `Z_meas - Z_pred` (wrapped angle).
- No angle-wrapping statement, no inlier-rate/label statement.

**Shapes / dtypes / counts**
- `poses_initial.npy`: `(544, 3)` float64. **N = 544 confirmed.** pose0 = `[0, 0, 0.35]`; x∈[-15.6, 23.9], y∈[-2.0, 29.9], θ∈[-3.05, 2.95] (i.e. angles already wrapped to (-π,π]).
- `odometry_edges.csv`: 543 data rows (544 lines incl. header), CRLF, cols `edge_id,from,to,dx,dy,dtheta,sigma_trans,sigma_rot`; dtypes int64/int64/int64/float64×5. `from = 0..542`, `to = 1..543` (strictly sequential), `edge_id` unique, no NaN, `sigma_trans ≡ 0.0478`, `sigma_rot ≡ 0.0207` (constant).
- `loop_candidates.csv`: 55 data rows, same column layout (`loop_id` instead of `edge_id`), `loop_id = 0..54` unique, no NaN, no duplicate `(from,to)`, all `from<to`, min index gap 68, `sigma_trans ≡ 0.075`, `sigma_rot ≡ 0.03` (constant).
- `|dx|≤0.301 m, |dy|≤0.178 m, |dθ|≤0.064 rad` for **all** loops (mean ‖t‖ = 0.098 m) → every candidate asserts an almost-identity relative pose, i.e. a genuine "same place" revisit.

**Initial poses vs odometry (rough residual stats, no solve)**
- Integrating odometry from `[0,0,0.35]` with the stated convention reproduces `poses_initial.npy` **exactly** (max pos error 0.000 m, max |Δθ| 0.0000 rad). So `poses_initial` is pure dead-reckoning — zero independent information; with θ₀=0 the residual is 6.5 m mean (just the frame offset), which confirms the convention.
- Odometry step length: median 1.034 m, p99 4.9 m, max 18.34 m; 31 edges with |Δθ|>1.0 rad, all **positive** ≈ +1.57 rad, at phases 17/34/51/67 (mod 68) → ~4 right-angle corners per 68-step lap.
- Loop residuals vs `poses_initial` (measured − predicted): median **8.5 m**, p75 12.6 m, p90 17.3 m, max 23.8 m; rotation error median 0.65 rad, max 1.46 rad. So initial path is *globally* badly inconsistent with the loop set (odometry drift), even though it is exactly self-consistent with odometry — the classic "noiseless-but-wrong path" trap in the task statement.

## 2) Explicit outlier signal in the data? — **No**
- No label/truth/inlier column, no confidence or weight field beyond the **constant** per-file sigmas, no duplicate `loop_id`, no NaN/inf, no impossible values, no file-level metadata about inlier rate.
- Only *implicit* signals: (a) the whole loop set is inconsistent with `poses_initial` (drift, not proof of falseness); (b) one candidate (loop_id 1, 104→240) has ‖t‖=0.323 m → Mahalanobis χ²₂ ≈ 18.6 (≈4.3σ) — the single gross-looking candidate. Next worst are 0.20/0.184/0.183/0.179/0.178 m (2.4–2.7σ, i.e. within noise expectations).
- ⇒ **Scoring must be purely geometric/unsupervised.** No supervised calibration data exists; probabilities have to come from an inlier/outlier mixture model, not from labels.

## 3) Discovered structure (drives the design — please sanity-check my reading)
- **The run is 8 traversals of one closed lap of period 68.** Evidence: (i) all 55 loop `(to−from)` are exact multiples of 68 (1,2,3,5 laps); (ii) odometry measurements at the same phase agree across laps at exactly nominal noise level (per-phase across-lap std: dx 0.042, dy 0.043, dθ 0.018 vs σ=0.0478/0.0207) and this disagreement does **not** grow with lap separation (mean|Δ| vs lap0: 0.045→0.055 m flat), ruling out per-lap drift; (iii) span-wise loop means show no trend with number of spans spanned (per-lap drift ≲ 0.02 m / 0.004 rad).
- Under a strictly periodic lap, every loop's predicted measurement is identity, and measured-vs-identity residuals are median 0.085 m, p90 0.178 m, max 0.323 m (nominal Rayleigh mean 0.094 m). ⇒ **false loops, if any, are subtle (≤ ~4σ), not gross.** Expect limited AUC; ranking quality is what we can control.
- **Odometry also contains gross outliers**, at a regular stride: edges 67, 135, 203, 339, 407, 475 (phase 67) have ‖t‖ = 7.7–18.3 m along ±(0.94,−0.36) while edge 271 (same phase) is a normal 1.11 m step; per-phase same-phase comparison flags exactly these 6 (deviation 12.9–21.7 m). These 6 edges alone explain the absurd 18 m "steps" in `poses_initial`. ⇒ robustification is needed for **odometry too**, not only loops. (Note at that phase 6 of 7 measurements are corrupted, so naive per-phase median is unsafe; joint optimization + robust kernel handles it.)
- Pooled-lap closure check: summed per-phase mean rotation = 6.553 rad = 2π + 0.270, and pooled lap position fails to close by ≈ (2.0, −2.2) m. Loops demand closure to ≲0.02 m. The 0.27 rad is ~5× what nominal iid σ_rot predicts for the mean of 8 laps ⇒ nominal sigmas are somewhat optimistic/correlated; plan inflates rotation σ (or uses robust scale) rather than trusting σ_rot literally.
- Loops touch only **60 of 544 poses**, at 8 phases (0,9,…,63, i.e. every 9th pose), in 13 components, all 8 laps touched. So loops give global anchoring every ~9 poses; between them only odometry acts.

## 4) Proposed pipeline (concrete)
**Objective** — sparse pose-graph least squares on SE(2), variables `X ∈ R^{3·544}`, residuals per edge (i,j,Z,Σ):
`e = [ wrap(Δθ_meas − (θ_j−θ_i)) ; R_i^T(p_j−p_i) − t_meas ]`, `Σ = diag(σ_t², σ_t², σ_θ²)`, cost `Σ ρ(||e||_Σ)`; angles always handled through `wrap` (no atan2-free ambiguity), Jacobians analytic, LM/Gauss-Newton with `scipy.sparse` (1632 unknowns, block-banded → ms-scale per iteration).

**Robust losses (different for the two edge families, because their outlier types differ)**
- Odometry: Huber (δ = 2.5√χ²) with mild σ inflation — keeps the graph connected/identifiable while capping the 6 gross phase-67 outliers (we must *not* trust a hard trim here: 6/7 corrupted at one phase but the rest of the lap is clean).
- Loops: Cauchy (or GNC/switchable-constraint) with **annealing** — start with kernel scale γ₀ ≈ 25 m (so the 8–20 m initial residuals still pull the laps together instead of being rejected outright), anneal geometrically γ ← 0.7γ down to ≈ 3σ_meas, re-weighting between outer iterations (IRLS). Rationale: at odometry init *every* loop looks like a 100σ outlier; a fixed-scale robust loss from this start would kill all loops and return exactly the degenerate "noiseless odometry" path the task warns about.
- Loop inlier/outlier posterior via EM (mixture: inlier `N(0, Σ_meas + J Σ_pose Jᵀ)` vs outlier broad/heavy-tailed density with free prior π); E-step = posterior inlier prob, M-step = weighted LM, iterate to convergence. This same posterior is our score.

**Initialisation / seeding (multi-start, pick best by robust objective)**
1. `poses_initial` + GNC anneal (above).
2. Data-driven global init: detect the self-similarity period from the odometry measurement sequence (autocorrelation peaks at 68/136/204 — measured 0.65/0.55), build a per-phase robust consensus motion template, lay 8 traversals on it; then refine with the same robust GN. This init is nearly correct (max loop residual 0.32 m already), so it de-risks the anneal.
3. Choose the solution with the lower robust objective; report both objectives in `metrics.json` as evidence that the chosen optimum is a genuine global robust optimum, not an artifact.

**Scores → `false_probability`** — per loop: `d² = eᵀ Σ_eff^{-1} e` with `Σ_eff = Σ_meas + J_ℓ Σ_pose J_ℓᵀ` (pose covariance from sparse Hessian inverse blocks), computed **leave-one-loop-out** (rank-1 downdate / refit) so an included loop cannot shrink its own residual. Map monotonically: `p_false = 1 / (1 + (1−π)/π · exp(−(d² − d₀²)/2) · Z_ratio)` — the mixture posterior; strictly increasing in d, calibrated by the EM-estimated inlier prior π. Output all 55 rows `loop_id,false_probability` (no thresholding).

**Anchoring / gauge** — hard-fix pose 0 = `poses_initial[0]` (3 pinned DOF, per task_info), so no rank deficiency and no free-floating/gauge-drifting result; the answer is a robust ML estimate that (a) does not reproduce odometry exactly (odometry residuals will be ~1σ, with the 6 gross ones strongly down-weighted) and (b) satisfies the loops.

## 5) Planned diagnostics
- `metrics.json`: N, edge counts; odometry vs loop inlier/outlier counts at 3σ + EM posterior cut at 0.5; robust vs raw cost before/after; RMS/median/p95 of trans & rot residuals per family **before → after**; per-edge robust residual arrays (odometry + loops); per-loop table (residual, Mahalanobis d, LOO d, posterior, weight); EM π trajectory & iteration count; convergence/conditioning info; **independent self-consistency diagnostics** (cross-lap odometry agreement, pooled lap closure error before/after, estimated per-lap drift with CI); the 6 flagged odometry outlier edge_ids; loop score summary (mean/median/max p_false, count > 0.5/0.9, top-5 loop_ids).
- `map_diagnostics.png`: (a) trajectory before (dead-reckoned spiral) vs after (closed repeated lap), same frame, pose-0 marker; (b) loop edges drawn on the optimized map, coloured inlier (p<0.5) / outlier (p≥0.5) / uncertain, thickness ∝ weight; (c) histogram of loop Mahalanobis distances with inlier/outlier mixture fit + π annotation; (d) residual-vs-lap/phase scatter (before/after) + odometry residual histogram with the 6 gross edges marked.

## 6) Assumptions & uncertainties (things I cannot know from the public data)
1. **False-loop generation model & rate** unknown; data suggests offsets ≤ ~4σ (only loop 1 is gross). If false loops are ≤2σ, achievable AUC is intrinsically limited (~0.6–0.75) — no method can do much better.
2. **Evaluator angle convention**: I will output θ wrapped to (−π, π] to match `poses_initial` (note the true cumulative heading is ≈ 8×2π ≈ 50 rad, so wrapped vs unwrapped differ hugely if the grader compares raw).
3. **Trajectory metric details**: anchored RMSE vs GT? per-pose? tolerance/threshold? unknown.
4. Whether exploiting the discovered 8-fold periodicity is considered legitimate modelling or "overfitting the generator" (see Q2 below) — this is the single biggest lever on trajectory accuracy.
5. Whether GT is *exactly* periodic or has sub-cm/lap drift (I can only bound it: ≤0.02 m, ≤0.004 rad per lap).
6. Nominal sigmas may understate correlated rotation error (0.27 rad/lap closure anomaly ≈5σ) — I plan to handle this with mild σ inflation + robust kernels rather than exact-ML.

## Specific questions before I implement
1. **Score grading**: is `false_probability` graded by ranking (AUC/AP) or by calibration (Brier/log-loss)? If calibration matters I must commit to an assumed inlier prior π (I'd take EM's π̂); if AUC-only I'll keep raw monotone posteriors.
2. **Periodicity**: OK to use the data-driven 8-fold self-similarity beyond initialization — i.e. optionally share/couple parameters across repeated traversals as a soft prior — decided by held-out odometry cross-validation (fit both models on 80% of odometry edges, compare held-out residuals)? Option A = textbook robust PGO only (expected ATE maybe 0.2–0.4 m); Option A+ = A plus CV-selected self-similarity coupling (expected ATE maybe 0.1 m, but a structural prior not stated in the task). I recommend **A as the deliverable + A+ evaluated and reported, used only if CV clearly favours it**.
3. Do you have any priors on inlier rate / false-loop offset scale, or on whether "false" means wrong data association vs corrupted values? (Data says all 55 pairs are geometric revisits, so "false" can only mean corrupted values — that changes how aggressively we can down-weight.)
4. Odometry outliers at phase 67: OK to robustify odometry (Huber) and name them in metrics, or do you want odometry treated as trusted and only loops robustified? (Recommendation: robustify — otherwise 6 edges inject up to 18 m of distortion.)
5. Anything you want to see in the figure/metrics that I've missed (e.g., per-loop residual CIs, or a covariance ellipse overlay)?

Approve kar do (ya Q1/Q2 ka answer de do) — phir main `analysis.py` likh ke poses/scores/metrics/plot nikaalunga.

payload.message:
Approach approved. Kaam shuru karo. Aapke 5 sawalon ke answers, aur kuch binding constraints:

**Q1 (scoring)**: Evaluator ka grading rule mujhe bhi pata nahi, isliye dono par safe raho. `false_probability` ko EM posterior hi rakho (calibrated, strictly monotone in d), lekin `metrics.json` me raw per-loop Mahalanobis d aur LOO-d bhi daalo taaki ranking-based grading me koi calibration artifact interfere na kare. Koi hard thresholding ya score clipping mat karo; 55 rows, loop_id 0..54, koi bhi ties mat chhodo (ties na aayein iski guarantee LOO-d se milni chahiye).

**Q2 (periodicity)** — mera final ruling: **Option A (textbook robust PGO) = deliverable**. Periodicity ka use (i) multi-start initialization, aur (ii) diagnostic/cross-check ke liye allowed hai. Soft cross-traversal coupling sirf tab use karo agar held-out odometry CV (80/20 edge split, 3+ folds, pre-registered criterion: mean held-out robust residual clearly better, e.g. >15%) genuinely favour kare — aur us decision ka evidence metrics.json me CV numbers ke roop me likho, aur final map/poses dono models ka comparison report karo. Bina CV evidence ke coupling mat lagana. Agar A+ use karte ho to bhi pose 0 anchor aur measurement model same rahe.

**Q3 (priors on inliers)**: Mere paas koi hidden prior nahi hai — tumhara "false = corrupted values, not wrong pairs" inference data-se justified hai, usi par aage badho. Inlier prior π ko EM se hi estimate karo; agar posterior distribution bimodal nahi hai (yaani koi loop clearly 4.3σ wala loop 1 jaisa gross nahi hai), to scores ko overconfident mat banao — π̂ ke saath honest, spread-out probabilities do. Muqable me agar EM π̂ ~1 ke paas chale jaye to ye bhi metrics me note karo (ye ek scientific finding hai, chhupao mat).

**Q4 (odometry robustification)**: **Haan, odometry ko bhi robustify karo** — task kahata hai "some of the additional measurements may be mutually inconsistent with the full trajectory", aur phase-67 ke 6 edges bina robustification ke 8-18 m distortion daal denge. payload.answer:
## 1) Inspection facts (verified, not assumed)

**data/poses_initial.npy** — shape (544, 3), dtype float64 (confirms N=544). Ranges: x∈[-15.62, 23.91], y∈[-2.03, 29.94], θ∈[-3.05, 2.95]. Pose 0 = [0, 0, 0.35]. **Key fact:** dead-reckoning the odometry measurements from pose 0 reproduces `poses_initial.npy` to ~1e-16 m (residual mean/max = 0.000). So the initial poses are *not* an independent noisy estimate — they are exactly the noiseless-integration ("noiseless path" the brief warns about), and all correction information must come from the loop candidates via joint optimization.

**data/odometry_edges.csv** — 543 data rows. Columns: `edge_id, from, to, dx, dy, dtheta, sigma_trans, sigma_rot`. IDs: edge_id = 0..542 with strictly `from=i, to=i+1` (verified) — a sequential chain, so odometry ordering = time ordering. Sigmas are constant: sigma_trans=0.0478 m, sigma_rot=0.0207 rad. Translation magnitudes mostly ~1.0–1.1 m, but there are genuine long transitions (up to 18.3 m with dtheta≈π/2); since sigma is noise (not step size), these are large *moves*, not necessarily outliers — consistent with a structured survey path with quarter-turn transitions. Path length ≈ 624 m; odometry does not close the loop back to start (final dead-reckoned pose [21.9, 12.8, 0.94]).

**data/loop_candidates.csv** — 55 data rows (matches task_info `num_loop_candidates: 55`). Columns identical: `loop_id (0..54), from, to, dx, dy, dtheta, sigma_trans, sigma_rot`, constant sigmas 0.075 m / 0.03 rad. All 55 pairs unique; index gap (to−from) ∈ [68, 340]. **Every measured translation is tiny: |t| ≤ 0.32 m** — each candidate asserts "pose_from ≈ pose_to" (co-location). In the initial odometry frame the from/to world distances are 0.74…23.8 m only 1 loop is <1 m apart; 21 are >10 m apart. Raw loop-vs-initial residual norms span 0.32–4.17 m as a continuum (drift confounds them) — so false loops must be identified by *joint-consensus*, not per-loop thresholding on the initial poses.

**Measurement convention (from task_info.json):** "relative measurement from pose i to pose j in the local frame of i" → z_ij = T_i⁻¹·T_j, i.e. predicted [dx,dy] = R(θ_i)ᵀ(p_j−p_i), dθ = wrap(θ_j−θ_i); this convention is confirmed by the exact dead-reckoning reproduction. It is a body-frame (not world-difference) convention; no inverse. Angle wrap to (−π, π] (standard; not explicitly stated). Sigmas given per-row; natural information weights Ω = diag(σ_t⁻², σ_t⁻², σ_θ⁻²). World frame: "pose 0 defines the world-frame anchor; keep outputs in the same frame as poses_initial.npy".

## 2) Proposed approach

- **Formulation:** Sparse Gauss–Newton / Levenberg–Marquardt least squares over all 544 SE(2) poses (1632 DOF), residuals r_ij = wrap(z_ij − T_i⁻¹T_j) with the body-frame convention and angle wrapping, weighted by the given per-row sigmas. Built with scipy.sparse (block 3×3 Jacobians), Cholesky/LSMR solves; init from poses_initial (with small perturbation awareness that odometry-chain-only LS is exactly the initial path).
- **Robust loop rejection:** treat all 55 loops with a robust loss (Cauchy/Huber IRLS) plus hard χ² gating in an iterative trim-and-re-fit loop: solve → compute per-loop Mahalanobis distance D² = rᵀΩr (3 DOF) → downweight/prune loops exceeding a gate (D² > ~12–16), re-solve until the inlier set is stable (graduated-non-convexity style annealing on the gate to avoid good-loops-first bias). Odometry kept Gaussian (it is the only structural information), but I'll report its final residuals as a sanity check.
- **Scores:** for each loop, D² at the *final* solution; convert via a 2-component mixture posterior: inlier D²~χ²₃ vs outlier diffuse density → false_probability = P(false | D²) ∈ [0,1]. Monotone, calibrated-ish, and I'll also record the raw D² and inlier flags in metrics.json. Expect the scores to separate strongly once drift is corrected by consensus loops.
- **Gauge:** the global SE(2) frame is unobservable; per task_info, pose 0 defines the anchor → I'll **fix pose 0 = poses_initial[0]** (hard clamp / tiny-sigma prior). This is the *specified* gauge, not an arbitrary one, and outputs stay in the poses_initial frame. The estimate is a genuine robust LS solution (loops pull the trajectory off the dead-reckoned path), not the noiseless path itself.
- **Outputs:** `analysis.py` (full pipeline), `poses.npy` [544,3], `loop_closure_scores.csv` (loop_id,false_probability), `metrics.json` (odom/loop chi², inlier/outlier counts + loop_ids, residual stats before/after, trajectory adjustment RMS vs initial, solver iterations/convergence), `map_diagnostics.png` (initial odometry path vs optimized path, accepted loops as green chords, rejected as red chords, residual/D² inset panels).

## 3) Assumptions & uncertainties

**Assumptions (evidence-backed where noted):**
1. z = T_i⁻¹T_j body-frame, wrap to (−π,π] — convention verified; wrap rule itself is standard, not stated in task_info.
2. Odometry edges are 543 sequential i→i+1 edges, Gaussian with the listed sigmas; large π/2 transitions are real motion, not outliers (no evidence of odometry corruption; brief only suspects the loop candidates).
3. **No ground-truth loop labels exist anywhere** (only the 4 listed input files exist; confirmed by listing data/) — consistent with your expectation. Labels must be inferred; the split is only verifiable via residual separation.
4. Pose-0 anchor from task_info is the intended gauge; hidden scoring (if any) is assumed to be in this same frame.
5. Info weights = inverse given sigmas; no extra weighting stated.

**Uncertainties:**
- Number of false loops unknown; initial-pose loop residuals are a continuum (0.3–4.2 m) because odometry drift (order 1 m+ by random-walk over 543 edges, amplified by rotation errors/lever arms) contaminates them. Confidence that the *final* residuals separate — but the gate threshold choice will affect borderline loops and their scores.
- Exact score calibration is a modeling choice (χ²₃-mixture posterior chosen; any monotone map would rank identically).
- Whether a soft vs hard pose-0 anchor matters slightly for the first few poses; proposing hard clamp per task_info wording.

If this looks right, I'll implement `analysis.py` with the robust GN pipeline + trim loop, then report the accepted/rejected split and diagnostics.

2) Отсев петель. Твоя тревога про «good-loops-first bias» реальна, так что anneal шлюз правильно: начни с очень мягкого Cauchy/Huber и очень широкого gating-порога, сужай постепенно. Жёсткий prune по D² сразу на initial-позах запрещён — ты сам показал, что там непрерывный диапазон 0.3–4.2 м из-за дрейфа, там любой порог произволен. Зафиксируй правило остановки (стабильный набор инлаеров, или max_iter, или изменение D² < eps) и сохрани историю: сколько итераций, как менялся размер инлаер-множества. Это твой главный защитный артефакт.

3) Одометрия. Держишь гауссовой — правильно, сомнительны только петли, и их подозревает сам бриф. Но тогда в metrics.json обязательны финальные одометрические резидуалы (mean/max/chi2 на DOF). Если у тебя после подтяжки петель одометрические невязки улетят сильно за 3σ — это красный флаг, что мы пережали петли, и тогда это надо показать, а не спрятать.

4) Оценки петель. D² бери строго с ФИНАЛЬНОГО решения, не со среднего. Отдельно настаиваю: сохрани в metrics.json и сырой D² по каждой петле, и bинарный флаг инлаер/аутлаер, и гистограмму D². Смешанная апостериорка — это твоя модельная калибровка; нам важно, чтобы ранжирование было видно сырьём. Если разделения на «почти 0 / почти 1» нет, так и напиши прямо в метриках и в своём отчёте, не рисуй уверенности где её нет.

5) Реалистичный шум. Проверь, что 543 ребра × σ_trans 0.0478 дают ожидаемый случайный дрейб порядка σ·√543 ≈ 1.1 м плюс вращательный рычаг — сравни с тем, насколько финальное решение ушло от initial. Если твои поправки на порядок больше правдоподобного дрейфа, значит петли-выбросы затянули граф, и это надо диагностировать, а не принимать.

6) Артефакты. Сделай картинку читаемой при печати — без тонких линий и без смысла, переданного только цветом.

Specifically, please report:
1. Input shapes and dtypes: `data/poses_initial.npy` (confirm N and whether it equals the required 544 output rows), row counts and exact column names/headers of `data/odometry_edges.csv` and `data/loop_candidates.csv`, and the full contents of `data/task_info.json` (especially pose/angle conventions, edge representation, and the output spec).
2. Measurement conventions: how relative poses are parameterized (body-frame vs world-frame composition, angle wrapping convention), and how `loop_id` is defined/uniquified.
3. A proposed approach outline for the two coupled deliverables:
   a. A robust trajectory estimate over the full measurement graph (sequential odometry + candidate loop closures), e.g. sparse pose-graph adjustment with a robust loss (Huber/soft-L1 or IRLS) rather than unweighted least squares, plus initialization strategy from `poses_initial.npy`.
   b. A per-loop-candidate falsification score mapped into a `false_probability` in [0,1], e.g. robust residuals / measurement consistency after joint fitting, with an explicit calibration rule.
   c. Contents you intend to put in `metrics.json` and what `map_diagnostics.png` will show (before/after trajectory, loop closure inliers vs outliers, residual histograms).
4. Consequential assumptions and uncertainties you want me to weigh in on, for example: whether to keep the trajectory anchored (gauge fixing) since the graph is unobservable in global frame; how to avoid outlier loop closures dominating the initial fit (robust initialization / RANSAC-style gating vs pure robust kernel); expected outlier fraction in `loop_candidates.csv`; and whether sequential odometry edges should be treated as trusted or also down-weighted.

Also flag any data-quality observations (duplicate/conflicting edges, non-contiguous indices, NaNs, unusually large odometry steps) that could affect the formulation. Keep it concise and structured; hold off on implementing the pipeline until we agree on the approach.

READ-ONLY INSPECTION COMPLETE — data report + proposed approach. No deliverables written yet (exploratory diagnostics only, in /workspace/.scratch/). One finding is consequential and needs your call before I implement.

=====================================================
1. INPUTS (verified)
=====================================================
data/poses_initial.npy: float64, shape (544, 3) — N=544 = required output rows ✓. theta already in [-pi,pi] (min -3.055, max 2.948), no NaNs. Pose0 = [0,0,0.35] (world anchor has non-zero heading).

data/odometry_edges.csv: 543 rows (= N-1, a single contiguous chain), columns exactly:
  edge_id,from,to,dx,dy,dtheta,sigma_trans,sigma_rot  (int64 / float64)
  edge_id 0..542 contiguous; from=k, to=k+1 for every row; no dups, no NaNs; sigmas constant 0.0478 m / 0.0207 rad.

data/loop_candidates.csv: 55 rows, columns:
  loop_id,from,to,dx,dy,dtheta,sigma_trans,sigma_rot
  loop_id 0..54 contiguous; 55 unique (from,to) pairs; all from<to; 21 repeated `from`, 17 repeated `to`; no NaNs; sigmas constant 0.075 m / 0.030 rad. Index gaps are ONLY 68/136/204/340 (all multiples of 68).

data/task_info.json (full): num_poses 544; num_loop_candidates 55; pose_convention "pose row is [x_m,y_m,theta_rad]"; world_frame_anchor "pose 0 defines the world-frame anchor; keep outputs in the same frame as poses_initial.npy"; edge_convention "relative measurement from pose i to pose j in the local frame of i"; outputs = poses.npy [544,3], loop_closure_scores.csv (loop_id,false_probability in [0,1]), metrics.json, map_diagnostics.png.

2. MEASUREMENT CONVENTIONS (verified numerically, not just read)
- Body-frame composition z_ij = T_i^{-1} ⊗ T_j: r = R(-theta_i)(p_j-p_i) - [dx,dy]; r_theta = wrap(theta_j-theta_i-dtheta).
- CONFIRMED: with this convention all 543 odometry residuals against poses_initial are EXACTLY 0.0 (max 0.0e0). So (a) the convention/axis order is right, and (b) poses_initial is literally the dead-reckoned integral of the odometry file — it is NOT an independent estimate and it inherits every odometry error.
- Wrapping: I use (a+pi) mod 2pi - pi everywhere (residuals + outputs).
- loop_id is just a contiguous 0..54 index; uniqueness lives in (from,to), which is unique. Scores must be emitted for all 55 loop_ids.

=====================================================
3. DATA-QUALITY OBSERVATIONS (these drive the formulation)
=====================================================
a) Trajectory structure: closed quadrilateral ~19x19 m traversed 8 times; period is exactly 68 poses (corners = +1.57 rad every ~17 steps). Loop gaps are multiples of 68 → every candidate connects geometrically coincident poses ("revisits").
b) 6 GROSS ODOMETRY OUTLIERS: edges 67,135,203,339,407,475 have translations of 7.7/9.7/7.6/9.7/16.3/18.3 m while every other step is 0.89–1.44 m (median 1.03). All sit at the 68-periodic corners, all have normal dtheta≈+1.57, and their offsets point along a near-constant world direction with alternating sign → classic injected translation corruption (gross-error rate 1.1%). poses_initial therefore contains 6 physical "teleports" plus ~20 m accumulated drift (loop residuals vs poses_initial: median 8.5 m, max 23.8 m).
c) Loop measurements are ALL small: |t| median 0.085 m (max 0.323 m = 4.3 sigma), |dtheta| max 0.064 rad; the magnitude distribution matches a single Rayleigh(0.075) very well (median 0.085 vs 0.088 predicted; p95 0.183 vs 0.184). I.e. no large fabricated measurements.
d) No duplicate/conflicting edges, no non-contiguous indices, no NaNs, no suspicious odometry rotations otherwise.

=====================================================
4. THE CONSEQUENTIAL FINDING (please weigh in)
=====================================================
Two competing explanations for the inconsistency, both locally optimal:
